layers, the per-layer answers, what would decide it and the fallbacks
used: `abrupt_textural_change_fao88()`, `andic_properties_fao88()`,
`calcareous_fao88()`, `calcaric_fao88()`,
`continuous_hard_rock_fao88()`, `ferralic_properties_fao88()`,
`ferric_properties_fao88()`, `fluvic_properties_fao88()`,
`geric_properties_fao88()`, `gleyic_properties_fao88()`,
`stagnic_properties_fao88()`, `gypsiferous_fao88()`,
`interfingering_fao88()`, `nitic_properties_fao88()`,
`organic_soil_materials_fao88()`, `permafrost_fao88()`,
`plinthite_fao88()`, `salic_properties_fao88()`, `slickensides_fao88()`,
`smeary_fao88()`, `sodic_properties_fao88()`,
`soft_powdery_lime_fao88()`, `strongly_humic_fao88()`,
`sulfidic_materials_fao88()`, `tonguing_fao88()` (albic or Chernozem
tongues), `vertic_properties_fao88()` and
`weatherable_minerals_fao88()`. A property with no depth in the key is
read in the layers starting within 125 cm (p. 42); `max_top_cm` reads
“within X cm” and `window_cm` “throughout X-Y cm”, as the key will ask.
Nothing is registered or classified yet.

The numbers are the printed ones. The abrupt textural change doubles the
clay below 20 % or adds 20 points from 20 %, over an abrupt or clear
boundary. The andic properties read their three items, with the volcanic
glass sliding from 30 % at 0.4 % Alox + 1/2 Feox to 5 % at 2.0 %.
Calcareous is more than 2 % CaCO3 or strong effervescence, calcaric
calcareous throughout 20-50 cm. The ferralic properties ask a CEC below
24 cmol(+)/kg clay or 4 per kg soil in the cambic B or right below the
A; the geric properties 1.5 cmol(+)/kg clay of bases and KCl acidity, or
a delta pH of +0.1. The salic properties ask an ECe above 15 dS/m within
30 cm, or above 4 at a pH (1:1) above 8.5; the sodic properties 15 %
sodium or 50 % sodium and magnesium; the sulfidic materials 0.75 %
sulfur with less than three times as much CaCO3 and a pH above 3.5;
strongly humic more than 1.4 % organic carbon over 100 cm. The fluvic
properties read organic carbon above 0.20 % to 125 cm or irregular with
depth, or stratification in a quarter of the soil, on sediments where
their origin is recorded. Gleyic properties are two of three signs
(reduction, groundwater whose capillary fringe reaches the surface, gley
colours in more than 95 % of the matrix); stagnic properties are
reduction with the mottling pattern within 50 cm. The ferric properties,
soft powdery lime, tonguing, interfingering, nitic and vertic
properties, permafrost, plinthite, slickensides and smeary consistence
read the field record; what an unrecorded observation means for each
(absent or undecided) is listed below and in the readings.

Hugo’s decisions of 2026-11-08 are applied: the colour pattern stands in
for a reduction test that is not recorded, flagged, and the chroma
increasing with depth supports the stagnic properties without being
required (Q21); “many” coarse mottles are 15 % and more than 20 mm
(Q22); and the defaults on the abrupt textural change, fluvic, nitic and
vertic properties. The andic properties of p. 34 move to this file, and
item 7 of the ferralic B reads them as before (absent, flagged, unless
volcanic material is recorded). They also decide now whether a mantle of
35 to 50 cm buries the horizons below it (p. 42), which was left
undecided in 0.9.382.

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-09). A boundary over less than 5
cm is one recorded abrupt or clear (abrupta, clara), read by one shared
reader for the abrupt textural change and item 6 of the argic B; not
recorded, it is absent, flagged, in both, and an argic B that fails on
it keeps the flag. The abrupt textural change also compares a layer
starting less than 5 cm below the upper one, across a thin transitional
layer. Without CaCO3, strong effervescence makes a layer calcareous and
a water pH below 6.5 makes it not calcareous, flagged (both recorded:
undecided, flagged); anything else leaves it undecided. An increase of
organic carbon of more than 0.2 points is an irregular decrease for the
fluvic properties. The three reduction tests are read as an OR, a
negative one alone does not refute, and the gley colour confirms
reduction but never refutes it, never in an E. Below a buried horizon
only the properties bound to a horizon (ferralic, ferric, nitic,
tonguing, interfingering) are removed. The frozen suffix f and the
plinthite suffix v are read only in the notation that writes them (z for
frozen in the Canadian one); elsewhere they leave the test undecided.
Fe-Mn nodules alone, carbonate coatings named without an amount, a
sulfur lower bound against CaCO3 and Chernozem tongues without a width
are undecided; skeletans not recorded are absent; any recorded
slickensides that are not none count. A petrocalcic pan is never
continuous hard rock, strongly humic passes when the carbon described
already exceeds the 100 cm mean, the Podzol ignition route shows stagnic
as well as gleyic properties, and the oxalate iron of the nitic
properties is compared as Fe (0.2 % Fe2O3 = 0.14 % Fe). The readings are
in `data-raw/fao_readings.yaml`. Every classification is unchanged (the
fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

## soilKey 0.9.382 (2026-11-09)

### FAO-Unesco legend: the diagnostic horizons of 1988

Second part of the FAO-Unesco soil legend (the Revised Legend of 1988,
read in the ISRIC reprint of 1997). A new file,
`R/diagnostics-fao88-horizons.R`, reads the 16 diagnostic horizons of
chapter IV (pp. 25-33) as internal predicates, each returning a
`DiagnosticResult` that passes, fails or stays undecided, with the
layers, what would decide it, the fallbacks used and any stand-in:
`histic_h_fao88()` (with `base = "eutric"` or `"dystric"`),
`mollic_a_fao88()`, `fimic_a_fao88()`, `umbric_a_fao88()`,
`ochric_a_fao88()`, `argic_b_fao88()`, `natric_b_fao88()`,
`cambic_b_fao88()`, `spodic_b_fao88()`, `ferralic_b_fao88()`,
`calcic_fao88()`, `petrocalcic_fao88()`, `gypsic_fao88()`,
`petrogypsic_fao88()`, `sulfuric_fao88()` and `albic_e_fao88()`. They
build on the readers of 0.9.381: depths from the soil surface, H and O
included; horizons buried under 50 cm of new material are not
diagnostic; the subsurface horizons have their upper limit within 125 cm
(p. 42, argument `max_top_cm`). Nothing is registered or classified yet.

The numbers are the printed ones. The histic H is more than 20 cm of
organic soil material within 40 cm, or a thin surface layer or a plough
layer that, mixed to 25 cm, has at least 8 + 8 x clay / 60 % organic
carbon. The mollic and umbric A mix their upper 18 cm and ask a moist
chroma and value below 3.5, a dry value below 5.5, a value one unit
darker than the C (waived when strongly humic), 0.6 % organic carbon
(2.5 % with more than 40 % lime), a base saturation of 50 % or more (the
umbric A less), and a thickness of 10 cm on rock or a cemented pan, else
18 cm and a third of a solum under 75 cm, or more than 25 cm. The argic
B asks sandy loam or finer with 8 % clay, the increase of 3 points, a
ratio of 1.2 or 8 points (breaks at 15 and 40 %) within 30 cm with clay
skins and 15 cm without, one tenth of the overlying horizons and 7.5 cm
(lamellae 15 cm), and without clay skins a coarser horizon of 18 cm
above it (5 cm over an abrupt transition); it is not ferralic and not
natric. The natric B adds columnar or prismatic structure and more than
15 % exchangeable sodium in its upper 40 cm. The ferralic B asks a CEC
of 16 or an ECEC of 12 cmol(+)/kg clay or less, 30 cm, under 10 %
weatherable minerals and water-dispersible clay, a silt/clay ratio of
0.2 or less, no andic properties and under 5 % rock structure. The
spodic B reads the pyrophosphate chemistry of Soil Taxonomy 1975 with
its index of accumulation of 65. The calcic, gypsic and sulfuric
horizons ask 15 cm; the petrocalcic and petrogypsic horizons have no
minimum thickness.

Hugo’s decisions of 2026-11-08 are applied: a recorded Bt designation
counts as the clay-skin observation, flagged, and “few” clay films are 1
% (Q13); the citric P2O5 of the mollic and umbric A decides when
measured, else the anthropic layers it targets do, absent if not
recorded (Q14); the eutric and dystric histic H by pH (1:5) 5.5, and
organic soil materials undecided between the saturated limit and 20 %
unless the drainage is recorded (Q15); the ferralic B asks 8 % clay and
reads the 20-200 um weatherable minerals, flagged (Q16); without the
1975 spodic chemistry, `spodic_horizon_usda()` and then the WRB
[`spodic()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/spodic.md)
stand in, flagged (Q17); the sulfuric horizon does not ask for jarosite
(Q18). soilKey’s own readings of this part (among them: the mixing of
the mollic A, the layers that can hold a B, carbonate and gypsum read as
absent from the pH, the HCl reaction or the ECe when not measured,
volcanic glass read as none unless volcanic material is recorded, and
the albic E read on its moist colour when no dry colour is recorded) are
in `data-raw/fao_readings.yaml` for his word. Every classification is
unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-09). soilKey’s readings of this
part are accepted, with these changes. The spodic B is ruled out without
its chemistry only by free carbonate or a water pH of 7 or more; a
designation without h or s no longer rules it out, the older suffix ir
counts as an illuvial sign, and the stand-ins now decide only the
chemistry and are recorded only when they decide. An albic E without a
dry colour takes the moist value + 1 as its dry value, flagged; an
undesignated layer is read as albic only below a surface layer and above
a B or C. Andic properties left undecided are absent, flagged, unless
volcanic material is recorded. The thickness of the mollic A and its
solum are both measured from the mineral surface. Moderately well
drained leaves the saturation of organic materials undecided. The review
also fixed these defects: an A layer straddling 18 cm is now read on its
own values; the lime waiver of the mollic A is an alternative to the
printed colour, with 2.5 % organic carbon on its branch only, and
undecided when CaCO3 is not known; a plough layer may be an Hp or Op;
lamellae count only when recorded above 0; argic item 6 is undecided
when a clay on the way up is missing; an A no more than a third of an
open solum fails; “closer to 2 than to 3” is a chroma below 2.5; the
petrocalcic and petrogypsic horizons read their cementing agent (km, ym)
from the designation; and the Bt of an E&Bt counts as a clay-skin
observation.

## soilKey 0.9.381 (2026-11-08)

### FAO-Unesco legend: the attributes and the shared readers

First part of the FAO-Unesco soil legend in its two editions, the
Revised Legend of 1988 (World Soil Resources Report 60, read in the
ISRIC reprint of 1997) and the Legend of 1974 (Soil Map of the World,
Vol. I). Both will be one module with an edition switch, registered as
two systems in a later part; nothing is registered or classified yet.

New horizon attributes, from the plan’s list as Hugo decided (Q19,
2026-11-08): `p2o5_citric_mg_kg`, `extractable_acidity_ph82_cmol`,
`cec_ph82_cmol`, `al_dcb_pct`, `exch_acidity_kcl_cmol`, `ph_h2o_1to1`,
`ph_h2o_1to5`, `rock_structure_pct`, `smeary_consistence`,
`bleached_ped_coatings`, `ignition_redder`, `spodic_pellets`,
`skeletans_pct`, `skeletan_thickness_mm`,
`carbonate_coatings_faces_pct`, `nodule_size_max_cm`,
`dta_low_endotherm`, the rubbed moist colour (`munsell_hue_rubbed`,
`munsell_value_rubbed`, `munsell_chroma_rubbed`), `pitted_quartz_pct`,
`palygorskite_pct` and `aeolian_crack_infill`. New site attributes:
`flooding_days_growing_period`, `rudic_recorded` and `reference_fao74`.
Each names the criterion it serves, with its page, and its fallback when
not recorded. `inst/ATTRIBUTES.md` and `inst/schemas/pedon-schema.json`
are regenerated.

A new file, `R/fao-readers.R`, holds the internal readers the
diagnostics of both editions will share, all three-valued, each saying
what it read, what would decide it and the fallbacks it used: depths
from the literal soil surface, H and O horizons included (Q9); windows
read “throughout” or “in some part”, and “within X cm” by the top of the
feature; thickness-weighted means and the mixed surface, with the depth
below a shallow soil counted as zero where the strongly humic test of
1988 says so; organic matter as organic carbon x 1.724, flagged (Q11);
pH at 1:1 and 1:5, the CEC per kg clay by NH4OAc or NH4Cl, the effective
CEC of each edition and the base saturation, each flagged where the
method differs (Q12); the three texture classes of the map symbol in
each edition, the class of the upper 30 cm and the 1974 depth of 125, 90
or 75 cm by that class (Q10), sandy loam or finer and the texture groups
of tonguing; the solum, buried horizons under 50 cm of new material (35
cm over an andic mantle in 1988); the clay increase in three bands with
its numbers as arguments, equal to the USDA branch of
`test_clay_increase_argic()` on a grid of clay contents, within a
vertical distance and undecided across a lithological discontinuity; the
hue rank and hue comparisons; the rubbed colour, the moist colour
standing in, flagged (Q24); and the fallbacks of smeary consistence, the
ignition test, rock structure and palygorskite.

The numbers of both editions, with their pages, are in
`data-raw/fao_thresholds_1988.yaml` and
`data-raw/fao_thresholds_1974.yaml`, and the readings in
`data-raw/fao_readings.yaml` (Hugo’s decisions of 2026-11-08 and
2026-11-09, his word on every reading of this part); the later parts
move them to the rule folders. No text of the books is shipped. Every
classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems
byte-identical). \# soilKey 0.9.380 (2026-11-08)

### Germany KA5: FAO horizon designations read on the data route

Ninth part of the German soil systematics of the KA5 (Bodenkundliche
Kartieranleitung, 5th ed., 2005; system id `ka5`). A profile that
declares the FAO notation in `site$designation_system` (as
[`isis_profile_to_pedon()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/isis_profile_to_pedon.md)
does) was read on the data alone: its FAO letters were thrown away, so
an E was often read as an Ah, a Bt or a Bw as a loose C, and the class
tests of the Ah/C-Böden and the Braunerden stayed undecided. A new file,
`R/ka5-fao.R`, keeps the letters where an FAO letter and a KA5 symbol
mean the same (the KA5 prints no correlation of horizon symbols; the
pairs are read from the two definitions, KA5 pp. 92-105 and WRB 2022
Annex 3, pp. 225-228). Each FAO designation bounds the KA5 horizons its
row may be: an E is an eluvial A (Al, Ael, Ae, Ahe), an A an A that is
not eluvial, a Bt a horizon with a Bt part, a Bw one with a Bv part, a
Bs or Bh one with a Bs or Bh part, a plain B a B, P or T, a C a C, an R
a solid rock (mC), an O an L, Of or Oh; the redox letters open the S and
G horizons (g both, by the water regime the KA5 asks; l and r the G).
Where a field descriptor is not recorded, a letter states what its
definition names: t the clay coatings of the Bt, w the browning of the
Bv, p the tillage of the Ap, k the secondary carbonate, g and l redox
mottling present with its share open. Measured data come first and
decide against a letter: recorded clay films, the clay difference,
Munsell colours.

Within the family the order of tests decides three-valued. When the data
leave one horizon undecided, it is the letter’s own translation (Bt for
Bt, Bv for Bw) and the open question is one the letter answers, the FAO
designation reads it, as a KA5 designation would be read; such a row has
a lower grade of evidence, listed in `provisional_because` as
`horizons:<code>`. The letter does not answer whether water is
groundwater or perched water (Q13), the organic band of Q10 (H or Aa),
or the origin of carbonate measured in a B: those rows stay undecided. A
finer horizon the letter does not name (an Axp for an FAO Ap) stays
undecided beside it. The letter and the data are in conflict, and the
row undecided with a note, when no horizon of the family holds on the
measured data (an FAO Bt with few clay films, an FAO E not lighter than
its Bt), or when a horizon outside the family holds on the measured data
first (an FAO C browner than the C below, an FAO Bw with the coatings
and clay of a Bt, an FAO Bt with a measured Sd or Go, an FAO A over a
measured Ah-Bv); the redox translations the data rule out are dropped
from the candidates. Numbered sub-horizons with the same defining letter
are one horizon (Bt1/Btg2, Bw1/Bwg2): each Bt sub-horizon must show the
clay enrichment on its own clay against the eluvial horizon above, a Bw1
is compared with the horizon under the Bw, an E looks for its Bt under
its sub-horizons and an EB. The A1, A2 and B3 of the 1977 numbering get
no FAO reading. Rows with no designation, profiles that do not declare
the FAO notation and profiles in the KA5 notation are read as before.
Hugo confirmed the readings (`readings.yaml`); the reading of the 1977
numbering is soilKey’s, for him to confirm.

On the ISIS profiles from Germany (`inst/benchmarks/ka5_isis.R`, which
now also counts a level as provisional when a horizon rests on a lower
grade of evidence): class 2 of 16 (12.5 %, 3.5-36.0) becomes 4 of 16
(25.0 %, 10.2-49.5) and type 1 of 15 (6.7 %, 1.2-29.8) becomes 3 of 15
(20.0 %, 7.0-45.2); one class and one type are firm, the rest
provisional. Profiles that stop at the division fall from 13 to 9 of the
16 labelled; DE007 (Parabraunerde) and DE011 (Braunerde) now key to
their type. DE002 (a Pseudogley in its label) keys as a
Normparabraunerde, its S class now closed by the measured rust; DE009
(Rosterde) as a Normbraunerde. The nine that still stop do so on what
the data do not say: groundwater or perched water (DE003, DE006, DE019),
bioturbation for an Axh (DE013, DE014, Q17), the origin of the carbonate
measured in the Bt (DE015, DE016), a clay difference under the Bt
minimum (DE012), the Bg of DE008. One expectation of
`test-v09361-ka5-data-key.R` changes: an FAO Ap in a profile declared
fao2006 is now read Ap, not Ah. Every other KA5 test and every
classification of the other systems is unchanged (byte-identical).

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09). soilKey’s
readings of this part are accepted, with these choices: rock is an R
designation, or 90 % bedrock or more with a hard rupture resistance
recorded (bedrock alone is not rock); free iron below 0.5 % reads as not
turning redder on ignition, 0.5 % or more leaves the test undecided; the
texture of the upper 30 cm under an organic surface starts at the first
mineral horizon, flagged; the strongly humic mean of a soil shallower
than 50 cm over rock is divided by 100 cm, flagged; and a horizon
without a designation between the last A, E or B and the first C leaves
the solum undecided. A window is read only where the depths fill it: a
gap or a layer without depths leaves it undecided, overlapping layers
are flagged, and “within X cm” fails only when the description goes
below X or reaches rock at X. A vector answer with an undecided element
now names what would decide it, buried horizons are read after a figure
(Bt2b), a rock layer has full rock structure, and a base saturation
computed over another CEC method carries both flags.

## soilKey 0.9.379 (2026-11-08)

### Germany KA5: older German names and an offline benchmark on the ISIS profiles from Germany

Eighth part of the German soil systematics of the KA5 (Bodenkundliche
Kartieranleitung, 5th ed., 2005; system id `ka5`). A new file,
`inst/rules/ka5/legacy_names.yaml`, maps older German soil names to KA5
codes, for benchmarks only: the second names of the DBG systematics of
1998 (Schwarzerde, Kalkschwarzerde, Braunauenboden, Auenregosol,
Tiefumbruchboden and others), Haftnässepseudogley (the KA5’s own word
for the Haftpseudogley, p. 313), the older names the KA5 prints beside
its own (Rosterde, Borowina, Latosole, the Marschen subtypes such as
Typische Kalkmarsch), and Chernozem. Every row names its source and page
and resolves to a class, type or subtype of the key. A name the KA5
prints under two types (Typische Seemarsch, Übergangsbrackmarsch) is
read at the class M; Amphigley, printed for two classes (pp. 229, 245),
is excluded. Three leading modifiers are read: Acker- (the variety v,
p. 267), Typischer (the Norm subtype of a type name, pp. 191, 238,
250-253; the KA5’s own exceptions, Typische Kleimarsch and Typische
Flussmarsch, are rows of their own) and Primärer (dropped before a
Pseudogley only). A name of exactly two type names joined by a hyphen is
read with the older names put in; one the key does not print is the type
of its last part (p. 191).

A new internal matcher, `.ka5_match_label()`, reads a label against the
names of the key (21 classes, 54 types with a name, 223 subtypes;
soilKey’s bracketed codes left out) and the legacy file: exact names
only, with case, umlaut spelling, the sharp s and the spacing around a
hyphen alike. A name with brackets (but the modifier “(Acker)”), a
slash, a comma, a full stop or a digit, two names joined by a space and
names of three or more parts are not read. There is no generic tolerance
of misspellings; a name not read is NA, never a guess. In a label of
several parts the deepest part wins when the others are its ancestors,
else their common ancestor. A new script, `inst/benchmarks/ka5_isis.R`,
keys the 24 ISIS profiles from Germany with
[`classify_ka5()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_ka5.md)
and scores them at the class, the type and, where both sides give one,
the subtype, with Wilson 95 % intervals. It downloads nothing: it reads
the saved ISIS profiles from its first argument, `SOILKEY_ISIS_CACHE` or
`tools::R_user_dir("soilKey", "cache")/isis/profiles.rds`, and stops if
there is none. Its explicit variant list reads two names of the labels
with no printed source, flagged: a soil like a Schwarzerde as the class
T only (DE008), and a Braunerde of low base content as the type BB with
the variety dy noted (DE011). ISIS data are not shipped.

First run (soilKey 0.9.379): all 16 local names are read (one at class
level, nine at type level, six at subtype level); 8 profiles have no
local name and 6 have no horizons. Class 2 of 16 (12.5 %, 3.5-36.0),
type 1 of 15 (6.7 %, 1.2-29.8), subtype 0 of the 1 profile where both
sides give one. The low figures come from how far soilKey keys, not from
disagreements: on the data route 13 of the 16 labelled profiles stop at
the division, the class test of the Ah/C-Böden undecided in 11 of them
and that of the Braunerden in 8, because the FAO-style E and Bt horizons
are mostly left unread or read as Ah or lC. Only DE001 (Parabraunerde,
keyed Normparabraunerde), DE005 (Nassgley, keyed Normgley: the class
agrees) and DE004 reach a type. DE004 is a Gley-Podsol in its label and
a Luvisol in ISIS’s WRB; soilKey keys it as a Normgley. The label is
kept and scored as printed, a disagreement. Hugo’s decisions on the
readings of this part are in `readings.yaml`. Every classification is
unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

## soilKey 0.9.378 (2026-11-08)

### China CST 2001: an offline benchmark on the ISIS profiles from China

Eighth part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition; system
id `cst2001`). A new script, `inst/benchmarks/cst2001_isis.R`, keys the
51 ISIS reference profiles from China (CN001-CN051) with
[`classify_cst2001()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_cst2001.md)
and scores them against the CST name of their local classification. It
downloads nothing: it reads a saved list of raw ISIS profiles from its
first argument, the environment variable `SOILKEY_ISIS_CACHE` or
`tools::R_user_dir("soilKey", "cache")/isis/profiles.rds`, and stops if
there is none. The markdown report goes where the second argument says;
ISIS data are not shipped.

The labels carry the genetic name of the profile (the Genetic Soil
Classification of China) beside the CST one. A new internal matcher,
`.cst_match_label()`, finds the CST part and its taxon at any level
among the 779 names of the key (14 orders, 39 suborders, 138 groups, 588
subgroups; soilKey’s bracketed residuals left out): exact names only,
singular and plural, case and hyphenation alike, and the book’s aliases.
There is no generic tolerance of misspellings. The script adds an
explicit, documented list of the two known slips of the labels, tried
only when no part matches exactly and flagged in the report: Acidi-Undic
for Acidi-Udic Cambosols (CN008), and the order name Isohumisols of the
1991 and 1995 proposals, read as Isohumosols (CN049, scored at the
order). 50 labels match: 48 at group level, one at subgroup level
(CN014, Panic Sali-Orthic Aridosols) and one at order level (CN049);
CN043 gives the genetic name only. Each level is scored on the labels
that reach it, with a Wilson 95 % interval; a profile keyed to a
bracketed residual (CN020, \[E2\] \[Other Ferralosols\]) counts as a
disagreement and is reported apart.

First run (soilKey 0.9.378): order 26 of 50 (52.0 %, 38.5-65.2),
suborder 22 of 49 (44.9 %, 31.9-58.7), group 14 of 49 (28.6 %,
17.8-42.4), the one subgroup label not reached. The Ferralosols agree 7
of 7, the Argosols 6 of 7 and the Primosols 3 of 3; the four Anthrosols
and the two Aridosols are missed (keyed as Ferrosols, Argosols,
Cambosols or Primosols), three of the five Isohumosols go to the
Primosols, three of the seven Ferrosols to the Ferralosols, and the
Cambosols agree 5 of 13. Most names are provisional: at the order 46 of
the 51 profiles have a class tested before theirs that could not be
decided, and 48 at the group (the book’s own provisional marks are not
counted). Most of these are the Halosols (H), undecided in 27 of the 46,
and the Andosols (D), undecided in 24. The labels were given by ISSAS,
probably on the Chinese edition, so the group is the fair target and
differences below it are not errors by themselves. The genetic names
have no automatic crosswalk to the 2001 system and are not scored; WoSIS
was not queried (no national classification field is known in its
schema). Every classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other
systems byte-identical).

## soilKey 0.9.377 (2026-11-08)

### China CST 2001: gley colours in well-drained soils and the fine clay of the argic horizon

Two order-level fixes of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001; system id
`cst2001`), decided by Hugo on 2026-11-08.

Gley colours without a ferrous-iron test or Eh gave the gleyic features
provisionally (Q11) in any layer but an E or albic one, so a humus-grey
A horizon (10YR 4/2, 4/1, 5/1) of a well-drained profile keyed as
Gleyosols. A recorded drainage class of well drained or better, with no
saturation regime recorded, now rules the colour-only reading out in
every layer without redox features of its own, as it already did for the
low chroma of the redoxic features. Moderately well drained does not.
Redox features are read per layer: mottles (a mottle recorded as none,
absent, nil, - or 0 is none), redox concentrations, nodules, or a g or r
suffix of the designation (Bg, Cr). A positive test or rH 19 or less
still gives the features in any layer. With no drainage class recorded,
such an A stays provisional Gleyosols with the alternative in
`$candidates`. The drainage reader now also takes “excessively well
drained” and “somewhat excessively well drained” (the ISIS wordings) as
well drained or better, reads hyphens and underscores as spaces
(“Well-drained”), and takes the worst class of a range (“well drained to
moderately well drained” is not well drained); it serves the saturation
regimes, the redoxic features and the Foli- groups too. A mottle
recorded as none no longer counts as a redox sign beside a shallow water
table, nor as a mottle in item 3 of the redoxic features.

Item 2b of the argic horizon (p. 36) asks more total clay and more fine
clay than the eluvial horizon; soilKey read the fine clay only at 60 %
clay or more. Now, in the lower bands, the fine clay is compared with
the eluvial layers the total clay increases over: if every one with fine
clay measured has as much or more, item 2b fails; if the fine clay is
not measured in both layers (in one or neither), the total-clay increase
passes provisionally. The whole key is then run again with that increase
failing, no gate switched off: the first level whose class differs names
the fine clay as what would confirm it, even when it was assigned firmly
(an argic layer can block an earlier class, the Spodosols for instance),
and the class of that run is the alternative (a 1.2 times increase with
no clay films: Argosols, provisional, with Cambosols as the
alternative). The clay-pan and secondary clayification keep the total
clay alone. Clay films and the thin section remain alternatives to the
increase, as printed, and the fine-clay ratio a third higher stays a
“normally”. The alkalic horizon reads the same items, so it follows the
argic horizon; its evidence grade, read on its own items, is unaffected.
A block of alternatives in the key (any_of) is now provisional only when
every alternative that passed is.

Names are unchanged except the H2.2 example, a well-drained Halosol that
was Gleyic on colours alone and is now Typic Aqui-Orthic Halosols. The
suborder examples G2, H1, K1 and K2, whose argic or alkalic horizon
rests on item 2b, now record their fine clay, so they and the group and
subgroup examples built on them (the Alkalic Halosols, the Argi- and
Argic Ferrosols, the Argic Aridosols) keep their names, not
provisionally. On the 51 ISIS profiles from China no name changes; seven
Argosols, Ferrosols and Isohumosols with an argic horizon by the clay
increase alone now carry the fine-clay warning and an alternative. Every
other classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems
byte-identical).

## soilKey 0.9.376 (2026-11-07)

### China CST 2001: the subgroups of orders H to N

Seventh part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition; system
id `cst2001`).
[`classify_cst2001()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_cst2001.md)
now keys a pedon of orders H to N (Halosols, Gleyosols, Isohumosols,
Ferrosols, Argosols, Cambosols, Primosols) below its group to the 412
subgroups of key 5.2 (pp. 108-180), in the book’s order, in
`inst/rules/cst2001/subgroups/{H..N}.yaml`, with the page, the name as
printed (the canonical spelling of Q2, the other printed forms and the
singular as aliases), the adjective and soilKey’s Portuguese gloss.
Every group of the book now has its subgroups: the 588 names of Appendix
1 each resolve to one row, and the note that the name stops at the group
is gone (soilKey’s bracketed residuals keep theirs). J1.2.1, K1.1.1 and
M3.5.1 carry the book’s own provisional mark.

New presets in `presets.yaml`, with their criteria in
`R/key-cst-subgroups-hn.R`: the albic horizon, or a glossic horizon or
glossic evidence, anywhere, within a depth, below the mollic epipedon or
above the argic horizon; the calcic horizon alone, with soft powdery
lime, or with the hypercalcic horizon and the calcipan, with its upper
boundary within or between depths; Eutric and pH 7.0 as the converse
tests, Leachic as a share of the window, the ferric property throughout
the argic horizon or claypan or the B, and Dystric throughout the
claypan or the argic horizon; a property in some subhorizon of the B
(allitic, alic, ferric, spodic evidence); features in a share of the
window (Phosphic) or in every layer of it (Epigleyic); salic evidence
with its duration; para-alkalic evidence; gleyic evidence of perched
water (Stagnic); a hue in a subhorizon of the upper half of the B
(Xanthic of M5.4.4); Permic. Written directly: the kind of the histic
epipedon (Fibric, Sapric), the window below the top of the claypan
(L1.1.2), the Fe-Mn nodules of an indurated subhorizon (Concretic),
cinders over 0-25 cm (Cinderic), carbon over 0-20 cm (Grayic), vertic
evidence within 25 cm (Verti-lithic), and the torrential and marine salt
profiles of the Halosols (Dilluvic, Marinic). The presets of 0.9.375 and
the subgroups of orders A to G are unchanged. A new site attribute,
`salic_months_per_year`, gives the months a year with salic evidence the
Parasalic subgroups of M2.2 and M3.3 ask for; not recorded, the evidence
observed passes provisionally (Q15).

[`make_cst2001_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_cst2001_example.md)
gives one profile per subgroup of orders H to N, each keying to its own
subgroup, not provisionally (588 subgroup examples in all); the suborder
and group examples keep their order, suborder and group and now reach a
subgroup. Every other classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the
other systems byte-identical).

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-08). The nine defects of the
review are fixed: shajiang in a run (and the M2.2 group key), a B
subhorizon or the whole B measured within 125 cm of the mineral soil
surface, the upper half of the B of M5.4.4 capped at 125 cm, Dilluvic
with a layer not measured or a description ending above 200 cm, Marinic
with the carbonate not measured, and a Lithic contact or a horizon with
its upper boundary within a depth (gypsic horizon, salipan, alkalic
evidence, argic, sulfuric and plinthic horizons) are undecided when the
description stops above the depth asked, not on rock or a contact, as
the feature windows already were (the Lithic rows of orders A to G too);
phosphic evidence of N4.7.1 reads the mineral soil surface
(`phosphic_property_cst(datum =)`); M1.6.2 takes a calcic horizon
starting at 100 cm; Verti-lithic reads a half-open window. Alkalic
evidence is now read on its printed items (p. 39): the weakly developed
structure of the alkalic horizon and an ESP of 5 or more within 40 cm in
a subsurface layer, without the argic items. With a short paddy history
the anthrostagnic evidence passes its regime item on the paddy record,
and the saturation axis reads the anthrostagnic regime from paddy
records only when the history is not recorded or longer than half of the
years. The lithologic characters of sandy deposits are read from the
mineral soil surface, litter left out. The argillans of a claypan (item
4) qualify the first mineral layer, so a claypan can be exposed
(L4.3.1). With these readings every subgroup is reachable and has an
example. soilKey’s other readings of this part are accepted, with these
choices: Stagnic undecided under a flooded record, Recalcaric undecided
when the description ends above 100 cm, Concretic indurated only
(indurated or extremely hard) below the base of the albic run, and
M5.4.4 a run whose top lies in the upper half of the B. A class assigned
on a provisional reading now names what would confirm it (a ferrous-iron
test, a deeper description, the extent of the contact, the months with
salic evidence, the duration of the cracks).

## soilKey 0.9.375 (2026-11-07)

### China CST 2001: the subgroups of orders A to G

Sixth part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition; system
id `cst2001`). The registry now names the level subgroups, and
[`classify_cst2001()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_cst2001.md)
keys a pedon of orders A to G (Histosols, Anthrosols, Spodosols,
Andosols, Ferralosols, Vertosols, Aridosols) below its group to the 176
subgroups of key 5.2 (pp. 76-108), in the book’s order, one file per
order in `inst/rules/cst2001/subgroups/` keyed by group, with the page,
the name as printed (the canonical spelling of Q2, the other printed
forms and the singular as aliases), the adjective and soilKey’s
Portuguese gloss in `levels$name_pt`. Typic, the residual of each list,
passes by default. `[A1.3.x]` Lithic Hemi-Permagelic Histosols, listed
in Appendix 1 but not in the key, is keyed at its Appendix position with
the test of A1.2.3 (Q3), and the result notes it. C1.1.1 and D1.1.1
carry the book’s own provisional mark. The groups of orders H to N stop
at the group, with a note, until their subgroups follow in the next
part.

The same adjective carries different depths, thicknesses and extents in
different groups, so each subgroup row calls a preset of the new
`inst/rules/cst2001/presets.yaml` with the numbers printed for it
(Lithic, Mottlic, Gleyic, Parasalic, Sodic, Sulfic, Dystric, Eutrophic,
Trunic, Xanthic, Dark, Takyric, the cracks of the Aridic and Ustic
subgroups …).
[`load_rules()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/load_rules.md)
expands the calls into ordinary blocks when the rules are loaded
(`R/rule-presets.R`), so the rule engine does not change; a complex
subgroup (Calcari-mottlic, Aridi-trunic, Gypsi-panic, Sodi-takyric) is
both of its parts and is keyed before them, as printed.
`.validate_rules()` reports a preset called with an unknown parameter or
without a required one. The criteria the subgroup keys define are
written in `R/key-cst-subgroups.R`: a lithic contact within or between
depths (with the fragments and plane-extent alternatives of the later
orders), a feature in a run of layers, in layers totalling a thickness
or anywhere in a window, the Buric and Terric mineral layers and the
tier kinds of the Histosols, a lithic contact within the control
section, the carbonate pattern of anthro-recalcification, the soluble
salts of the Parasalic Siltigi-Orthic Anthrosols, base saturation or pH
in a window, base saturation in a share of it, hues in a run, a share or
the upper part of the B, the order’s horizon at the surface, the dark
mixed surface of the Aridosols and an argic horizon with lime
infiltrates. Every test is three-valued as before: an undecided subgroup
before the assigned one makes the name provisional, and a subgroup
assigned on a provisional reading (gley colours without a test, a window
cut by the base of the description) comes with the alternative the key
would reach.

[`make_cst2001_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_cst2001_example.md)
takes a subgroup code of orders A to G as well and gives one profile per
subgroup (176), each keying to its own subgroup, not provisionally; the
suborder and group examples keep their order, suborder and group. The
readings of this part, soilKey’s own for Hugo’s word, are in
`inst/rules/cst2001/readings.yaml`. Every other classification is
unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-07): a window that runs below the
base of the description is undecided there unless the description ends
on rock or a contact; the thickness not described joins the upper bound
only, so a feature already found above is a firm pass and otherwise the
subgroup is undecided and the name provisional (Mottlic, Endogleyic,
Gleyic, Sulfic, Parasalic, Sodic, Paracalcic, Paragypsic, Calcic,
Shajiang, and the tiers of the Histosols). soilKey’s other readings of
this part accepted as proposed. Trunic: a recorded A, AB, AC or E at the
mineral soil surface fails before anything else, and the anthropic
truncation flag is read only when the first layer has no designation; BA
and B/A count as a B; the ferralic horizon is tested on the first layer
whatever its designation. Where a subgroup names the gypsic horizon
alone (G2.1.7, G2.2.3, G2.2.5) a hypergypsic horizon does not count. The
preset expander also expands a preset written directly as a mapping and
reports a call with extra keys. New aliases Fe-leachic-Gleyi-Stagnic
Anthrosols (p. 83) and Gypsi-Panic Sali-Orthic Aridosols (p. 105).
Gypsic evidence left open by an undescribed layer below now names the
gypsum to measure.

## soilKey 0.9.374 (2026-11-07)

### China CST 2001: the groups

Fifth part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition; system
id `cst2001`). The registry now names the level groups, and
[`classify_cst2001()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_cst2001.md)
keys a pedon below its suborder to the 138 groups of key 5.2
(pp. 75-176), in the book’s order, one file per order in
`inst/rules/cst2001/groups/` keyed by suborder, with the page, the name
as printed (the canonical spelling of Q2, the other printed forms as
aliases) and soilKey’s Portuguese gloss in `levels$name_pt`. Where the
book prints no residual, soilKey’s `[A1.4] [Other Permagelic Histosols]`
and `[A2.5] [Other Orthic Histosols]` close the list (Q4); the result
notes that the name stops there, as it now also does for
`[E2] [Other Ferralosols]`, which has no groups. C1.1 and C2.1, all the
Spodosols, carry the book’s own provisional mark. The groups read the
horizons, characteristics and regimes of the earlier parts and the
criteria the group keys define, written in `R/key-cst-groups.R`: the
Foli- groups and the kind that predominates in the surface tier of the
Histosols, the grey iron-percoleached subhorizon and the iron
accumulation of the Stagnic Anthrosols, the hydromorphic cumulic
epipedon, the rhodic and xanthic colours of the Ferralosols by the
thickness of the window, the udic regime bordering on the perudic one, a
calcic horizon starting between 50 and 125 cm, the thickness of the
mollic epipedon, an albic horizon above the claypan, folic histic
evidence, shajiang, the takyric surface of the Halosols, coral sands
within 100 cm, carbonate rocks or coral sands in more than half of the
horizons, and a property in some subhorizon of the B or throughout it
(allitic, highly weathered, alic, acid). Every test is three-valued as
before: an undecided group before the assigned one makes the name
provisional, and a group assigned on a provisional reading comes with
the alternative the key would reach. A residual group named for a regime
that the soil does not have (the Udi- groups; the Aqui-Orthic Halosols,
named for the aquic regime) keeps its class, with a note.

[`make_cst2001_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_cst2001_example.md)
takes a group code as well and gives one profile per group (140, the two
bracketed residuals included), each keying to its own group, not
provisionally; the 39 suborder examples still key to their suborder, now
with a group (a few were given the measurements their group asks for, so
that it is decided). The readings of this part, soilKey’s own for Hugo’s
word, are in `inst/rules/cst2001/readings.yaml`. Every other
classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems
byte-identical).

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-07): soilKey’s readings of this
part accepted as proposed (J3.1 and M4.2 included). B1.2 reads the grey
colour alone (moist chroma 2 or less, as printed), with no test of the
iron. The Foli- groups take a well-drained record for the days of
saturation only as a stand-in, flagged in the trace and named in a
warning. Where a group names the calcic horizon alone (F1.1, F3.2, G1.1,
J2.4, L2.2) a hypercalcic horizon does not count. H1.1 reads the depth
of the polygonal cracks (`cracks_depth_cm`, 1-4 cm) first, the crust
thickness standing in, flagged. Fixed on the review: the depth below the
base of the description is undecided in the colour shares of the
Ferralosols and the coral share of M5.2, and a share that passes only on
the part described passes provisionally, with the alternative; the
thickness of the mollic epipedon (J2.3) is undecided while a layer below
it may still belong to it; `layer_run_cst()` takes
`grade = "at_least_evidence"`, so gleyic evidence counts in M4.2.

## soilKey 0.9.373 (2026-11-06)

### China CST 2001: the registry, the orders and the suborders

Fourth part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition). The
system is registered as `cst2001` (aliases `cst`, `china`, `chinese`;
experimental and opt-in; order 15 in the registry, after the German KA5
and South Africa planned at 13 and 14), with the levels orders and
suborders for now.
[`classify_cst2001()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_cst2001.md)
keys a pedon to the 14 orders of key 5.1 (pp. 72-75) and the 39
suborders of key 5.2, in the book’s order, on the 33 diagnostic horizons
(0.9.371), the 25 diagnostic characteristics (0.9.372) and the regimes
(0.9.370), plus the criteria the key defines where it uses them (the
share of the upper 60 cm with andic property, the organic soil materials
of the Histosols, an argic horizon above the spodic one, the base
saturation window of the Isohumosols, the claypan with illuviation
argillans, the humic spodic subhorizons, the texture of the Vitric
Andosols, the crack days of the Ustic Vertosols, the low n value or clay
of the Cambosols, irrigation and anthro-silting within 50 cm).
Three-valued: an undecided class before the assigned one makes the name
provisional; a class assigned on a reading the book leaves open (gley
colours without a test, cracks for their duration) carries a warning.
soilKey’s residual `[E2] [Other Ferralosols]` closes the suborders of
the Ferralosols, and E1 takes the udic or perudic regime (Q4). Names in
English as printed, with soilKey’s Portuguese gloss in `levels$name_pt`;
the book’s own provisional marks are read from `book_provisional` (none
falls on an order or suborder). A residual named for the udic regime
reached under another recorded regime keeps its class, with a note. The
approximate equivalents of each order in US Soil Taxonomy (1999) and the
WRB (1998), Tables 4.2 and 4.3, are a note in the result, the report and
the app (`inst/rules/cst2001/correlation.yaml`; Q1), never a class. The
horizon panel of `identify_horizons(pedon, "cst2001")` is in the trace
(phase `horizons`).

[`make_cst2001_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_cst2001_example.md)
gives one profile per suborder (39, each keying to its own suborder, not
provisionally) and, with `near_miss = TRUE`, fourteen near misses, one
per order. The app lists China among the national systems with the 39
examples; `data-raw/cst2001_taxa.csv` holds the 779 names of Appendix 1
in the canonical spelling of Q2 (with soilKey’s `[E2]`), the other
printed forms as aliases. A recorded drainage class of well drained or
better now rules out the saturation regimes of the CST (stagnic,
anthrostagnic, aquic, peraquic). The readings of this part are in
`inst/rules/cst2001/readings.yaml`. Every other classification is
unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-06): soilKey’s readings of this
part accepted, with these changes. The spodic materials by colour alone
only directly below an albic horizon or an E layer, elsewhere with a
sign (cementation, cracked coatings, Alo + 1/2 Feo 0.50 % with half or
less above, ODOE); measured oxalate without a sign gives spodic evidence
at most, no data leaves a red B undecided (red Ferralosols, Ferrosols
and Argosols no longer key as Spodosols). The base saturation of the
Isohumosols below the description is read as saturated under a
calcareous lowest horizon, otherwise the window stops at the base of the
description and the class is provisional. Runs of gleyic and redoxic
features skip rock and organic layers. The permafrost of the Cambosols
(M 4), the contacts of the Vertosols (F 2) and the anthroturbic layer
(N1) are read from the mineral soil surface (`datum = "mineral"` of
`permafrost_layer_cst()`, `lithic_contact_cst()`,
`paralithic_contact_cst()`, `anthroturbic_layer_cst()`). The
anthrostagnic epipedon and the agric horizon on a plain A are ruled out
when an item fails, instead of undecided. M 3 keeps the printed clay
under 80 g/kg and reads an unmeasured n value under 0.7 in a layer not
saturated. The Vitric Andosols take sand, loamy sand and sandy loam
only. Histosol item b is literal. A recorded non-volcanic parent
material rules out the andic property; pH(H2O) under 5.5 or a perudic
regime rules out the salic horizon where salts are not measured; under
an aridic regime a crust not recorded leaves the aridic epipedon
undecided. A class assigned on a provisional reading (gley colours
without a test, Q11) comes with the class the key would reach without
it, in `candidates` (kind “alternative”), a warning, the trace and the
printed result, never as the class.

## soilKey 0.9.372 (2026-11-06)

### China CST 2001: the diagnostic characteristics

Third part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition; system
id `cst2001`, registered in a later part). The 25 diagnostic
characteristics of the book (pp. 43-64) read on the data
(`R/diagnostics-cst-properties.R`), three-valued, with the layers, the
missing attributes and the fallbacks used: organic soil materials with
their five kinds (fibric, hemic, sapric, folic, mattic) and the control
section and tiers of the Histosols; the seven lithologic characters
within 125 cm (`lithologic_characters_cst(kind =)` and
`lc_<kind>_cst()`); lithic and paralithic contacts; anthro-silting
materials; vertic features and vertic evidence; the anthroturbic layer;
gleyic features and gleyic evidence (gley colours without a ferrous-iron
test or Eh met provisionally, Q11); redoxic features; the permafrost
layer; frost-thawic features; the n value; the isohumic property (Rh 0.4
or less, the printed “4” read as 0.4, Q9; the book’s default bulk
densities where none was measured, flagged, Q10); the humic, andic,
ferric (every layer of the B, Q23), allitic (the Ki of the sulfuric
attack flagged, Q16), alic, phosphic, sodic and calcaric properties with
their evidences; base saturation (eutric, dystric, eutrophic, dystrophic
in a window); sulfidic materials (no number in the book: the WRB number
and stand-ins, always with a lower grade). The two regimes are the
readers of 0.9.370. Layer characteristics take the grades of the
horizons (full, evidence, at least evidence) and join the horizon panel
(`characteristics`, `characteristic_evidences`,
`characteristic_stand_ins`); the sulfuric horizon now reads the sulfidic
materials under its base. Numbers in
`inst/rules/cst2001/thresholds.yaml` with their pages; Hugo’s decisions
as applied and soilKey’s own readings of this part, for his word, in
`inst/rules/cst2001/readings.yaml`. Fixtures of the differences from the
WRB 2022 (sodic ESP 30, the isohumic ratio, the Chinese gley colours,
alic pH(KCl) 4.0, andic of KST 1996, ferric). No new attribute. Every
other classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems
byte-identical).

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-06): rock layers carry no soil
colour; carbonate rocks by rock nouns only, undecided where the rock is
not named; the 60 cm Histosol tier needs fibric moss materials; frozen
designations read after a discontinuity numeral, and frozen ground not
recorded is absent where the description reaches the depth asked (only a
frigid or warmer regime rules permafrost out); the scaly structure in an
A or B only; provisional gleyic features marked in the panel, and gley
colours alone not read in an E or albic layer without redox features or
a saturation regime; the allitic fine-earth ratio (the sulfuric Ki) ORed
with the clay ratio; redoxic item 3 without a carbon exclusion, false
under a well-drained record; northern red earths by a red earth or red
clay parent material; the calcaric property on measured CaCO3, else
effervescence, else pH under 6.5 non-calcaric; the isohumic depths
scaled to the contact; the sulfuric horizon’s lower grade only on the
WRB stand-ins; the phosphic pattern with no reversal over 10 %; the
sandy carbon as a weighted mean; every purplish layer with fragments
under 4 cm.

## soilKey 0.9.371 (2026-11-06)

### China CST 2001: the diagnostic horizons

Second part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition; system
id `cst2001`, registered in a later part). The 33 diagnostic horizons of
the book (pp. 20-43), each read layer by layer on the data
(`R/diagnostics-cst-horizons.R`, `R/diagnostics-cst-anthropic.R`): a
grade per layer, full, evidence (the book’s weaker grade, for the 15
horizons that have one), none or undecided; readers
`<horizon>_cst(pedon, grade = "full" | "evidence" | "at_least_evidence", top_max)`
for the key, `phos_agric_horizon_cst()` for the phos-agric kind of the
agric horizon and `argic_horizon_cst(natro = TRUE)` for the natro-argic
horizon of the Aridosols. A WRB or USDA diagnostic of soilKey stands in
only where a CST descriptor is missing, flagged with a lower grade.
`.cst_identify()` gives the horizon panel (the horizons, evidences,
kinds and stand-ins of each layer);
`identify_horizons(pedon, "cst2001")` reaches it once the system is
registered. The numbers are in `inst/rules/cst2001/thresholds.yaml` with
their pages; soilKey’s readings of this part, for Hugo’s word, in
`inst/rules/cst2001/readings.yaml`. Fixtures of the differences from the
WRB 2022: the argic clay increase (+3 / x1.2 / +8 / fine clay +8),
plinthite 10 %, the alkalic horizon at ESP 30 and pH 9.0, the salic
horizon on salts or the 1:1 EC. Every other classification is unchanged
(the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

## soilKey 0.9.370 (2026-11-05)

### China CST 2001: the attributes, the shared readers and the regimes

First part of the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001, English edition; system
id `cst2001`, registered in a later part). New horizon attributes (36,
section “Chinese system (CST 2001)”, among them `fine_clay_pct`,
`clay_films_thickness_mm`, `reduced_matrix_pct`, `ferricyanide_test`,
`eh_mv`, `p_olsen_mg_kg`, `ec_1to1_dS_m`, `shajiang_pct`,
`pyroclastic_fragments_pct`) and site attributes (14: `aridity_index`,
`aridity_index_max_month`, `climatic_moisture_regime`,
`udic_perudic_border`, `mean_summer_soil_temp_C`, `summer_saturated`,
`cracks_open_days`, `irrigated` and others), each with its fallback.
`soil_moisture_regime` takes stagnic, anthrostagnic and peraquic, which
the USDA key reads as aquic; `soil_temperature_regime` takes permagelic,
read by the USDA key as gelic. The shared readers (`R/cst-readers.R`:
units, clay activity, free iron, texture and particle-size classes, hue
ranks, the mixed surface, windows and shares, storage with the book’s
default bulk densities, the arid region) and the regime readers
(`R/cst-regimes.R`, each regime with its source in the trace) read the
numbers of `inst/rules/cst2001/thresholds.yaml`. The moisture regime is
read on two axes, climatic (aridic, ustic, udic, perudic) and saturation
(stagnic, anthrostagnic, aquic, peraquic), so a paddy recorded udic is
anthrostagnic and a value on one axis says nothing of the other;
permafrost within 50 cm gives the permagelic regime ahead of an estimate
from the air; Cr is a paralithic contact only with a contact recorded or
an FAO, WRB or USDA notation declared (otherwise the redox r of the
Chinese field notation); an O horizon without a measured bulk density
takes the range 0.1-0.4 Mg/m3, so a storage is a range. Hugo’s decisions
of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 are in `inst/rules/cst2001/readings.yaml`.
Every other classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other
systems byte-identical).

## soilKey 0.9.365 (2026-11-07)

### Germany (KA5, 2005): the varieties and subvarieties

[`classify_ka5()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_ka5.md)
now keys the fifth and sixth levels of the German systematics (section
5.7.1.4, pp. 263-282), an additive level after the subtype (Hugo’s
decision Q1): the 38 variety codes of Tab. 49 by the 22 criteria of Tab.
46, offered where Tab. 50 marks the subtype, plus the six of its note 1
(og, c, z, k, v, ku) everywhere except where the subtype’s own formula
writes the feature; the subvarieties as a digit on the letter (s and g
flach 2 or tief 4, p schwach 2, mäßig 3 or stark 4; the base-saturation
class BS1-BS5 of Tab. 48 on the potential or effective CEC is reported
in the trace). Tab. 50 is in `inst/rules/ka5/varieties.yaml` with its
pages, all 223 subtype rows read from the page images (the terrestrial
rows of pp. 274-279 for the first time), with the codes, criteria,
thresholds, subvariety classes, symbol rules I-VII and the printed
examples. Each criterion is read on the horizons, three-valued: on the
notation by the symbols written (Aeh, Ahe, Sew, rGo, eGo, zAh, oAh, Bms,
Gkso, Cbtv, Ctv, Akh, Ap, the base-saturation marks), on the data by the
record (base saturation, colours, organic substance, carbonate, EC,
jarosite, cementation, clay films and bands, erosion degree, rewetting,
land use); the humus forms only as recorded. A variety the data leave
open is not named: it is listed as undecided in `trace$varieties` and
one warning, the result not provisional (p. 263). The result gains rows
of level `variety` (the code with its digit, the word of the name, the
gloss, the full symbol in a `symbol` column), the full name in `name`
(“podsolige pseudovergleyte Normbraunerde”, “(Acker)Gley”) and the
symbol in `trace$variety$symbol` (`p2.s2BBn`, `vGGn`); the development
depth of Tab. 47 is reported in the trace. The further subtypes of the
type that pass join as a combination (Q21; Tab. 46 no. 17, rules II-IV:
`PP-GG-BB` Podsol-Gley-Braunerde, `BB-GGe`, `GGh-GGc` (Humus)Kalkgley);
the overlays of Tab. 46 no. 18 stay out of the levels and the name,
reported in the trace (`trace$variety$overlay`); r and e stand before
the letter they qualify (`BB-rGG`, `r.gLFn`, `LF-eBB`). An Aeh, Ahe, Akh
or Aka takes a subtype formula’s plain Ah slot, so a podzolic or
cultotrophic topsoil keeps the Norm subtype.
`make_ka5_example(variety = ...)` gives a profile for each of the 38
codes; every printed example of pp. 268-272 reads back to its name from
its symbol. The levels above the variety of every KA5 example are
unchanged; their names gain the varieties their data carry (the default
Bv and Tv colours of the examples are no longer iron-rich or reddish;
the podzolic B of the subtype examples keeps its colour, so their data
twins key as before, and is read as reddish). New horizon attribute
`schwertmannite_present` (the variety sf). soilKey’s readings are in
`readings.yaml`. Every other classification is unchanged.

Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-07): the name carries the
varieties, the overlays do not (the decision of 0.9.364 stands); open
varieties stay out of `provisional_because`; rt is read on the type’s
own B or T horizon (Bv, Bs, Tv, Bt); a feature the subtype’s formula
already writes is not named (an optional (e) counts as written; no
note-1 c on the Kalkpaternia, Pararendzina, Rendzina and
Kalktschernosem); on the notation route the carbonate data stand in for
the prefix e only on rows with no symbol, and a Tschernosem’s carbonate
is not geogenic by default; an Ae under an Ahe is stark podsolig; rule
IV allows a hydromorphic type last (BB-LL-SS); a rewetting not recorded
is absent; the base-saturation class goes to the trace only; a and g on
the same deep aGo name a only; no anthropic-truncation stand-in for e;
eu, m and dy are open where no horizon outside the C reaches into 2 to
\< 5 dm, and the O/C soils read their O horizon; the relict r qualifies
a g or s only when that one is named, otherwise the type (rMCn); b on
the data needs a brown colour; the aG of the variety a lies strictly
deeper than 8 dm, and a description ending above it leaves a open; sf
accepts schwertmannite.

## soilKey 0.9.364 (2026-11-06)

### Germany (KA5, 2005): the semiterrestrial, subhydric and Moor subtypes; the overlays

[`classify_ka5()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_ka5.md)
now keys the subtypes of the semiterrestrial, subhydric and Moore types
from the type texts (pp. 238-262): 85 subtypes (A 12, G 40, M 15, Ü 3, I
3, H 4, K 7 and the unit KV-KM; the Nassstrand and the four subhydric
types of class J have none), in
`inst/rules/ka5/subtypes/{A,G,M,UE,I,J,H,K}.yaml`, with the order and
fallback of Q21: the Auenböden by their aGo at 4 to \< 8 dm (Gley-X) or
their aG at 8 dm or deeper (the Norm, an aG under the description
allowed); the Gley transitions of the terrestrial and Auen types (the Gr
typically 8 to 13 dm, not required), the Hang- and Quellen- subtypes by
the prefix s or q (on the data by `groundwater_source`, the slope for
the s), the Oxigley by the oxygen-rich groundwater or no Gr in a profile
described to 13 dm (Q16), the Moorgley with no Norm subtype; the
Marschen, the Strand and the Watt by their tidal prefixes tm, tb, tp;
the Niedermoor and Hochmoor by the pH of their peat where measured; the
Erd- and Mulmmoore by their suffixes, with the transitional unit KV-KM.
Two open subtypes of Q22, in brackets: “\[Übergangsmoorgley\]” and
“\[vermulmtes Erdhochmoor\]”. The Rohmarsch keeps Q20: a Go-Ah is a
Rohmarsch unless the site is embanked or not tidally flooded.

The overlays (Tab. 46 no. 18) are reported in `trace$overlay` and the
warnings, as varieties that change neither the levels nor the name: a
mineral cover on a Moor keeps the Moor (Q7), named as substrate only
under 2 dm, “flacher Gley über Niedermoor” (`GG\HN`) at 2 to \< 3 dm and
“Gley über Niedermoor” (`GG/HN`) at 3 to \< 4 dm, the cover keyed as the
mineral soil it would be; a fersiallitic or ferrallitic palaeosol under
the soil is named “… über Fersiallit / Ferrallit” (Q19); a buried soil
(fossil horizons of a layer II or deeper) is keyed alone from its own
top and named by the thickness of the soil above, under 3 dm “flach”, 3
to \< 7 dm, the Organomarsch over a Podsol by its own steps (1.5 and 3
dm, p. 254). `make_ka5_example(subtype = ...)` gives a profile for each
of the 85 subtypes and the two open ones, with a data twin (63 key on
the data alone); the wet type examples key to their Norm subtype and
keep their types. The Paternia gate now leaves a Paternia-Vega (an aM
under the ilC) to the Vega, and the Auenböden take an S under an aM
anywhere above it (the Pseudogley-Vega). soilKey’s readings are in
`readings.yaml`. Every other classification is unchanged.

- After the review (Hugo, 2026-11-06): the readings accepted; only an aM
  (prefix a) beginning above 8 dm takes a profile out of the Paternia,
  aM bands in the ilC keeping it; the Gley-Rambla, Gley-Paternia and
  Gley-Kalkpaternia allow their aG under the description; the
  Wechselgley takes no q; a Moorgley whose peat is of no known kind
  leaves the subtype undecided, and the Hang-, Quellen- and Hochmoorgley
  are tested before the Niedermoorgley; the Normhochmoor and the
  Hochmoor gate read the pH in the hH(w); on the data route a horizon
  among a row’s candidates, or one the data key does not build (Gso,
  Hvm, an unrecorded secondary carbonate, a layer II, an A or M part),
  leaves a subtype undecided rather than failed; a Moor under a cover of
  less than 4 dm reads its type from the top of the peat (Ah/Go over an
  nHv: GG/KV).

- The bleached and podzolic horizons on the data (Hugo, 2026-11-06): the
  order of tests on the data reads a pale first row over a pale Ae over
  a Bh or Bs as an Ahe; a B with the Cp/Fep of a Bh or Bs is no Bt when
  no clay coatings are recorded; illuvial humus (the Ah’s humus minimum
  under a pale horizon without it) or oxalate Fe and Al accumulated
  under a pale horizon leave the Bt and the podzolic B both undecided;
  under a podzolic B a clay increase with no clay coatings recorded is
  no Bt, and the eluvial Al of a Parabraunerde under a podzolic B is
  read; a G with a podzolic B part is a Bhs-Go, not an Ah-Go. On the
  data the Podsol-Gley twin now keys PP-GG (it read Ah/Al/Bt-Go before),
  the Podsol-Braunerde PP-BB (was a Parabraunerde), the Braunerde-Podsol
  BB-PP (was LL-PP), the Plaggenesch-Podsol a Podsol (was a
  Parabraunerde); LL-PP, GG-PP and YK-PP keep their subtypes with fewer
  candidates. The types of the type examples and of the notation route
  are unchanged.

## soilKey 0.9.363 (2026-11-06)

### Germany (KA5, 2005): the subtypes of the 28 terrestrial types

[`classify_ka5()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_ka5.md)
now keys the subtypes (Subtypen) of the terrestrial types from the type
texts (pp. 202-237): 138 subtypes of the 13 terrestrial classes (F 2, O
3, R 27, T 11, D 8, B 10, L 15, P 11, C 6, S 27, X 4, Y 14; the
palaeosols VV and VW have none), in `inst/rules/ka5/subtypes/`, and the
registry lists the level `subtypes`. Each subtype is its printed formula
or formulas, matched on the horizons with the sequence engine, its depth
windows read from the GOF (the Gley-X subtypes by the first G at 4 to \<
8 dm, the Pseudogley-X by the first S, the Podsol-X and X-Podsol by the
bottom of the podzol B, the humic and anthropogenic parts by 4 dm …) and
its numbers (the base-saturation marks of the Ah/C-Boeden on the subtype
scale, the clay band of the Parabraunerde-Braunerde, the Fahlerde’s clay
difference in the LF-X subtypes, Cp/Fep, the slope of the
Hangpseudogley, the Terra material …), with the limits in
`thresholds.yaml`. Following Hugo’s decisions: inside a type the
transitional subtypes come first in printed order, then the deviation
subtypes, the Norm subtype last as the fallback, and every subtype that
passes is listed in `trace$subtypes_passing` (Q21); the Treposol has no
Norm subtype, and the Rigosol and Treposol take an open subtype for the
type still recognisable under the R, written in brackets (“\[BB-YY\]”,
“\[Treposol aus Braunerde\]”, Q22). A subtype the data leave open makes
the result provisional, with the others as candidates; the Fahlerde-X
subtypes and the Parabraunerde-Braunerde hold on the designation,
provisionally, when their clay is not measured (C13).
`make_ka5_example(subtype = ...)` gives one profile per subtype in the
KA5 notation and its data twin (51 of the 138 key on the data alone);
the 56 type examples keep their types and key to their Norm subtype. The
Pseudogley gate now takes the Scw and Scd of the Kalkpseudogley, and the
Ranker gate a thin loose layer over solid rock under 3 dm. The readings
are in `readings.yaml`. Every other classification is unchanged.

- After the review (Hugo, 2026-11-06): the horizons under a formula are
  free and its final C is met by any deeper row, undecided when nothing
  is described under it; a slot (X-)Y takes a run of X-Y and Y horizons;
  the Lessives gate takes a Bt-Sd (the first forms of SS-LL and SS-LF);
  the Fahlerde’s clay difference is the Ael against the Bt, not the
  Ael+Bt (also for the type); the Euranker and Euregosol need no Bv; the
  Norm subtype tests its formula and the marks that complement a
  deviation and holds provisionally, the deviation a candidate, when
  they fail (R1); an Sw written without s on a slope of 9 % or more
  leaves the Hangpseudogley undecided (R2); the open subtypes need a Bt
  for LF, the printed window for a G or S, and never repeat a printed
  code; a solid rock with no recorded top leaves the Ranker undecided;
  the base-saturation marks read every horizon of the topsoil.

## soilKey 0.9.362 (2026-11-06)

### Germany (KA5, 2005): the registry and the key to the 56 soil types

[`classify_ka5()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_ka5.md)
keys a profile to the divisions (Abteilungen), classes (Klassen) and
types (Typen) of the German soil systematics by Tab. 51 of the
Bodenkundliche Kartieranleitung (pp. 283-288): the Moore, the subhydric,
semiterrestrial and terrestrial soils, 21 classes and 56 types, read on
the horizons of `identify_horizons(pedon, "ka5")` (the KA5 notation,
else the order of tests on the data). The system is registered as `ka5`
(aliases `germany`, `kartieranleitung`, `bodensystematik`), experimental
and opt-in. Following Hugo’s decisions: Tab. 51 with the numbers of the
type texts (Q6) and two rules of the figures (Q5), the Moor under a
cover of less than 4 dm (Q7), the last symbol carrying the horizon (Q8),
the rock of the Ah/C-Boeden (Q15, Q18), a thick Ah without Axh undecided
(Q17), the upper soil over a palaeosol (Q19), the Rigosol and Treposol
by the record (Q23). A gate the data leave open makes the name
provisional; the Fahlerde on its designation without the clay (C13) and
the Rigosol without the kind of cultivation are listed as provisional
too. The names are as printed (German), with English and Portuguese
glosses in the rules; the horizon panel is in `trace$horizon_panel`, the
figures’ consistency flags in `trace$figures`.
[`make_ka5_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_ka5_example.md)
gives one profile per type in the KA5 notation, its near miss and its
data twin (51 of the 56 key on the data alone; the Knick-, Dwog- and
Haftnaessemarsch and the palaeosols need the notation). The Pro app
offers the 56 examples. The subtypes, overlays and varieties come next.
Every other classification is unchanged.

- After the review (Hugo, 2026-11-06, the 19 defects): buried soils no
  longer decide the present soil; tidal prefixes count only in the
  present solum, z as tidal; the Axh window and the colour conflict of
  the Schwarzerden; truncated descriptions and missing depths undecided;
  the peat body across thin interbeds; the Kalkmarsch by its carbonatic
  horizon under 4 dm; one strict R bound; the Moore types on the
  topsoil; stand-ins and a class without type shown as provisional; the
  Organomarsch without o, marl under a Terra and an Ai on block debris
  (Syrosem) as Hugo decided.

## soilKey 0.9.361 (2026-11-06)

### Germany (KA5, 2005): the horizons on the data

The KA5 horizons read on the recorded data, used by nothing yet:
`.ka5_identify()` (the identification `identify_horizons(pedon, "ka5")`
will reach once the system is registered) reads every layer by soilKey’s
fixed order of tests (Hugo’s decision Q9: F, H and O, Y, R, E, M, G, S,
A, B with T and P, C, then the prefixes and suffixes and the transitions
Bv-Sw, Sw-Bv, Bv-Go, Go-Bv, Ah-Bv, Ah-Go). Every test is three-valued:
an undecided one gives candidates and the attributes that would decide
them. A layer written in the KA5 notation keeps its horizon and the
data’s reading goes to the evidence. The readers (`R/ka5-readers.R`):
the depth datum GOF (p. 79), organic substance with the 15 to \< 17.4 %
band (Q10), the Ah minimum with the silt of other fractions (Q11), the
Munsell pages (Q12), the area classes and field codes, the carbonate of
the rock (Q15), the clay differences of the Bt and the Fahlerde. The
numbers are in `inst/rules/ka5/thresholds.yaml` with their pages;
soilKey’s new readings, for Hugo to confirm, in `readings.yaml`. Every
classification is unchanged.

- After the review (Hugo, 2026-11-06): a recorded water table makes a
  horizon G only within its fluctuation zone; a notation C or H without
  its prefix takes it from the data or leaves it open; the Ael without
  colour is undecided against the Al; no topsoil under 30 cm of peat;
  the Srd and Srw conventions and the F colour cuts (a lower grade)
  recorded.

## soilKey 0.9.360 (2026-11-05)

### Germany (KA5, 2005): the horizon notation and the formulas

The first piece of the German soil systematics of the Bodenkundliche
Kartieranleitung, 5th edition (Ad-hoc-AG Boden 2005), used by nothing
yet: the notation reader, its catalogue, the formula dialect of the
types and subtypes, and the new attributes. Every classification is
unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

- **The catalogue** `inst/rules/ka5/horizons.yaml`: the 15 masters, 23
  prefixes, the suffixes with their meaning by host (a, f, k, m, t, v,
  w), the base-saturation marks, the joiners, Tab. 12 of the permitted
  combinations, the 166 symbols 5.6.3.3 defines (checked on the page
  images) and the transitions it names, the KA6 symbols with a
  one-to-one reading, the field codes that are not horizons and the
  collisions with the other notations.
- **The reader** (`R/designation-ka5.R`): the last part carries the
  horizon (Ah-Bv is a Bv, fAh°Sd an Sd in a buried Ah), lower case
  before the master is a prefix and after it a suffix, Roman numerals,
  sub-horizon digits, letters in parentheses as sets of readings
  (B(h)s), the typing slips IC, AI and the degree sign typed o. A
  profile is in the KA5 notation when declared (ka5, ka4, ka3,
  kartieranleitung, bodensystematik, agboden, dbg; ka6 through its
  one-to-one symbols) or recognised by one strong sign or two likely
  ones, with no symbol only the FAO, USDA, Canadian, RP, CPCS or Russian
  notation writes; a mixed profile is undecided; never by the country
  (Hugo’s decisions Q2, Q3, Q4, Q8).
- **The formulas** of Liste 31 and of the 223 subtypes
  (`.ka5_parse_formula()`) read into the sequence engine’s formula
  object, with no unknown token; the strings, transcribed from the page
  images, are in `tests/testthat/fixtures/ka5-formulas.tsv`.
- **New attributes** (Hugo’s decision Q24): 26 horizon columns
  (`bleached_pct`, `reduction_colours_pct`, `rh_value`,
  `air_capacity_pct`, `total_porosity_pct`, `sand_ffs_pct`,
  `carbonate_whole_soil_pct`, the KA5 field codes `humus_class_ka5`,
  `carbonate_class_ka5`, `texture_class_ka5`, `colour_ka5`,
  `hydromorphic_features_ka5` …) and 13 site properties
  (`particle_size_scheme`, `embanked`, the groundwater levels of Tab.
  59, `reductgas_source`, `deep_cultivation_kind` …); the field codes
  are read into them by their class ranges.
- **Matching a profile to a formula** (`.ka5_horizon_frame()`): the last
  part carries the horizon and the whole symbol is the engine’s token,
  so Bv-Ah over Ah stays two horizons; Ap takes a plain Ah; the buried
  soil of `II...` runs from the first fossil row of a layer II; a
  geogenic prefix written in front (a, tb, tm, tp, e, z, s, q, o) holds
  for the whole horizon, f and r only for their part. Before the engine
  reads the table, a KA5 formula’s own hook (`prepare_table`, which no
  other system carries) lets a master written without suffix (C, G,
  aG, O) or a slot with commas take a run of rows (Ah/Bv/Cv/Cn is
  Ah/Bv/C, p. 199), and merges a transitional row into its neighbour
  with the same carrying code unless the formula names the transition
  (Al+Bt into the Bt, Go-Bv into the Bv).
- Hugo’s decisions on soilKey’s readings and on the review (2026-11-04)
  are in `inst/rules/ka5/readings.yaml`: the strong signs exactly as his
  card lists them (Btv is none); the Canadian j forms (Btj, Aej) and Ck
  and Oe written as designations veto the KA5; IIIC is II and lC with no
  layer II above it; the degree sign typed o only in a KA5 profile.

## soilKey 0.9.359 (2026-11-06)

### South Africa 1991: the families

[`classify_za1991()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_za1991.md)
now keys the second and last level of the South African soil
classification of 1991: the 404 families of the 73 forms, by the 19
family criteria. The name follows the identification of the book (Q23):
the form, the family code and name, and the USDA texture class of the A
when its clay, silt and sand are recorded
(`"Hutton, Hu1200 Kelvin, sandy loam"`; the sand grade with
`sand_grade`). Every other classification is unchanged (the fixtures of
the other systems byte-identical).

- **The families** (`inst/rules/za1991/families.yaml`, written by
  `data-raw/za1991_families.R`): codes of the form and the four printed
  digits, names as printed, the slips of the key pages read as in the
  plan (Plooysburg 1000 and 2000, the 1110 headers, the Shortlands 3000
  families on the B1, the signs of wetness of the soft carbonate
  horizon). The first family whose classes all hold is the family; a
  criterion undecided for lack of data leaves the result provisional,
  with the families still possible and soilKey’s partial code, an x for
  each undecided digit (`"Hutton, [Hux200]"`).
- **The 19 criteria** (`R/families-za.R`), each read once on the horizon
  its family names, as the form key identified it (the B1 of Q20, the A,
  the E, the upper G, the upper C, the layer under the placic pan or the
  podzol B, the profile within 1500 mm): the base status of the B1
  (S-value x 100 / clay %), the luvic B1 (Q21), hard lithocutanic B and
  saprolite (Q19), calcareous (Q22), the colours (Q9-Q12), podzolic
  character (Q13), the humic A, fibrous O, lamellae, structure, black
  cutans, ortstein, the consistence of the C and the material under
  the O. `qualifiers$za_family` lists every criterion read: its class,
  the layers, the stand-ins and the attributes missing.
- **Examples**: every form example holds the classes of its first
  family, and `make_za1991_example(form, family = "Hu1200")` gives a
  profile of any of the 404 families, by the data and by the notation.
- **Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-06)**, in `readings.yaml`: an
  organic O of unrecorded lower limit no longer stops the key; the
  absence of wetness or carbonates is undecided on a description that
  stops above 1500 mm or has nothing under the A; a pale soft carbonate
  horizon shows signs of wetness only by its mottles or a gley hue;
  hardness follows the USDA rupture resistance (dry hard, moist very
  firm, moderately cemented or more); the 500 mm under the organic O is
  the book’s (K 17); one pair of brackets around a partial code, and
  none when no class of a digit holds; a redder E is grey; Dundee reads
  its wetness from the alluvium down; a calcareous part anywhere in the
  B makes the calcareous Shortlands families; a fibrous O needs one run
  of 200 mm; the B1 is the upper layer of the first B; on a B of several
  colours FC 5 takes the larger share of dark or red; the other readings
  of this part confirmed.
- **A diagnostic horizon of several layers** on the data: the lower
  layers of a red structured B (and of a placic pan) under a layer of
  the same horizon were read as no horizon, and those of a lithocutanic
  B as saprolite; they are now read as the horizon, as the other B
  horizons, the E and the G already were (a layer under a lithocutanic B
  is saprolite only by its own rock).
- The criteria names in English and Portuguese, the families level in
  the app and the report.

## soilKey 0.9.358 (2026-11-05)

### South Africa 1991: the registry and the 73 soil forms

The South African soil classification of 1991 joins the registry as
`za1991` (aliases `za`, `sat`, `sat1991`, `south_africa`), experimental
and opt-in:
[`classify_za1991()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_za1991.md)
keys a profile to its soil form,
[`make_za1991_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_za1991_example.md)
gives one synthetic profile per form, and
`identify_horizons(pedon, "za1991")` reads every layer as one of the 30
diagnostic horizons and materials. Every other classification is
unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

- **The 73 forms** (`inst/rules/za1991/key.yaml`, written by
  `data-raw/za1991_key.R`) in the order of van Huyssteen (2020), each a
  sequence of diagnostic horizons and materials with the horizons that
  would make it another form (Q3: Hutton over hard rock is Hutton, over
  a soft plinthic B Bainsvlei); Lichtenburg keyed, always provisional
  (Q1); no form gives the nearest forms, an orthic A under 100 mm over
  nothing the land class rock and lithosols (Q2).
- **The general rules**: 1500 mm (Q7), a recent deposit over a buried
  soil (Q8), truncated profiles; a description stopping above 1500 mm
  leaves the longer forms undecided (Q4); the 500 mm rules of the form
  pages (Valsrivier, Sepane, Swartland, the podzol forms, Witbank,
  Dundee, Namib).
- **Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-06)**, in `readings.yaml`:
  the saprolite of Swartland, Houwhoek and Groenkop may lie within 500
  mm under the B, below unconsolidated material; the match is one pass
  over the horizons, however many are undecided; a topsoil of several
