  layers is a vertic, melanic or humic A when that covers half of it or
  its upper 200 mm, for every completion of its undecided layers; a
  topsoil over a recent deposit is part of the deposit; a red over a
  yellow-brown apedal layer is one horizon unless each is 20 cm or more;
  a B reaching 1500 mm reads the layer described below it; registry
  order 14.
- The form names and soilKey’s glosses in English and Portuguese, and
  the examples in the Pro app. The families follow in the next part.

## soilKey 0.9.357 (2026-11-05)

### South Africa 1991: the other horizons and materials on the data

The third part of the South African soil classification of 1991:
three-valued tests on the recorded data for the other seventeen
diagnostic horizons and materials, the position pass and the
identification of every layer (`R/diagnostics-za-horizons.R`). Nothing
is classified yet; every other classification is unchanged (the fixtures
of the other systems byte-identical).

- **The tests**: the E horizon (grey dry, eluvial), the podzol B and the
  placic pan, the soft and hard plinthic B, the soft and hardpan
  carbonate horizons, the dorbank, saprolite, hard rock, stratified
  alluvium, regic sand, the man-made soil deposit and the unconsolidated
  material; the podzol B, placic pan, dorbank and carbonate horizons by
  the WRB numbers standing in, flagged (Q13-Q16), in `thresholds.yaml`.
- **The position pass**: a grey low-chroma matrix is the G horizon under
  a topsoil or E, the unspecified material with signs of wetness under
  an apedal, neocutanic or neocarbonate B, the unconsolidated material
  with signs of wetness under a podzol or pedocutanic B; G or
  prismacutanic under an E by the 500 mm of K 19 and 27; lithocutanic B
  under the topsoil, saprolite under a B; the placic pan only under a
  podzol B; T-humic (iv) on the horizon identified below.
- **`.za_identify()`**, the identification of the registry namespace
  `za` for
  [`identify_horizons()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/identify_horizons.md)
  (registered with the system in the next part): the notation where a
  layer is named, else the data, with the stand-ins and fallbacks in the
  trace.
- **Decided by Hugo on the review (2026-11-06)** and recorded in
  `readings.yaml`: the B horizons by position (an apedal or structured B
  only under a topsoil, an E or the same B; under a podzol or
  pedocutanic B such a layer is unconsolidated material); the E with
  less clay than the layer below or at most 2 points over the one above,
  only under an orthic A or an E, and a grey eluvial layer never a G; a
  grey pedocutanic B is the G only with one more sign of wetness; a B1
  soft plinthic only with grey of its own or as many mottles as the
  layer below; organic carbon on the oxalate route of the podzol B;
  saprolite under the topsoil or an E is the lithocutanic B; a red or
  yellow apedal surface layer with under 0.3 % organic carbon over rock,
  a lithocutanic B or a dorbank is that B; a surface layer designated C
  is a topsoil.

## soilKey 0.9.356 (2026-11-05)

### South Africa 1991: the topsoils and the B horizons on the data

The second part of the South African soil classification of 1991:
three-valued tests on the recorded data for the five topsoil horizons
and the eight apedal and structured B horizons
(`R/diagnostics-za-horizons.R`). Nothing is classified yet; every other
classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems
byte-identical).

- **The topsoils** (organic O, vertic A, melanic A, humic A, orthic A),
  in that order (default 7): the organic O by 10 % organic carbon over
  200 mm and its saturation, recorded or by its evidence, flagged (Q18);
  vertic against melanic by the plasticity index, else the slickensides,
  flagged (Q17); humic against melanic by the 4 cmol(+) bases per kg
  clay per 1 % organic carbon; the humic A tested twice, the second time
  on the layer below it, and orthic when that fails.
- **The B horizons**: red apedal, yellow-brown apedal, red structured,
  neocutanic, neocarbonate, pedocutanic, prismacutanic (the clay rule of
  S 32, 20 % exactly by the +20 rule, Q21) and lithocutanic B, with the
  CEC under 11 cmol(+)/kg soil only for a borderline structure
  (default 16) and calcareous by effervescence or CaCO3 (Q22).
- **The colours** of Hugo’s decisions Q9-Q12: grey dry, yellow-brown,
  red (moist hue, the dry one flagged) and low chroma.
- **`inst/rules/za1991/thresholds.yaml`**: every number with its source
  and a `stand_in` flag; the WRB and soilKey stand-ins are flagged in
  every answer that reads them (“stand_in:”), so the book’s numbers can
  replace them without a change to the code. The readings of this part
  were decided by Hugo on its review (2026-11-05), with his amendments:
  low chroma outside the gley hues only at a moist value of 4 or more,
  10Y a gley hue; red not grey (5YR 6/1 is not red); with no dry colour,
  a moist chroma of 4 or more is not grey; an A2 under an A1 is a
  candidate E; a borderline grade (weak to moderate) is apedal under 11
  cmol(+)/kg soil and moderate at 11 or more; no B horizon on rock; the
  uniform dark brown weak B is neocutanic; red structured and red
  pedocutanic stay candidates together when the transition is not
  recorded; a calcareous stratified layer stays the material (Q6).
  `readings.yaml` records them.

## soilKey 0.9.355 (2026-11-05)

### South Africa 1991: the diagnostic horizons and their names

The first part of the South African soil classification of 1991 (Soil
Classification Working Group, 1991; the “Blue Book”, read from its open
pages, SASRI 1999 and van Huyssteen 2020, without the book): the
catalogue of its 30 diagnostic horizons and materials, the reader of
their names, and the attributes the later parts read. Nothing is
classified yet; every other classification is unchanged (the fixtures of
the other systems byte-identical).

- **The catalogue** (`inst/rules/za1991/horizons.yaml`): the 5 topsoil
  horizons (organic O, humic A, vertic A, melanic A, orthic A) and the
  25 subsoil horizons and materials, each with its printed name,
  soilKey’s English gloss, a token in capitals (OA, RAB, SPL …), what
  the preface says of it in 1977, and its pages; the names of 1977 the
  preface changed; the other words for the hard and carbonate horizons
  (calcrete, ferricrete, ouklip, silcrete); the hints of the FAO
  letters.
- **The reader** (`R/designation-za.R`; Hugo’s decision Q5). A new
  horizon attribute `diagnostic_za` holds the name as surveys write it
  (“red apedal B”, “Soft plinthic B horizon”, “B2 soft carbonate”,
  “none”), in any case and with or without “horizon”, or soilKey’s token
  (RAB); E and G alone are the E and G horizons. A 1977 name is read as
  its 1991 equivalent, flagged (ferrihumic B: podzol B; gleycutanic B: G
  horizon or unspecified material with signs of wetness by the horizon
  above; calcareous apedal or neocutanic B: neocarbonate B). A negated
  name (not red apedal B, E horizon absent) is not read; a
  non-diagnostic one (saprolite (non-diagnostic)) records no diagnostic
  horizon; one written with doubt (E?, possibly red apedal B) stays a
  candidate; calcrete is read by its adjective. The same names written
  inside `designation` (“Ap orthic A”, “B1 red apedal”) are read when
  `site$designation_system` declares the notation (`za`, `za1991`,
  `sat`, `sat1991`, `south africa` …; `SA` and `RSA` declare nothing),
  when the profile records a name in `diagnostic_za`, or when a
  designation holds a name only this system writes; never from the
  country, never when the site declares another notation. FAO and USDA
  letters are hints only (Bt: pedocutanic, prismacutanic, red structured
  or neocutanic B; Cr: saprolite, the wet materials, G or lithocutanic
  B); a word (Clay, Hutton) gives none.
- **New attributes**: on the horizons `diagnostic_za`,
  `plasticity_index`, `liquid_limit_method`, `bedrock_pct`,
  `coatings_hue_moist`, `coatings_chroma_moist`, `coatings_continuity`,
  `recent_deposit`, `cross_bedding` and `sand_grade`; on the site
  `reference_za_form`, `reference_za_family`, `reference_za_raw` and
  `reference_za_edition` (benchmarks only).

#### Readings decided on the review (2026-11-04)

Hugo decided the nine readings of this part with the fixes of its
review: soilKey’s two-letter short forms (ot, re, ye …) are not read
until checked on a survey sheet; calcrete by its adjective (alone
undecided between the soft and the hardpan carbonate horizon); Cr hints
at the saprolite, the wet materials, the G horizon and the lithocutanic
B; the other six (recognition by name, the gleycutanic B by position,
Afrikaans names, words of no diagnostic horizon, the master letter, the
declared values) as recommended. `inst/rules/za1991/readings.yaml`
records them with the four decisions of 2026-11-04 this part applies.

## soilKey 0.9.354 (2026-11-04)

### France: the correspondence tables of the Référentiel pédologique 2008

The annexes of the RP 2008 that correlate it with other systems, and the
labels of the RP of 1995, are shipped as data (Hugo’s decision Q1):
codes and names as the book prints them, with the page, its doubts (“?”)
kept as a flag and its slips noted; no sentence of the book. They are
notes for display and benchmarks: no classifier reads them, and every
classification is unchanged (the fixtures of all systems
byte-identical).

- **Annex 5, the WRB 2006** (pp. 378-392;
  `inst/rules/rp2008/crosswalk_wrb2006.yaml`). The 110 references with
  their WRB 2006 name (the brunisols eutriques in two rows by their
  saturation, the lithosols stricts in a row of their own), the 12
  reference horizons beside a WRB 2006 diagnostic horizon or FAO letter,
  the qualifiers (65 rows for the 64 of the book: the row of the calcium
  chapter, p. 380, holds for that chapter only) and the 15 “faux amis”.
  The WRB is the 2006 edition the book cites, not soilKey’s WRB 2022.
- **Annex 6, the CPCS 1967 horizons** (p. 393;
  `crosswalk_cpcs_horizons.yaml`). The table row for row, exported as
  data; the notation reader keeps its own copy in `horizons.yaml` for
  the hints of Q9, and a test keeps the two equal. BTfe, FSj and the Ha
  under the A1 are flagged as slips.
- **Annex 7, the CPCS 1967 categories** (pp. 394-398;
  `crosswalk_cpcs_classes.yaml`). Each row keyed by the `cpcs1967` code
  of its category (class, subclass, group or subgroup), its RP entries
  resolved to reference codes or groups, with their qualifiers, the
  double attachments and the “???” of the categories with no equivalent;
  the 14 categories the book calls new.
- **The labels of the RP 1995** (p. VII; `legacy_rp1995.yaml`). The 13
  references removed in 2008 and the names of 2008 the book gives for
  such solums.
- [`rp2008_crosswalk()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/rp2008_crosswalk.md)
  returns each table as a data frame;
  [`rp2008_from_label()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/rp2008_from_label.md)
  reads labels of French datasets (a reference, a type, a double, a
  label of 1995) as the references of 2008, for benchmarks.
- The report and the Pro app show the WRB 2006 names of the references
  of an RP result (Annex 5) and the RP equivalents of a CPCS result
  (Annex 7), as notes.

#### Readings confirmed (2026-11-04)

Hugo confirmed the readings of this release, with the points of its
review: all the tables of Annex 5 shipped; the table of Annex 6 as data
beside the reader’s copy, FE, OX and F of row B intertropical and BTfe,
FSj and the Ha under the A1 flagged as slips; a CPCS result shown the
row of the most specific category of its chain; the entries of Annex 7
that name no reference read through their chapter (fersialsols calcaires
and saturés as the carbonatés and calciques, luvisols-rédoxisols as the
double of any luvisol reference); the brunisols oligo-saturés read as
dystriques, the histosols recouverts and the humiferous andosols of 1995
as any reference of their group. Entries of `readings.yaml` record them.

## soilKey 0.9.353 (2026-11-04)

### France: the humus forms of the Référentiel pédologique 2008 (Annex 1)

The new
[`humus_form_rp()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/humus_form_rp.md)
attaches the épisolum of a profile to a humus form of Annex 1 of the RP
2008 (pp. 327-355), and
[`classify_rp2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_rp2008.md)
reports it beside the name: the new field `$humus_form` (one row: the
form, its name, type, group, the route, the candidates, the recorded
form and any conflict, the qualifiers) and `$trace$humus_form` (the
whole reading). The “à

” part of the name waits for the name builder of a later part, so the
name, the levels and the candidates of the references do not change.
Every other classification is unchanged (the fixtures of the other
systems byte-identical).

- **The order of the reading** (Hugo’s decision Q22;
  `inst/rules/rp2008/humus_forms.yaml`). H horizons at the top leave the
  épisolum to the histosols, with no form (p. 351); an OHta makes a
  tangel (p. 349) and an An as the first mineral horizon an anmoor
  (p. 351), the codes the references read (organosols à tangel,
  réductisols à anmoor); O horizons directly over an X, R or D give the
  forms without fine mineral earth, the type read on the O horizons
  alone (peyromull, lithomoder, peyromoder, lithomor, peyromor,
  peyro-amphimus; pp. 348-349); the land use or a ploughed L gives the
  open-land forms (agri-mull, mull de pelouse, agri-moder, moder de
  pelouse, agri-mor, mor de pelouse, amphimus de pelouse; p. 337); then
  the key of Figure 2 (p. 354), walked by `.walk_key()` on the O and A
  horizons to its eleven outcomes (eumull, mésomull, oligomull, dysmull,
  hémimoder, eumoder, dysmoder, hémimor, humimor, mor, euamphimus); a G,
  AG or g under the O horizons makes the outcome hydromorphic
  (hydromull, hydromoder, hydromor; p. 350).
- **Three-valued.** The key reads the kind of the O horizons (the
  notation, or `fine_organic_matter_pct`), their zoogenic character (zo,
  noz, or `o_zoogenic`), their lateral cover (`lateral_cover_pct`, 90 %
  or more continuous, or the parentheses of the RP notation: an O
  horizon written in parentheses is now read as that horizon,
  discontinuous, p. 340), the thickness of the OH and the biological
  structure of the A. What is not recorded leaves the form undecided
  among its candidates (when they share a type, the type is decided);
  with no O horizon recorded the form is undecided.
- **The recorded form** (Q22). A recorded `site$humus_form` (the forms
  and types of the annex, accents and case free) decides when the
  horizons leave the form undecided, a type keeping the candidates of
  that type; outside the forms the horizons leave possible it still
  decides, and the conflict is reported; when the horizons decide
  another form they prevail, the conflict reported. The schema lists the
  four forms de pelouse.
- **The qualifiers of the humus forms** (pp. 338-340), read on the first
  A: the pH and S/CEC classes (half-open, a neighbouring class within
  the tolerance of p. 64 listed as imperfect), carbonatée, the Ca/Mg
  classes on a saturated or subsaturated non-carbonated A
  (hyper-magnésique under 1/3), sodisée, lignique and xylique by the
  woody debris of the O horizons. They are listed beside the form, not
  yet in the name.
- [`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html) of a result of the RP
  shows the humus form, and
  [`key_trace_table()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/key_trace_table.md)
  gives it one row of information.
- **An O horizon written in parentheses** (“(OLn)”, “(OHzo)”:
  discontinuous, p. 340) was an unread designation; it is now read as
  its code. This also reaches the references: such a profile is now
  recognised as written in the RP notation, and an “(OLn)” litter is
  left out of the depths as an OLn is (p. 64), so “(OLn)/A/R” with the R
  at 12 cm is a lithosol, as “OLn/A/R” was, instead of “\[non
  rattaché\]”. Other designations in parentheses, as the “(B)” of the
  CPCS, are read as before.

#### Readings confirmed, and the review (2026-11-04)

Hugo confirmed the eight readings of this release (the order of the
reading, no O horizon recorded, the continuity of the O horizons, the
wet épisolum, the open land, the forms without fine earth, the recorded
form, the qualifiers). An independent review then found the key itself
right and fourteen defects around it, all fixed: a form is no longer
decided when the horizons may also fit no form (a dead end of the key, a
gate with no form after an undecided one, a top layer that may be an H),
the new `no_form_possible` saying so; the recorded form no longer stands
in for the biological structure of the A inside the key; the wet test
reads the layer under the organo-mineral one for a mor only; the forms
without fine earth keep every type an undecided OH or an undecided R, D
or X leaves possible; the amphimus de pelouse needs an OHzo; the land
uses are read as whole words, the present use first (a cleared forest
now grazed is grassland); a qualifier that needs a non-carbonated A is
undecided while the carbonates are; the continuity of an O of open kind
is undecided. Hugo decided its four open points: a continuous OLn gives
a mésomull as the key does, with a note on the early-winter eumull
(p. 342); only continuous OH horizons count toward the 1 cm of the
dysmoder (p. 344); the label of a decided type is the name of the type;
`woody_fragments_pct` stands in for the woody debris, flagged. Twelve
entries of `readings.yaml` record them.

## soilKey 0.9.352 (2026-11-04)

### France: the Référentiel pédologique 2008 attaches its last 18 references

[`classify_rp2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_rp2008.md)
now tests the 110 references of the 34 groups of references (GER): the
ninety-two of 0.9.346 to 0.9.351 and the six chapters that close the
book, pp. 291-326: régosols (1), salisols et sodisols (7), thalassosols
(3), thiosols et sulfatosols (2), veracrisols (1) and vertisols (4), in
`inst/rules/rp2008/references/<ger>.yaml`. They are plugged into the
attachment of 0.9.346 as parts 5 to 7 were; their signposts leave
`key.yaml`, which no longer holds any, and no double or precedence waits
for a later release. Every other classification is unchanged (the
fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

- **Régosols** (pp. 291-293). Within 10 cm (+/- 5; the OL not counted)
  an M or D layer or a C horizon under one organo-mineral or holorganic
  horizon at most, the holorganic O counting as one, read as the
  lithosols are (`lithic_obstacle_rp(window = TRUE)`: an undecided layer
  deeper than the window is no obstacle); the hardness from the horizon
  frame (the notation, the rupture resistance, soilKey’s
  [`continuous_rock()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/continuous_rock.md);
  not recorded, undecided). H of 10 cm or less over M, D or C is the
  régosol épihistique (p. 209); the young alluvial and marine deposits,
  the fluviosols bruts and juvéniles and the thalassosols bruts and
  juvéniles, take the name before it (p. 291), and an A over 10 cm makes
  the arénosol (pp. 101, 292).
- **Salisols et sodisols** (pp. 294-302). The salic horizon within 60 cm
  (+/- 10), chloruro-sulfatés in the neutral series and carbonatés in
  the alkaline one (`salic_series_rp()`: the anions of the salts, else
  the pH in water standing in for the paste extract, Q12); the sodic
  horizon within 60 cm with no salic one: indifférenciés with no E and
  no BT, solonetziques an E over the NaBT, solodisés an Ea or an E at pH
  5 or less (+/- 0.2) over it; the sodisalisols and salisodisols by the
  order of the two horizons (`superposed_rp()`). A code written with its
  Na or Sa (NaBT, SaA) needs the overlay. With a G or g within 50 cm the
  doubles with the réductisols and rédoxisols (pp. 298-299); too sandy
  for a paste, an arénosol salin (exclusions).
- **Thalassosols** (pp. 303-306). A marine or fluvio-marine material
  recorded (`marine_rp()`, Q14; such a material is no longer an alluvium
  of the fluviosols), the closed list of horizons of p. 304, no TH, U,
  salic or sodic horizon within 60 cm; bruts, juvéniles and poldérisés
  by the horizons, the site confirming (`tidal_site_rp()`: a polder
  fails the bruts and juvéniles, a tidal flooding the poldérisés,
  `artificially_drained` stands in for `poldered`; not recorded,
  provisional). A G within 50 cm makes the double
  réductisol-thalassosol, a g the rédoxisol-thalassosol poldérisé
  (pp. 285, 305; Q8).
- **Thiosols et sulfatosols** (pp. 307-312). A TH within 50 cm (+/- 10)
  and no U, its consistency n over 1.4 and its pH after drying under 3.5
  tested when recorded (`maturation_rp()`, `acidification_rp()`); a U
  within 50 cm with a TH directly under it (`sulfidic_under_rp()`) and n
  under 1.4. Sulfur at a shallow depth attaches the solum first to them,
  in every case (p. 310): a salisol with their characters is a
  sulfatosol or thiosol salique.
- **Veracrisols** (pp. 313-316). The vermihumic Ah (`vermihumic_rp()`):
  written Ah, or the dark A layers of the surface run on the data (moist
  value 3 or less, chroma 2 or less), biomacrostructured; under heath
  over 50 cm (+/- 10), S/CEC under 30 % and Al/S over 1; under culture
  an Ah under the LAh or LA with its base deeper than 50 cm; Ah of 30 to
  50 cm the veracrisol leptique, imperfect (p. 315); with an alocrisol
  humique the double of p. 316. The climate is reported, not tested.
- **Vertisols** (pp. 317-326). An SV over a V starting within 100 cm
  (strict), 40 % clay or more in every SV and V, smectitic when the
  mineralogy is recorded; in the order of Q20 the paravertisols
  planosoliques (an E or Eg directly over the SV, abruptly bounded),
  hapliques (an A under 40 % clay directly over the SV), then the litho-
  and topovertisols with a vertic surface (`vertic_surface_rp()`: on the
  data the characters of the Av read on the surface A), told apart by
  the site, else by the SV (`vertisol_site_rp()`). The vertisols take
  the name before a salisol or sodisol (VSa, VNa) and a planosol; the
  doubles with the réductisols and rédoxisols of p. 325 are written.
- **The rows that waited** (pp. 253, 282, 285): the peyrosols over 50 cm
  and a G within 50 cm now rank before the régosols, salisols, sodisols,
  thalassosols, veracrisols and vertisols as before every other
  reference, the thiosols and sulfatosols kept first; with E, BT, BP or
  Sp beside the redox features the other reference takes the name before
  the rédoxisol, the doubles still written.
- [`make_rp2008_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_rp2008_example.md)
  gives the 18 new profiles (the chalk of Champagne, a sebkha of
  Tunisia, the natron of the Kanem, the puszta, the prairies of Alberta
  and the Riverina, the bay of the Mont-Saint-Michel and the Marais
  poitevin, the mangroves of the Casamance, the touyas of Béarn, the
  marls of the Gâtinais, the basalts of Uruguay and the clay plains of
  the north of Cameroon), and the Pro app offers them. Each of the 110
  examples attaches simply to its own reference, and the test of this
  part keeps every candidate of each as a snapshot.

#### The review, and the readings confirmed (2026-11-04)

Hugo confirmed the eleven readings of this part as recommended, amended
by his decisions on its independent review, and the defects it found are
fixed:

- **VSa and VNa** are the salic and sodic horizons too (the overlay
  beside the feature; on the data a V with Na over 15 % of the CEC is a
  VNa), so the salisols and sodisols are among the candidates of such a
  vertisol (Q20). A written A, LA or SaA over the SV reads its vertic
  characters on the data, undecided when they are not recorded; a dark,
  humic SV under the A run stays an SV candidate; a written SV or V
  carries its clay, tested only when recorded (decision 7).
- **The sodic horizon** known by its ESP only (the Na derived with the
  CEC, or an ESP of 15 % or more as evidence) counts a massive
  structure. The solodisés need an Ea written, or an E at pH 5 or less
  (`solodic_e_rp()`: a written E with no pH is none, on the data
  undecided); an A directly on the NaBT is the sodisol solonetzique
  imperfect, and a sodic BT names the sodisol before a luvisol; the
  indifférenciés need no E or BT within 60 cm.
- **The régosols** count adjacent layers of one code as one horizon
  (A1/A2; the lithosols too) and exclude a recorded recent alluvium
  (`alluvial_rp()`).
- **The thalassosols** forbid R, D, X and Z only within the solum (100
  cm); a polder, reclaimed, embanked or former tidal land is read before
  the tidal words, and the marine words are read as words (not
  submarine, not non-tidal). A provisional thalassosol or vertisol says
  why.
- **The veracrisols** whose description ends in the Ah are undecided; a
  vermihumic Ah of 30 cm or more names the veracrisol before a luvisol
  tronqué (decision 1).
- **Hugo’s decisions**: an unsaturated SV makes the lithovertisol even
  in a low position, and with no site recorded the litho- or
  topovertisol is provisional (2); a U with no TH under it is the
  sulfatosol imperfect, before the réductisol (3); only the réductisols
  typiques make the double with the thalassosols (4); the salsodic
  doubles need a réductisol that holds strictly (5); the thiosols and
  sulfatosols come before the peyrosols (6). Seven entries of
  `readings.yaml` record them.
- The example fluviosol brut no longer lists the régosol among its
  candidates (the snapshot of the test updated).

## soilKey 0.9.351 (2026-11-04)

### France: the Référentiel pédologique 2008 attaches 21 more references

[`classify_rp2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_rp2008.md)
now tests the 92 references of twenty-eight groups of references (GER):
the twenty-one of 0.9.346 to 0.9.349 and the seven chapters that follow
in the book, pp. 243-290: pélosols (3), peyrosols (1), phæosols (2),
planosols (3), podzosols (8), rankosols (1) and réductisols et
rédoxisols (3), in `inst/rules/rp2008/references/<ger>.yaml`. They are
plugged into the attachment of 0.9.346 as parts 5 and 6 were; their
signposts leave `key.yaml`. The 18 references of the other 6 GER
(régosols, salisols et sodisols, thalassosols, thiosols et sulfatosols,
veracrisols, vertisols) come later. Every other classification is
unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

- **Pélosols** (pp. 243-248). The Sp over 30 cm (+/- 5), starting within
  40 cm for the three references (D6, strict), never acid: a pH in water
  of 5.0 or more (+/- 0.2) in every Sp layer (D5); no V or SV. Typiques
  the Sp under the A or ploughed at the surface, brunifiés under a thin
  S, différenciés under an Ae and E or an LE under 30 % clay and 30 cm
  thick at most (else a planosol). On the data a prismatic
  over-structure alone, with no slickensides or wedge-shaped aggregates,
  over a layer that meets the Sp is the Sp, not an SV. A pélosol typique
  with redox features from under 50 cm is the double pélosol
  typique-rédoxisol of p. 285; a différencié includes them, no double.
- **Peyrosols** (pp. 249-254). Peyric horizons from the surface over
  more than 50 cm (+/- 10), or 10 to 50 cm directly on M, R or D
  (leptique) (`peyric_rp()`): an X (by weight, Q11), or a horizon of the
  notation with its coarse elements recorded over 60 % by weight. Over
  50 cm the peyrosol takes the name whatever the context (p. 253), in
  the doubles the book names: an alocrisol typique, the anthroposols
  artificiels and reconstitués, the andosols, a colluviosol, a fluviosol
  brut, the podzosols (the peyrosol-podzosol meuble of p. 252), the
  fersialsols, the réductisols, a rankosol. A peyric X of the data whose
  fine earth holds an E, BP, FS or G serves those horizons’ tests in the
  run from the surface.
- **Phæosols** (pp. 255-258). An Aso of 30 cm or more (D8), its S/CEC 50
  to 80 % under permanent vegetation read on its layers (over 80
  undecided against the chernosols, D9; under 50 the phæosol dystrique,
  imperfect), over an Sh or BTh: written with h, or on the data over 0.6
  % organic carbon and over 80 % S/CEC (`humic_under_rp()`); an E under
  5 cm only, no Km. Hapliques with an index under 1.3, mélanoluviques
  1.3 to 3 (gradual) or 1.3 to 2 (abrupt), read against the adjacent Sh
  or BTh only (`idt_rp(adjacent = TRUE)`). With an Aso of 30 cm or more
  the phæosol, dystrique or within the tolerance, takes the name before
  a brunisol. The climate is reported, not tested (D10); the solums the
  book places in no reference (an Aso over an E of 5 to 15 cm over a BT;
  an index of 2 to 3 with an abrupt transition) are reported in
  `$trace$book_gaps`.
- **Planosols** (pp. 259-264). The four characters of the textural
  planosols (`planosol_rp()`): a clay difference of 20 points (D1), the
  least clayey E 30 % at most, the most clayey horizon 25 % at least,
  the abrupt change within 8 cm (under 20 % more than the double, from
  20 % 20 points more, D2) on the lower boundary of the E, a
  subhorizontal contact; the Eg, \[Ae + E + Eg\] of 15 cm, the floor
  within 120 cm, no Eg on a BP. Typiques the Eg within 50 cm, distaux at
  50 cm or deeper (D4), structuraux over a compacted or indurated floor;
  the truncated typiques of p. 263 imperfect, tronqué (D3). They take
  the name before the rédoxisols (no double, p. 263) and before very
  planosolic luvisols dégradés or derniques (p. 227); the pélosols
  différenciés before them (p. 244).
- **Podzosols** (pp. 265-275). The BP of the frame directly under some E
  or the A (`below_rp(layer = "any")`: the matcher reads a slot as a run
  of one code), cemented (written with c, recorded, or an m of another
  notation on the data, Bhsm) or loose (`cemented_rp()`), the humus no
  mull (`podzolic_humus_rp()`: an A at pH 5.0 or more with no O recorded
  leaves it undecided), the placic Femp directly above or inside the BP
  (`placic_rp()`); ocriques (no E; a mor directly on the BP imperfect,
  as an A over a cemented BP), meubles and duriques (E), humiques and
  humo-duriques (Eh), éluviques (an E on C or R, the BP downslope
  recorded, `lateral_bp_downslope`, Q14: else a candidate), placiques,
  post-podzosols (a ploughed layer on the BP, or LE/E/BP; on the data
  L/E/BP undecided), in soilKey’s order of D11. E and BP over 10 cm
  under an Aho make any podzosol, the organosol a candidate (p. 241).
- **Rankosols** (pp. 276-278). (O)/A/R: \[O+A\] over 10 and under 35 cm
  on a non-carbonated R, no C, M or D, coarse elements over 25 % and
  under 60 % by weight in the A (`coarse_band_rp()`; not recorded, the
  rankosol undecided), organic carbon under 8 % (+/- 2), nothing
  calcareous, calcic or magnesic, no E, BT, S or g over 5 cm, a Sal
  under 10 cm (p. 73), a BP under 10 cm: 5 cm or less the rankosol, over
  5 the double rankosol-podzosol ocrique (D14); 60 % or more the double
  rankosol-peyrosol of p. 277 (D15).
- **Réductisols et rédoxisols** (pp. 279-290). Functional reductic or
  redox features (g over 5 %, Q17; a relict one recorded is not
  functional, Q13; a drained site keeps the attachment) starting within
  50 cm and continuing over 50 cm (`hydromorphy_rp()`); a G within 50 cm
  makes a réductisol whatever lies above (default 20); stagnique with an
  R or M under the G or a perched water table recorded, typique with the
  G to the base or with a C or D under it and a phreatic water table
  recorded (`reductic_base_rp()`); the redox g or -g alone a rédoxisol.
  The depth class of the hydromorphy is in `$trace$hydromorphy`.
- **The hydromorphic doubles** that earlier parts waited for are written
  (Q8, Q13): luvisol typique, dégradé or dernique-rédoxisol
  (pp. 226-230, 285), brunisol-rédoxisol with an aerated S over the Sg
  (p. 107), colluviosol-rédoxisol from 20 to 50 cm (p. 133), cryosol
  minéral-rédoxisol and -podzosol (pp. 141-142), the podzosols with the
  rédoxisols and réductisols (pp. 273, 285); a double with the rédoxisol
  only when it holds strictly. H over 50 cm over a G is the histosol,
  the réductisol a candidate (no double, the histosols réductiques of
  p. 209). In alluvium the rédoxisol fluvique takes the name and the
  double fluviosol-rédoxisol stays among the candidates
  (`status: candidate`, marked `double_possible`). The pairs with the
  thalassosols wait for them.
- [`make_rp2008_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_rp2008_example.md)
  gives the 21 new profiles (the marls of Lorraine, a scree of the mont
  Ventoux, the loess of Uruguay, the Champagne humide, the Sologne and
  the boulbènes, the Vosges and the Landes, a granite of the Massif
  central, valley bottoms and a clayey colluvium), and the Pro app
  offers them.
- The precedence pairs and the doubles are read only among the
  references that may attach, and the order of the rapid key once per
  rules object: the 44 canonical fixtures classify as fast as with
  0.9.350, the results identical.

#### Readings confirmed, and the review (2026-11-04)

Hugo confirmed the twelve readings of this part, amended by his
decisions on its review: the 50 cm of hydromorphic features, the base of
the réductisols (and the substrate and water, decision 5), the doubles
the book names with the rédoxisols and réductisols, the aerated S of the
brunisol-rédoxisol, the doubles of the podzosols named by the GER, no
histosol-réductisol (decision 2), the 8 cm of the planosols, the
planosols tronqués, the pH and 40 cm of the pélosols, the humus and the
post-podzosols, the rankosols (decision 7), the Sh and BTh of the
phæosols. Nine entries record the decisions of the review.

## soilKey 0.9.350 (2026-11-04)

### France: the FE of the ferruginosols on the data

On the data route the FE horizon of the ferruginosols was read as a BT
whenever a clay increase over the A let soilKey’s
[`argic()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/argic.md)
stand in for clay films that were not recorded, so ferruginous tropical
profiles described without designations went to the fersialsols or the
luvisols. On the notation route nothing changes.

- **FE against BT** (pp. 17, 170-171). In the intertropical domain the
  illuviation cutans separate the zones of clay illuviation from those
  of weathering, and the A over an FE is depleted of clay by sheet
  runoff. Recorded clay films decide: common or many a BT, even in a
  ferruginous context, none or few no BT; a BT mark of another notation
  (Bt, B2t) keeps the BT. With the clay films not recorded, a layer that
  holds FE is no BT at 5YR or redder (outside the BT colours of the
  ferruginosols, 10YR to 7.5YR) and the fixed order goes on (an FE, or
  an F tested before it); it stays undecided between FE and BT at 7.5YR,
  when the FE holds only within the tolerance of p. 64, or when the FE
  itself is undecided. A layer under an FE is a BT by
  [`argic()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/argic.md)
  only with more clay than the FE directly above it: the BT is more
  clayey than the A, E, S or C of the solum (p. 17), and the increase of
  the FE over the depleted A is not its own (Hugo’s decision 4); the
  BTss reads the BT above it the same way. With the domain not recorded
  nothing changes.
- **FS against a kaolinitic clay** (pp. 150, 171, 179). In the domain a
  CEC of 16 cmol+/kg of clay or less, the upper bound of the ferrallitic
  F, is no FS when no clay mineralogy is recorded (a recorded smectite
  or other 2:1 clay keeps the FS): the BT under an FE stays the BT of
  the ferruginosols instead of an FSt.
- **The field route of the FS** (pp. 171, 179; Hugo’s decision 3,
  everywhere). With no FFE measured an FS needs an angular blocky (or
  cubic) structure: of strong grade it makes the FS, of moderate grade
  the FS imperfect (the fersialsol attaches as imperfect); a recorded
  subangular, prismatic, granular or massive structure, or a weak grade,
  is no FS by the field route, and the grade or the angularity not
  recorded leaves it undecided. With the FFE measured the structure is
  read as before.
- Outside the intertropical domain only the field route of the FS
  changes, and none of the probes of parts 4 to 6 moves. The four
  ferruginosol probes of part 6 now attach (meubles, semiluviques twice,
  luviques) and the book’s sequences of pp. 173-174 written as data
  attach to their references; the tropical fersialsols, luvisols and
  ferrallitisols of the twins keep theirs. Every other classification is
  unchanged (the fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

#### Readings confirmed (2026-11-04)

Hugo confirmed the two readings of this release with the amendments of
its review (the BT mark of another notation, the FE within the
tolerance, the clay mineralogy before the CEC), and decided the field
route of the FS and the clay increase of a BT under an FE; four entries
of `readings.yaml` record them.

## soilKey 0.9.349 (2026-11-04)

### France: the Référentiel pédologique 2008 attaches 18 more references

[`classify_rp2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_rp2008.md)
now tests the 71 references of twenty-one groups of references (GER):
the fifteen of 0.9.346 and 0.9.348 and the six chapters that follow in
the book, pp. 201-242: histosols (5), leptismectisols (1), lithosols
(1), luvisols (6), nitosols (1) and organosols (4), in
`inst/rules/rp2008/references/<ger>.yaml`. They are plugged into the
attachment of 0.9.346 (registry, precedence, doubles, rapid key) as part
5 was; their signposts leave `key.yaml`. The 39 references of the other
13 GER come later. Every other classification is unchanged (the fixtures
of the other systems byte-identical).

- **Histosols** (pp. 201-216). Almost only H horizons (Hf, Hm, Hs, Ha,
  LH), the first within 50 cm (a cover is the qualifier recouvert), and
  under them only G, M, D or R, or thin limnic and terric materials
  (`histic_solum_rp()`; a C read as the M). The predominant horizon is
  the thickest kind of H, thicknesses cumulated, between 40 and 120 cm,
  or 0 and 50 cm over an M, D or R within 50 cm; a tie is no kind truly
  predominant, the Ha and LH count for no kind (D3); the 60 cm of the
  fibriques and 40 of the mésiques and sapriques are the thickness of
  that kind in the solum (D1, `histic_kind_rp()`); over 50 cm of H by
  the figure of p. 209, the composites the remainder; the leptiques 10
  to 50 cm of H over M, D or R. H of 10 cm or less over R is a lithosol,
  over M, D or a C read as the M a régosol (a later release), under 50
  cm over G a réductisol (a later release), with a permafrost within 2 m
  a cryosol histique (p. 211; `precedence.yaml`). The kinds on the data
  by the rubbed fibres, then von Post (D4); H against O by the
  designation, then the water (Q19): an organic layer the data leave
  between the two leaves both GER undecided. The habitat notes are
  reported, not tested (D18).
- **Leptismectisols** (pp. 217-218). Av over SV, \[Av + SV\] 50 cm or
  less, no V, every horizon 40 % clay or more, the complex saturated
  over 90 % by Ca and Mg (+/- 5, default 9), over R, Kc, Km or C; the
  smectites tested only when the clay mineralogy is recorded
  (`clay_mineral_rp()`). With no V read the leptismectisol takes the
  name before the signpost of the vertisols.
- **Lithosols** (pp. 219-220). An R, Km, Fem or Sim at 10 cm or less (10
  to 15 cm imperfect), the OL not counted, or an OXc or OXm there in the
  intertropical domain (Q18), with at most one horizon over it, the
  holorganic O horizons counting as one (`lithic_obstacle_rp()`; Hugo’s
  decisions 1 and 2: A-Sal-R with the R at 12 cm is an alocrisol
  typique, imperfect). A cuirasse or carapace of the tropical chapters
  stays a ferrallitisol, oxydisol or ferruginosol only when an F, OX,
  ND, RT, FE, Ea or BT lies under it within 120 cm (`under_rp()`; the
  ferruginosol pétroxydique tronqué of p. 175); without them it is a
  lithosol pétroxydique or duroxydique (decision 3).
- **Luvisols** (pp. 221-232). The texture contrast
  (`luvic_contrast_rp()`): the band set by the mean clay of the E (with
  no E, the ploughed LA or LE), against the most clayey BT: néoluvisols
  from 3 points, an index of 1.3 or 9 points more, to under the
  typiques’ 8 points, index over 1.8 or 24 points (D11); in the band of
  10 to 30 % and for the derniques the index is the lexicon’s, the most
  clayey BT over the poorest E or Ae (p. 401; decision 4). When
  recorded, a BT of 5YR or redder or micro-polyhedral fails them
  (`siallitic_rp()`, p. 230; decision 6), and an h on the E or the BT
  bars them (p. 194; decision 7). Dégradés a BTd under the E; derniques
  an Ea directly on the BTd and the index over 1.8, named before the
  dégradés (D9); tronqués no E over 10 cm under forest, named before a
  typique or néoluvisol that also attaches (decision 8), an LBT or a
  ploughed horizon with no contrast left under crops (D12);
  quasi-luvisols an E over a II BT (`discontinuity_rp()`), the others
  read in the first material. The FFE over total iron of the BT over
  0.20, measured, fails them (p. 230; `iron_release_rp(low = TRUE)`).
  The grisols come before the néoluvisols and luvisols typiques
  (p. 194). The doubles with the rédoxisols wait for them (Q8); a
  cryoturbated luvisol with a permafrost is a luvisol-cryosol (p. 141).
- **Nitosols** (pp. 233-237). The nitic Sn, under an A or a ploughed
  horizon; on the data its halloysite recorded decides, else Ki and Kr,
  else soilKey’s
  [`nitic_horizon()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/nitic_horizon.md)
  stands in for the mineralogy as well, flagged (D14). The nitosol takes
  the name before the brunisols, whose S slot reads the Sn (p. 236), and
  yields to a ferrallitisol when an F lies with the Sn (the
  ferrallitisol meuble polylithique of p. 157). The chapter is a first
  version of the book (p. VI) and its climate is reported, not tested.
- **Organosols** (pp. 238-242). OF, OH, OHta and Aho over 10 cm (+/- 5),
  no H, thin organo-mineral horizons 10 cm or less in all and the
  organic ones at least twice as thick (`organic_dominance_rp()`); an S
  over 10 cm fails them, strict, and OF/OH over an S of 15 cm is a
  brunisol, imperfect, with no A (a new imperfect case of
  `brunisols.yaml`; decision 9). Holorganiques OF and/or OH and/or OHta
  and no A; calcaires an Acaho; saturés the Aho over 80 % S/CEC and
  insaturés under 80 % (no carbonated Acaho), the Aho read as a whole
  (p. 239), the insaturés with 20 cm of O and Aho from the surface and
  well drained to 50 cm. An S, an Sca or Sci or E and BP over 10 cm make
  a brunisol, calcosol or calcisol or podzosol humique; a Sal over 10 cm
  an alocrisol humique, under 10 an organosol insaturé, the other a
  candidate, and the double organosol insaturé-alocrisol humique only at
  10 cm (decision 5); an Acaho with OF and OH over 40 cm an organosol
  before a rendosol (p. 241).
- [`make_rp2008_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_rp2008_example.md)
  gives the 18 new profiles (peats of the Jura, the Beauce, the Causses,
  the loess of the Paris basin, Poland, Guadeloupe, the Jura and the
  Vosges), and the Pro app offers them.

#### Readings confirmed, and the review (2026-11-04)

Hugo confirmed the nine readings of this part, amended by his decisions
on its review: the lithosol obstacle at 10 cm or less, with one horizon
over it; the tropical references before the lithosols only with their
horizons under the cuirasse; the index of the lexicon in the middle band
and for the derniques; the BT of 5YR or redder or micro-polyhedral, and
an h on the E or the BT, barring the luvisols; the tronqués before the
typiques; an S over 10 cm under the O barring the organosols; the Sal of
the organosols and alocrisols humiques. Six entries record those
decisions. An unread mineral designation (ASa, SSa) is no longer read as
a possible organic horizon, and an O of undecided kind may be an OHta.

## soilKey 0.9.348 (2026-11-03)

### France: the Référentiel pédologique 2008 attaches 24 more references

[`classify_rp2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_rp2008.md)
now tests the 53 references of fifteen groups of references (GER): the
nine of 0.9.346 and the six chapters that follow in the book,
pp. 146-200: ferrallitisols et oxydisols (7), ferruginosols (4),
fersialsols (4), fluviosols (4), grisols (3) and gypsosols (2), in
`inst/rules/rp2008/references/<ger>.yaml`. They are plugged into the
attachment of 0.9.346 (registry, precedence, doubles, rapid key) without
changing it; their signposts leave `key.yaml`. The 57 references of the
other 19 GER come later. Every other classification is unchanged (the
fixtures of the other systems byte-identical).

- **Ferrallitisols et oxydisols** (pp. 146-168). Only in the
  intertropical domain (Q18, the new `tropical_rp()`: declared, a Köppen
  climate A or a latitude between the tropics; outside, they fail). The
  hardness precedence OXm \> OXc \> ND \> meuble sets the reference (D3,
  in `precedence.yaml` with its pages); the thicker loose horizon within
  120 cm, F or OX (their nodular forms included), makes a ferrallitisol
  or an oxydisol, neither a ferrallitisol (D4, `loose_rp()`); an OX with
  an OXc and no OXm is a ferrallitisol duroxydique, with an ND as well
  (A-OX-ND-OXc, the hardness precedence: Hugo’s decision R2), since the
  book has no oxydisol duroxydique (D5). No FE, E or BT (pp. 162-163).
  The proximal (0-60 cm, the chapter, Q17) and distal (80-120 cm) types
  are reported with the depth of the first ND, OXm or OXc in
  `trace$position` and the warnings; between 60 and 80 cm the reference
  stays, with no type (D2).
- **Ferruginosols** (pp. 169-177). Intertropical; an FE, or an E or BT
  under an OXm or an OXc (the pétroxydiques accept the OXc, D10, D11);
  the meubles without an S are the imperfect case of p. 173,
  “ferruginosol meuble sans horizon S”. The climate is reported, not
  tested.
- **Fersialsols** (pp. 178-182). An FS, its iron release read again at
  the reference (`iron_release_rp()`: FFE over total iron above 0.20
  when measured, the free iron as evidence, the field route otherwise,
  D14); carbonated over the larger part of the FS thickness
  (`carbonated_rp()`; a local effervescence is not carbonated), calcic
  (not effervescent but locally, S/CEC over 80 %, Ca/Mg over 5),
  unsaturated (S/T under 80 %) or eluvic (an E over an FSt, IDT over
  1.3). A saturated, non-effervescent FS with Ca/Mg 5 or less is a
  fersialsol calcique, imperfect, calcimagnésique or magnésique (D13);
  some FS carbonated but not the larger part, a calcique, imperfect,
  bathycarbonaté or recarbonaté (Hugo’s decision D3). On the data the t
  of an FS needs common or many clay films; an FSt with no E is an
  éluvique, imperfect, tronqué (IDT from the A over 1.3), or a calcique
  or insaturé, imperfect, luvique (R1).
- **Fluviosols** (pp. 183-191). The alluvial origin is required (Q14,
  `alluvial_rp()`); the position in the valley and the water table are
  read when recorded (`valley_position`, `flood_frequency`,
  `groundwater_kind`, `groundwater_depth_cm`): a terrace or an alluvial
  fan fail, and the water table only when the flooding and the
  groundwater are both recorded as none (an embanked valley, or “none
  observed” in the pit, leave it not recorded: Hugo’s decision D1); the
  French words lit mineur, lit majeur, terrasse, cône and marais are
  read, another position leaves it undecided; not recorded, the
  fluviosol attaches and is provisional, said in the warnings
  (`provisional_unless` in its file,
  “references:`” in ``provisional_because``). No E, BT, BP, sodic, salic, sulfated or thionic horizon, no G or H within 50 cm. A structureless surface layer (single grain, massive) is no Js (p. 25) but the raw alluvium of the bruts, with no Jp under it, which the data now reach; a C stands for the M of the typiques (A-Jp-C). A g within 50 cm keeps the fluviosol in the name, provisional by the rédoxisols of a later release (Q8; the doubles fluviosol-rédoxisol and peyrosol-fluviosol brut wait in ``doubles.yaml``). The bruts come before the régosols (p. 188), the colluviosols yield to them (p. 132), and they take the solum before the brunisols, calcosols, calcisols and arénosols by the rapid key (5a).`
- **Grisols** (pp. 192-195). The Aso by the chapter (Q17, D15,
  `sombric_rp()`): value under 4.5 and chroma under 4, 4/3 excluded, not
  calcareous, S/CEC 50-80 % and pH 5.5-6.5 under permanent vegetation,
  the general definition of p. 13 in the strict pass only (met by the
  chapter alone, imperfect); cultivated (an L or the land use) the
  complex is not tested (D19); a written Aso with no colour still reads
  its recorded S/CEC, pH and carbonates. On the data a layer that
  continues the A run and reads E is the Eh when it is lighter than the
  layers above and below, with less clay than below and a weak
  structure; otherwise it stays undecided, its h possible. Clinohumic,
  S/CEC under 95 % in the Eh, BTh and BThd (not in a deep non-humic BT),
  the texture differentiation index 1.3 itself hapliques (S19). Still in
  soilKey’s 7c (Q6), and before the chernosols and phaeosols (p. 194),
  so that the signpost of the phaeosols no longer makes a grisol
  provisional.
- **Gypsosols** (pp. 196-200). A Ys from the surface or under a Ym, its
  top within 10 +/- 5 cm (D18); a Yp makes no gypsosol (it gives “à
  horizon gypsique” to the other references, with the qualifiers).
- **The first version of the book.** The results of the ferrallitisols,
  oxydisols and ferruginosols say that the book calls these chapters a
  first version (p. VI, Q18; `first_draft` in `key.yaml`); `result_note`
  adds what a chapter reports without testing (the climates of the
  ferruginosols and gypsosols).
- [`make_rp2008_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_rp2008_example.md)
  gives the 24 new profiles (in Côte d’Ivoire, New Caledonia, Burkina
  Faso, Provence, the Loire valley, Romania and Tunisia), and the Pro
  app offers them.

#### Fixed

- **The parent material written last.** A last optional slot such as
  `(C|M|R)` now reads one optional slot per layer, the C, M and D in any
  order and the R last: the matcher reads a slot as a run of one code,
  so A-S-C-R was \[non rattaché\] in 0.9.346 and is now a brunisol,
  A-S-M-C too, Aca-Sca-C-R a calcosol.

- **The iron of the FS on the data** is read on one basis, the free iron
  as Fe against the total as Fe2O3 (Q23, as `fe_total_pct` documents
  it): FFE / (0.6994 x Fe2O3) above 0.20, free / (0.6994 x Fe2O3) above
  0.50.

- **Timing.** The sequences are matched on the table already read, the
  completions of the undecided layers stop at the first sign of
  disagreement, the strict and tolerant passes share one match when no
  layer is read within tolerance, and the memberships of the frame are
  memoised: the 44 canonical fixtures classify in about the time of
  0.9.346, every result unchanged.

#### Readings confirmed (2026-11-03)

Hugo confirmed the eight readings of `readings.yaml` for this part (the
intertropical domain of a profile written in the RP notation with no
climate or latitude; F against OX, the hardness and the types; the
sequences of the ferruginosols; the A, the FSt, the carbonates and the
iron of the fersialsols; the origin, the site and the sequences of the
fluviosols; the Aso, Eh, BTh, BThd and the index of the grisols; the
crust of the gypsosols; the parent material written last), those of the
fersialsols and fluviosols amended by his decisions D1, D2, D3 and R1,
and three entries record his decisions D3, R1 and R2.

## soilKey 0.9.347 (2026-11-03)

### Russia: the species, and the 1977 analogue as a note

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) now names its
soils down to the species (вид) of chapter 5.1, after the subtypes, and
gives the analogue of the type in the USSR classification of 1977
(chapter 6) as a note that never changes the classification (Hugo’s
decision Q1). The varieties and ranks of 5.2 and 5.3 are not keyed, and
a technogenic surface formation still stops at trunk E.

- **The twelve tables of 5.1** (pp. 135-137), in the new
  `inst/rules/kidpr2008/species.yaml`: the thickness of the grey-humus
  and light-humus horizons (маломощные, среднемощные, мощные) and of the
  dark-humus horizon (мелкие to сверхмощные), of the peat horizon of a
  mineral soil, of the agro horizon; the depth and place of gleying
  (глубоко-, поверхностно-, профильно-оглеенные); the lower boundary of
  the bleached horizon; the layer over the solonetzic horizon (корковые
  to глубокие); the depth of the carbonates (карбонатные to
  сильновыщелоченные) and of the soluble salts (солончаковые to
  глубокозасоленные); and, in the organogenic trunk, the decomposition
  of the peat, its botanical composition and the thickness of the peat
  body. Each table says what it measures, on which horizon, for which
  types, and its class limits as numbers.
- **The species level.** Every table that applies to the type is read;
  the class that holds is a row of level `species` of `levels` (code
  `<table>:<class>`, the English gloss in `name`, the Russian in
  `name_native`), named after the subtypes in the order of the tables:
  “Sod-podzolic \[typical\], medium-thick, deep-eluvial”,
  “Дерново-подзолистые \[типичные\], среднемощные, глубокоэлювиальные”.
  The bleached species takes the prefix form of p. 136 with the term of
  its horizon (мелкоподзолистые for the E of a podzol,
  глубокоэлювиальные for an EL, неглубокоосолоделые in the solods); two
  dominant plants give the double name of the peat (древесно-осоковые).
  `qualifiers$species` and `species_native` list them, and the trace has
  every table read (phase `species`) with its measure, layers and
  evidence.
- **Three-valued, as intervals.** A depth not recorded, a layer whose
  horizon the data leave undecided at the edge of a horizon, or a
  horizon that reaches the bottom of the description when a deeper class
  is possible, leaves the species undecided: it is not named, it is
  listed in `qualifiers$species_undecided` with a note, and the name is
  not made provisional. A value at a limit is read by the owner’s rule
  (the lower end of a range for a minimum, the upper end for a maximum).
- **The 1977 analogue** (pp. 139-161), in the new
  `inst/rules/kidpr2008/correlation_1977.yaml`: the 268 rows of the
  correlation table, each a 2004 type with its 2004 formula, the type of
  2008 it stands for, whether the soils were distinguished in 1977, and
  the 1977 units it names (their short printed names, level and extent:
  full, approximately, partly, mostly), with soilKey’s English
  paraphrase. 267 rows resolve to a type of 2008, each to a different
  one (one 2004 type has no type of 2008); 144 say the soils were not
  distinguished; eight types of 2008 have no row.
  [`classify_kidpr2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_kidpr2008.md)
  adds the analogue of the assigned type as a line in `warnings` and as
  `qualifiers$analogue_1977`; the note says so where the soils were not
  distinguished or chapter 6 has no row, and a soil whose type is
  unassigned, or a chemozem, gets none. The report and the Pro app show
  it.
- **Two formulas of chapter 6** that the text layer had hidden
  (AY-AEL-BM-C on p. 143, printed letter-spaced, and P-TUR-C on p. 156,
  printed on the line of its name) join the fixture of the formulas: 268
  rows of chapter 6, not 266.
- **A new horizon attribute**, `peat_botanical_composition` (the plants
  of the peat with their shares, in English or Russian), for the
  botanical species.
- [`classify_kidpr2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_kidpr2008.md)
  gains `species` (default: as `subtypes`); `subtypes = FALSE` still
  stops at the type. New i18n keys `classify.level_species`,
  `classify.levels_species`, `classify.kidpr_1977`,
  `report.level_species`, `report.kidpr_1977` and
  `report.kidpr_1977_desc` (EN, PT).
- The other systems are unchanged (their fixtures byte-identical).

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-03)

- **Gleying by its continuity:** surface-gleyed is gleying in the upper
  horizons (those starting above 50 cm) that does not continue below 50
  cm; profile-gleyed is gleying from a horizon starting above 50 cm down
  to the bottom, only a humus or agro horizon that is not gleyed allowed
  over it (AU-G-CG and PU-G-CG are profile-gleyed); deep-gleyed is
  unchanged (a gleyed layer from 100-130 cm, nothing gleyed above 100
  cm). A layer whose gleying is undecided is read both ways.
- **Depths from the mineral surface:** the depths of the species are
  measured under the organic horizons O and T that start the profile,
  since the litter-peat O does not count (p. 136); the species of the
  peat itself still measure the peat. A podzolic soil O 0-8 over EL 8-23
  is shallow-eluvial.
- **A double botanical name puts the larger share last**, as Russian
  writes it: wood 45 with sedge 50 is древесно-осоковые.
- **The other readings are accepted:** the class limits (the lower end
  of a range for a minimum, the upper end for a maximum, the last
  carbonate class 80-120); what each table measures; an undecided
  species not named and the name not provisional; the rows of chapter 6
  resolved to the types of 2008; the readings of its two columns.
  Transitions such as AUBCA stay out of the thickness of the dark-humus
  horizon. No reading of the Russian classification waits for
  confirmation.

#### Fixed after the review (2026-11-03)

- Cotton-grass is no longer read as herb: “grass” after “cotton” is not
  the herb, and the spellings of one plant (cotton-grass, cottongrass,
  Eriophorum, пушица) add up, in a layer and across layers.
- A transition one of whose masters is a carbonate horizon (AUBCA) has
  carbonates: a chernozem AU 0-40 over AUBCA 40-70 is slightly leached,
  no longer medium leached.
- The bleached species needs only the lower boundary of its horizon: an
  EL whose top is not recorded no longer leaves it undecided. Whether a
  horizon reaches the bottom of the description is read on the depths,
  not on the order of the layers.
- The adjective мелкие, printed by two tables (the dark-humus horizon
  under 30 cm and the layer of 5-10 cm over the solonetzic horizon,
  p. 136), is named once; both rows stay in `levels`.
- The 1977 note keeps what the table adds to a unit (a new `qualifier`
  of the analogues): the varieties of CE03, the genus рихковые of CP10,
  the erosion of CS13, the reclaimed peat soils of raised and fen bogs
  of CS05 and CS06 (now the 1977 types торфяные болотные верховые and
  низинные).
- The PDF report escapes the marks of the formulas (, the backtick) in
  the 1977 section.

## soilKey 0.9.346 (2026-11-03)

### France: the Référentiel pédologique 2008 attaches its first 29 references

The French Référentiel pédologique 2008 (AFES; Baize and Girard coord.;
Éditions Quæ, 2009) enters the registry as `rp2008` (namespace `rp`,
aliases `rp` and `referentiel`; `france`, `french` and `fr` stay with
the CPCS 1967), experimental and opt-in:
[`classify_all()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_all.md)
runs it only when asked.
[`classify_rp2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_rp2008.md)
tests the 29 references of the first nine groups of references (GER):
alocrisols (2), andosols (6), anthroposols (5), arénosols (1), brunisols
(2), the solums dominated by calcium or magnesium (7: rendosols,
calcosols, dolomitosols, rendisols, calcisols, magnésisols,
calcarisols), chernosols (3), colluviosols (1) and cryosols (2). Every
other classification is unchanged.

- **Not a key: an attachment.** Every reference is tested every time
  (Q3): its sequences of reference horizons, matched with
  [`match_horizon_sequence()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/match_horizon_sequence.md)
  on the horizon frame (the RP notation where written, else the horizons
  on the data of 0.9.343), and the side tests of its chapter (depths,
  thicknesses, forbidden horizons, saturation, carbonates, permafrost,
  colluvial and anthropic materials), in
  `inst/rules/rp2008/references/<ger>.yaml`, each with its page, its WRB
  2006 name (Annex 5, display only) and its distinctions in the
  comments.
- **Degrees.** Each reference is evaluated strictly and with the
  tolerances of p. 64 (`tolerances.yaml`: depth and thickness 10 to 200
  cm, pH 0.2, CEC 1, S/CEC 5, organic carbon 8 and 30; every other
  threshold strict, Q5): simple, imperfect (met only within tolerance,
  never promoted, Q4), simple or imperfect, undecided or failed. The
  imperfect cases the chapters name (calcosol leptique, rendosol
  pachique, arénosol rédoxique, anthroposol lithique, calcisol insaturé
  en surface …) attach imperfectly, their qualifier written in the name
  (“calcosol leptique”).
- **One main name and the candidates.** The precedence of the chapters
  first (`precedence.yaml`: a colluviosol only when no other reference
  attaches, a calcarisol before the other six of its GER, the arénosols
  before the rendosols, calcosols and dolomitosols, the perhydric
  silandosols first, the calcisol against the brunisol eutrique by the
  carbonate reserve of Q16 …), then the degree, then the order of the
  rapid key (`rapid_key.yaml`, pp. 66-68; the grisols in soilKey’s 7c),
  Q6. Doubles only for the pairs the book prescribes (`doubles.yaml`:
  calcisol-calcosol, anthroposol transformé-brunisol eutrique when the
  transformé is imperfect, calcosol-anthroposol transformé; the pairs
  with references of later releases listed and waiting), Q7. With no
  reference, “\[non rattaché\]” and the three nearest references. The
  new slot `candidates` holds every reference that may attach, with its
  degree, the criteria that fail, pass only within tolerance or are
  undecided, and the book’s statements that rank it after the name
  (`precedence`). The name is French, as printed, in the singular, the
  English gloss in `levels$name_en`, the GER a label (`rsg_or_order`).
- **The other 25 GER.** Their 81 references come in later releases.
  `key.yaml` lists all 34 GER and 110 references, with a signpost for
  each GER not implemented (the horizons or materials of its chapter: BT
  for the luvisols, BP for the podzosols, G or g within 50 cm for the
  réductisols and rédoxisols …): a profile that shows them gets the GER
  among the candidates, undecided and not implemented yet, and the name
  is provisional when it ranks first. No profile is attached elsewhere
  without saying so.
- `identify_horizons(pedon, "rp2008")` now reaches the RP
  identification;
  [`make_rp2008_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_rp2008_example.md)
  gives one profile per reference, in the RP notation; the examples are
  in the Pro app.
- [`load_rules()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/load_rules.md)
  reads the folders and files a registry entry names besides its levels
  (`rule_folders`, `rule_files`); no other system names any.

#### Hugo’s decisions read here (2026-11-02)

- Q1 (references and types, the GER a label), Q3 (one name and the
  candidates), Q4 (the tolerance band is imperfect), Q5 (the thresholds
  not in the table strict), Q6 (the book, the degree, the rapid key), Q7
  (the doubles the book prescribes), Q14 (the colluvial origin
  required), Q15 (the anthroposols by their materials and the recorded
  history), Q16 (the carbonate reserve by a positive proof), and the
  defaults 1, 2, 9, 13 and 21.

#### Hugo’s answers on the readings (2026-11-03)

- The 17 readings of this release (`readings.yaml`) are accepted,
  revised by the review: the imperfect cases (D1), the open sequences
  (D2), the perhydric andosols (D2, D3), the artificiels and construits
  (R3), the arénosols (D9 and decision 3), the brunisols (D6), the
  carbonate reserve (D7), the calcium GER (D4, D9), the chernosols (D5,
  R2) and the cryosols (decision 1).

#### After the review (2026-11-03)

- **D1.** A reference attached imperfectly within the tolerance of p. 64
  is named by the imperfect case of its chapter whose test holds
  strictly: calcosol leptique at \[A + Sca\] 32 cm, rendosol pachique at
  Aca 38 cm, arénosol rédoxique with -g at 70 cm, arénosol leptique with
  clay at 110 cm, vitrandosol leptique at Avi 27 cm, anthroposol
  artificiel leptique at Z 45 cm, anthroposol reconstitué leptique at
  Ltp 40 cm.
- **D2, D3, R5.** The perhydric silandosols and aluandosols take the
  name only when the perhydric test holds; the aluandosols hapliques no
  longer test it; an And, Snd, Alu or Slu under an Avi makes no
  vitrandosol (an épivitrique silandosol); the leptique case of the
  andosols needs the andic set thinner than 30 cm.
- **D4.** The calcium and magnesium GER excludes a V or SV within 100 cm
  only (bathyvertique deeper, p. 116), and a Ys or Ym within 10 cm (a
  deeper Ys no longer excludes).
- **D5, R2.** The chernosols typiques forbid only a BT directly under
  the Ach, or a humic BTh; the mélanoluviques need over 0.6 % organic
  carbon in the first BT; a cultivated LAh or LAch counts for the 40 cm
  of Ach.
- **D6.** The brunisols read their forbidden horizons, and their
  sequence, in the first material (the first lithological unit of 50 cm
  or more): A-S-IISca-IIRca is a brunisol eutrique; under crops their
  sequence is LS-S; S/CEC over 50 % eutric and under 50 % dystric as
  printed, both imperfect at exactly 50 %, the eutrique named.
- **D7.** The carbonate reserve reads a closed vocabulary of calcareous
  rocks and materials, whole words, and not when denied (non-calcareous,
  decalcified, décarbonaté); a tuff is no longer a reserve.
- **D8.** A test on the first layer of a set is undecided when an
  undecided layer above it could belong to the set and would give
  another verdict.
- **D9.** The arénosols come before the rendosols, calcosols and
  dolomitosols only when the A is not biomacrostructured, and are
  excluded by them when it is; the calcarisols come first only when they
  attach strictly (a Km within tolerance: a calcosol).
- **R3, R4.** The artificiels need a technological material dominant (an
  earthy Ztr or a holorganic ZO makes none); the construits have a
  leptique case (30 to 50 cm), and a recorded construction keeps them
  first; the signpost of the rankosols lets a Sal under 10 cm through.
- The nearest references of a solum attached to none include the
  colluviosols when colluvial material is recorded; the print of an
  attachment and the report’s provisional section speak of an
  attachment, not of a key (the report’s footer, common to every system,
  waits for the name builder).
- Undecided layers that leave the alternatives of a reference undecided
  are completed with their candidates (up to 32 ways); a layer of 50 %
  carbonates and gypsum or more, or indurated, is mineral even with no
  carbon recorded (a calcrete Km).

#### Hugo’s decisions after the review (2026-11-03)

- **1.** A cryosol minéral is simple with the cryoturbation recorded,
  imperfect when the data show the permafrost within 200 cm and record
  no cryoturbation, and then takes the name before the brunisols and the
  other references of later entries of the rapid key.
- **2.** The double anthroposol transformé-brunisol eutrique is written
  only when the transformé is imperfect (the intermediate case of
  p. 91); a simple transformé takes the name and the brunisol stays
  among the candidates.
- **3.** An Ach, And, Alu, Avi, Aso or Sal in the profile excludes the
  arénosols, so that a texture not recorded no longer makes those names
  provisional.

#### Hugo’s decisions on the readings of the review (2026-11-03)

- The first material (a cover under 50 cm skipped); the completion of
  undecided layers in the sequences; a calcrete with no carbon recorded
  is mineral; the first layer of a set under an undecided one (D8); the
  colluviosols among the nearest references; the signposts of the
  rankosols (a thin Sal) and gypsosols (a Ys within 20 cm).
- The carbon of a layer holds over its whole depth: a single Ach of 0-45
  cm with 3 % carbon is clinohumic (0.6 % or more below 40 cm). No
  reading of the Référentiel waits for confirmation.

## soilKey 0.9.345 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the subtypes and the full name

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) names its soils
down to the subtype (подтип): each division has one list of subtypes in
chapter 4, and a soil is named by its type and every subtype of the list
that passes, in the order of the list, comma-separated and in the plural
as printed: “Подзолистые глееватые, языковатые” (Hugo’s decision Q16).

- **The 26 lists, 558 entries** (the chemozems CU have none), in the new
  `inst/rules/kidpr2008/subtypes.yaml`, transcribed in the book’s order
  from pp. 79-133: AA 15, AB 10, BA 22, BB 12, BC 14, \[DA\] 19, CA 35,
  CB 30, CC 16, CD 24, CE 16, CF 17, CG 15, CH 27, CI 27, CJ 18, CK 16,
  CL 11, CM 22, CN 31, CO 22, CP 23, CQ 30, CR 30, CS 35, CT 21. Each
  entry has soilKey’s ASCII key (g, ELf, hh for \[hh\], e_hf for
  \[e-hf\], akl, cryoturb for @, perm for the permafrost sign, TTal for
  TT, TTash for TT”), the index as printed, the Russian name, an English
  gloss, the hosts, the page and notes; the universal subtypes are
  marked.
- **The subtype level** after the type, read by the feature tests of
  0.9.344 (data first, then the Russian notation, then the defaults):
  the subtypes are rows of level `subtype` in `levels` (as the Hungarian
  subtypes), the full name in English in `name` (“Podzolic gleyic,
  tongued”) and in Russian in `qualifiers$name_native`; every entry,
  with its evidence, route and hosts, is in the trace (phase `subtype`).
- **Typical and provisional.** When every entry is FALSE the soil is of
  the typical subtype, soilKey’s \[типичные\] (\[typical\]), which the
  lists leave out (p. 76); when some are undecided the name is
  provisional, the undecided entries in `provisional_because` and in a
  warning, the passing ones still named.
- **Not named again** when the formula of the type writes the feature: g
  in the gley types, q in the quasigley ones, ELg in CA03, BF in CB05, s
  and cs in the BCAs,cs of the solonetzes, the residual carbonates in a
  type written with Cca; a feature in parentheses (C(ca), Q(s)) is
  optional and does not count. A V or an S laid over a horizon (BCA+V,
  AU+S) names the soil vertic or saline. Where the list has ELg, g is
  read on the layers other than EL.
- **Single-type sentences.** The list decides where a feature applies; a
  sentence of 3.2 restricts it only when it names a single type: te in
  the oligotrophic peat soils, \[akl\] in the brown arid soils, crm in
  the podzolic soils, ct in the sod-podzolic soils, cf in the gleyzems,
  ocr in the peaty cryozems.
- **The carbonate profile** of CI, CJ and CQ to CT is one of a scale
  (default 19): nodules over pseudomycelium over diffuse carbonates, the
  form with the migrating carbonates of the humus horizon (AUlc-BCAmc,
  AUlc-BCAnc, AJlc-BCAnc) where lc holds. The double el of CI and CM is
  read by its place; \[BHF-BAN\]\>3 of the volcanic soils is a test of
  its own (more than three elementary profiles buried under the surface
  soil).
- **Buried soils and thin deposits.** A soil keyed by its buried
  horizons under a deposit of 40 cm or less keeps them for its subtypes,
  and the deposit written as a horizon of 5-40 cm over a bracketed humus
  horizon is rh (RU, RY, RJ) or r (C); only where the formula writes the
  buried soil (\[ABC\], {ABC}) is it left out.
- **Reachability.** On profiles built from the formulas of each
  division, every entry is named somewhere except those its division
  cannot have: s and cs in CK (written in every formula) and x in the
  divisions of trunk C keyed after the chemozems (an X within 30 cm
  makes a chemozem); pb in CC, CE and CG and agr, ad, pa in the abrazems
  are reached only by the feature tests, not in a classified soil.
- **The book’s own names** are reproduced: the sod-pale-podzolic gleyic
  soil and the podzolic soil with a podzol microprofile (p. 60), the
  podzolised podbur (p. 60), the contact-bleached podzol (p. 67), the
  dark-humus water-accumulative stratozem (p. 129), and the chemozem of
  p. 134 keeps its name.
- [`classify_kidpr2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_kidpr2008.md)
  gains `subtypes = TRUE`; `FALSE` stops at the type (the tests of the
  keys and types use it). A soil whose type is unassigned gets no
  subtypes.
- On the 27 examples the classification takes about 5 s instead of 3; on
  the 44 canonical fixtures 5 s instead of 4. The other systems are
  unchanged (their fixtures byte-identical).

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03)

Nine readings of the subtypes, accepted by Hugo and recorded in
`readings.yaml` as his decisions, as revised after the review of the
subtypes: no subtypes for a soil whose type is unassigned; the six
single-type sentences; what counts as written in the formula (the
horizon that is the feature in full: G, Q, V, ML, S, F, CR; Cca keeps
the residual-carbonate subtype out of the solods; an optional (ca) does
not; a V or S overlay is v or s); the hosts the lists narrow (h, mr, Th,
\[e-hf\], el of the weakly developed soils on W, hi of the agrozems
under PT, ae of CJ on AJ, crm of the cryozems on or over CR, ox, fn and
ff of the eluvial soils on their D or EL); a buried soil does not name
the soil over it where the formula writes it, and a thin deposit over a
buried soil is r or rh; the misprints corrected and the glosses kept;
the layered-ochric soils (buried profiles only); the subtypes their
division cannot have (pb in CC, CE and CG; agr, ad and pa in the
abrazems; s and cs in CK; x in trunk C after the chemozems; the
contact-eluviated podzol of p. 67, since the CB list has no el; no v for
CH04 with a V on its G; a solonchak under a small deposit loses its
division in the key); and the form of the full name. A tenth, of
2026-11-03: where the list has ELg, g is read on the layers other than
EL (gleying in EL alone is ELg alone, in BT too both). No reading of the
Russian classification waits for confirmation.

The report’s note on the undecided classes now covers the undecided
subtypes too, and [`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html) no
longer lists the Russian full name and the formula of the type among the
qualifiers.

## soilKey 0.9.344 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the tests of the genetic features

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) gains the tests of
its genetic features (признаки, section 3.2 and the subtype lists of
chapter 4): one test per feature, shared by every division that lists
it, for the subtypes that follow (the 26 lists and the full name come
next). Nothing is named yet, so every classification is unchanged.

- **67 tests, the 73 index forms.** One internal function per feature of
  `features.yaml` (the 64 of 3.2 and w, x, rx of the lists); the aliases
  of the book (tu, ko, ag, as, ael, hh, akl) and the host forms of the
  lists (ELf, ELg, Th, Oh, AUh, AUel, Gel, Pw, PUw, TEmr, Tote, Di, Del,
  AJ\[akl\], and the pairs AUlc-BCAmc, AUlc-BCAnc, AJlc-BCAnc, which
  need both parts) are read through them. Each test is three-valued and
  gives its evidence and the attributes that would decide it.
- **Data first, then the notation, then the defaults.** A feature is
  read on the recorded data where an attribute records what it describes
  (the proxies of Q17: g, q, v, s, cs, nn, i, the columnar sn, BH and BF
  by the carbon of the BHF, an by the oxalates, the sapric h, lc, mc, nc
  and dc by the form of the carbonates, ml, the permafrost sign, @, tr,
  y, \[hh\], ro, r, rh, ur, rr), and the key to horizons gives the small
  horizons and the features it ends in (ao, e, el, r, rh, tr, u, ca).
  Where the data say nothing, the Russian notation decides: a feature
  not written on a layer of a profile written in it is absent; a letter
  of another notation can add one (an FAO Bg suggests g). Where neither
  does, a field observation not recorded is absent and a measurement not
  recorded leaves the feature undecided. hi, pl, crm, f, el on a
  horizon, ic, agr, ad, pr, ff, fn, ocr and yu come from the notation
  only (Q17). Recorded data that contradict the notation decide, with a
  note.
- **Hosts and places.** A feature holds on the horizons the text puts it
  on, with the analogies of Q17 (pl in CRM, cf at the edge of CR) and
  the horizons of the lists that name it; a host the data leave
  undecided leaves a passing feature undecided, and with no host the
  feature is absent. The double el of CI and CM is read by its place: in
  the AU, solodised (осолоделые); under the AU, eluviated
  (элювиированные).
- **x, rx and ur (Q17).** x is an X horizon (pollutants at the extremely
  hazardous level within 30 cm) in a soil the key did not send to the
  chemozems; rx a toxic layer of 5-40 cm over a buried humus horizon; ur
  the same layer with 20 % or more of artefacts. pb is read in the agro
  horizon with over 1.5 % humus, and in the light-humus carbonate soils
  (CJ) on a natural soil with deflation or truncation recorded (Q19).
- **The dispatcher** (internal) runs a list of (feature, host, place)
  entries on a pedon and returns one row per entry: the feature, its
  code, the host, the place, the layers, the verdict, the route (data,
  notation or both), the evidence and what is missing. Its metadata are
  in the new `inst/rules/kidpr2008/feature_tests.yaml` (the test, its
  route, the hosts, the place, whether it is a field observation or a
  measurement, the attributes it reads); `features.yaml` keeps the hosts
  the text gives.
- On the 27 examples every feature is decided; on the 44 canonical
  fixtures of the other systems 2,849 of 2,948 feature tests are
  decided, the undecided ones mostly the salts and the permafrost, which
  those profiles do not record.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **Features read on the data where Q17 is silent:** te (high-moor over
  a thinner low-moor peat within 50 cm), e (also bleached spots recorded
  in a humus or middle horizon), el on the data only as the band of key
  52a, m (a weak pedogenic structure in the top C that is not sand), tk
  (a clay crust with polygonal cracks), ox (redox features of 50 % or
  more in G), ek (a whitish band of 5 cm or less over a heavier
  lithological layer or D), gr (a granular BFM), d (a platy surface
  layer of a natural soil), pa (abandoned or fallow land on a ploughed
  horizon), md (a sapric surface layer over the peat), pir (a pyrogenic
  layer of over 2 cm on the peat), aq and ae (the origin of the
  stratified horizon), TT and TT” (alluvial or ash bands in the peat), w
  (a W over the host) and ca (also local effervescence with no carbonate
  neoformation).
- **From the notation only:** mr, \[e-hf\], \[akl\], cf and ct, like the
  features of Q17’s list; in a profile not written in the Russian
  notation these features are absent, not undecided.
- **Hosts and places:** the hosts of 3.2 and of the lists that name a
  feature elsewhere (f, i, crm, fn, hi, ic, sn, pa, e, w on the horizon
  under the W); a small horizon counts for the host beside it; AUel is
