  el in the AU, the eluviated el is el under the AU, Gel el on G; an
  undecided host leaves a passing feature undecided, no host makes it
  absent.
- **Deposited layers and cut-points:** r, rh, ur, rr, rx need 5-40 cm
  over a buried humus horizon; ur 20 % to under half of artefacts, rr
  half or more and not toxic, rx a hazard above permissible; ro every
  mineral horizon 5YR or redder; cs visible gypsum (CaSO4 0 % none); s
  by the EC of chapter 9 (ECe 4, EC 1:5 0.2 dS/m); ml hard concretions;
  g not on olive mottles alone, q olive mottles of 5Y chroma 3-4; \[hh\]
  darker by a value and richer in carbon than the layer above; y with
  the retic or albeluvic stand-in, flagged.
- The four readings are in `readings.yaml` as his decisions; no reading
  of the Russian classification waits for confirmation.

#### After the review (2026-11-02)

- **Fixes.** y only under an eluvial horizon (E, EL, AEL, BEL), dark
  tongues from a humus horizon being yu; ca not where any form of
  secondary carbonates is recorded, nor on an FAO k layer, and the FAO
  Ck no longer suggests ca; v and sn not ruled out by a structure alone
  (the notation decides), q not by mottles of other colours; pa ruled
  out only by current tillage on an agro horizon; ro leaves out the
  organic and peat layers by their horizon and reads the gley, blue,
  purple and neutral hues as not red, RP as red; x ruled out by a hazard
  category recorded within 30 cm, and written only on a layer starting
  within 30 cm; g not on mottles recorded as “none”; m undecided when
  the texture of the rock is not recorded, a weak no when the grade is
  not; d read on the first mineral layer under an organic one.
- **The salts:** over 1 % in the top 20 cm makes the salt horizon S and
  no feature s in the profile; ECe decides over EC 1:5 where both are
  recorded.
- **Limits of the definitions:** te may be a small horizon; crm only
  over BT; i on the parent rock only at its top; nn 10-20 %; a crust
  layer of tk 0.5 cm or less; d not on a fine platy structure; the muck
  band of h on top of a humus horizon only on the AU of the dark-humus
  gley soils; ml in the middle or lower profile only; @ reads yes and
  TRUE; \[e-hf\] in or beside EL (the example of p. 60,
  O-\[e-hf\]-EL-BEL-BT-C).
- The dispatcher stops on an unknown host or place and returns an empty
  table for no entries.

#### Hugo’s decisions after the review (2026-11-02)

- **Accepted edits:** crm over BT only; \[e-hf\] in or beside EL.
- **New readings** (`readings.yaml`, “The feature tests after the
  review”): ca a field observation (effervescence not recorded is
  absent; an FAO k layer a weak no); m with 15 % clay or more as a loamy
  or clayey rock when no texture class is recorded; tk fails on a
  surface layer of 0.5-2 cm (a crust thicker than 0.5 cm); d fails on a
  fine or very fine platy structure; \[hh\] by the darker colour,
  confirmed by the carbon; q ruled out by mottles recorded as none,
  other colours only a weak no; sn never ruled out by the data; s ruled
  out for the whole profile by over 1 % salts within the top 20 cm; the
  muck band h on top of a humus horizon only on an AU in a profile with
  G.

## soilKey 0.9.343 (2026-11-02)

### France: the reference horizons of the Référentiel pédologique 2008 on the data

The Référentiel pédologique 2008 has no key to its reference horizons:
they are concepts read with the whole sequence (p. XII). This release
reads them on the recorded data, layer by layer, for profiles not
written in the RP notation, and gives the horizon frame the references
will be matched on. Nothing is classified yet, so every classification
of the other systems is unchanged; the registry entry and the references
follow.

- **A fixed order of tests** (internal, `.rp_identify()`), soilKey’s,
  from the book’s order of presentation (p. 6) and its statements of
  dominance: the layers and materials (R, M, D, P, TH, Z and its kinds,
  Mli, Mt); the holorganic horizons (H with Hf, Hm, Hs and Ha; O with
  OL, OFr, OFm, OHr, OHf and OHta); the coarse elements (ND, X with Xgr,
  Xc, Xp); G (Gr, Go, AG), which dominates every other character of the
  layer, so no SG or BTG; the indurated and accumulation horizons (U, K,
  Kc, Km, Si, Sim, Fe, Fem, Femp, Y, Ys, Yp, Ym, OXm, OXc); the surface
  A horizons (An, Ach, Aso, Aca, Ado, Aci, Amg, Alu, And, Avi, Av, Anod,
  Ae, A, Js); the subsurface ones (E, BP, BPh, BPs, BT, BTß, V, SV, Snd,
  Slu, F, Fox, Fhy, OX, RT, FE, Sn, FS, Sp, Sca, Sdo, Sci, Smg, Sal, S,
  Jp, C); then the features of every layer (g, ho, k, t, v, x, y, d, cn,
  j, cry, nod, c, b, ca, a, h of Scah) on the hosts the book lists, and
  the overlays L, Na and Sa (LA, NaBT, SaA, JZ). Every test is
  three-valued: the first that holds gives the code, the other codes
  that hold or stay undecided go to the candidates, and a layer the data
  leave open is undecided with the attributes that would decide it.
- **The frame** has the columns of
  [`identify_horizons()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/identify_horizons.md)
  and the RP ones: the family of the code, the code written with its
  prefixes, features and Roman numeral (`composed`: LAch, NaBTg, II
  Scag), the kinds a code may be refined to (`variants`: H to Hf, Hm,
  Hs), the thresholds met only within the tolerance of p. 64
  (`imperfect`), the WRB stand-ins and the other substitutes used, a
  lower grade where they were, the depths from the datum (`top_rp`,
  `bottom_rp`), the lithological discontinuity and the hints of other
  notations.
- **The notation and the data.** A layer written in the RP notation
  keeps its code; the order of tests runs on its data as well, and a
  different reading goes to the evidence (route “both” when they agree).
  A layer in the CPCS or FAO notation is read on the data, its
  designation narrowing the candidates through Annex 6 and the FAO
  letters.
- **The readers** (`R/rp-readers.R`): the moist colour, the carbon
  classes, the carbonates and effervescence (cold, hot, the molar
  CaCO3/MgCO3), S/CEC with its CEC method, the sodium over the sum of
  the bases, the coarse elements by weight with the volume band, the
  redox features (location, relict), the reduced matrix, the salts, the
  intertropical and andosol gates, ploughing, the depth datum (the top
  of the first layer that is not a litter OL, FAO Oi or CPCS A00) and
  the hydromorphy of a profile from its frame.
- **WRB stand-ins**, flagged and with a lower grade, where a field
  descriptor is missing: argic() for the clay coatings of BT, spodic()
  for BP, calcic() and petrocalcic() for K, vertic_horizon() and
  vertic_properties() for V and SV, nitic_horizon() for the pressure
  faces of Sn, ferralic() for F and OX, chernic() and mollic() for Ach,
  umbric_horizon() for Aso (never sombric()), albic() for E,
  stagnic_properties() for g, andic_properties() and vitric_properties()
  for the andosol domain, retic_properties() and albeluvic_glossae() for
  BTd, continuous_rock() for R, and some others.
- **New site field** `intertropical`: the site declared in or outside
  the intertropical domain, where F, OX, RT, ND, FE, OXc and OXm are
  tested (Q18).
- The identification is internal until the registry entry `rp2008`
  exists:
  [`identify_horizons()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/identify_horizons.md)
  does not reach it yet.

#### Hugo’s decisions read here (2026-11-02)

- **The order of tests (Q10):** soilKey’s order from the book’s order of
  presentation; the first test that holds gives the code, the others go
  to the candidates; a missing field descriptor is read through a WRB
  diagnostic, flagged, never the faux amis of p. 392.
- **Coarse elements (Q11), methods (Q12), functional redox (Q13), the
  most specific text (Q17), the tropical domain (Q18), H against O
  (Q19)** and the defaults 3, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 20, as
  the readers and `inst/rules/rp2008/readings.yaml` state them.
- **The new site field `intertropical` (Q18)** is kept: the site
  declared in or outside the intertropical domain, before the Köppen
  climate and the latitude.
- **The readings of the horizons on the data, accepted**
  (`inst/rules/rp2008/readings.yaml`): an undecided G leaves the layer
  undecided against the code read after it (G dominates, p. 280); the
  designation of another notation narrows the candidates and decides a
  single one left, never an H; a grey matrix is reductic only with a
  sign of water excess (Gr with 10 % redox features or less, Go with
  segregations at the voids); the holorganic layers by the loss on
  ignition, else carbon 30 +/- 5 %, and the kinds of O by the fine
  organic matter; the surface run of the A horizons and the A material
  (0.5 % carbon or more, not bleached), Js and Jp, Ae; Ach (value 3.5 or
  less, chroma 2 or less, carbon 3 % or more for every texture), Aso
  (the list of p. 13 as the test, the grisols of p. 193 as evidence,
  imperfect when only one holds) and An; the carbonates (a slight
  effervescence not generalised, no carbonate recorded at pH under 6.5
  not carbonated) and the calcimagnesian variant of Aci and Sci,
  imperfect; the stand-in of K only below the surface and with more
  CaCO3 than every layer below; BT (the increase of the WRB argic
  horizon, clay films common or many), BTss, BTd and E on the data; BP
  (the oxalate, else spodic() under a bleached layer or with more carbon
  above); V, SV and Av; the intertropical horizons (F by the CEC of the
  clay, OX, RT, FE; OXm and OXc, not Fem, in the domain); Sn, FS, Sp,
  Sal and the andosol gate; the layers and materials (R, M, D, P, TH, Z,
  Mli, Mt); coarse elements not recorded are none; gypsum, silica and
  iron (Ys, Yp, Ym, Si, Sim, Fe, Fem, Femp); the overlays L, Na and Sa;
  the features.

## soilKey 0.9.342 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the types of trunks A, B and D, and the name of the chemozems

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) gains the types of
the six divisions of the organogenic, synlithogenic and weakly developed
trunks: 58 types, matched as the types of trunk C are (0.9.338,
0.9.339). The chemozems (CU), which have no types, are now named by
their pollutants and the soil they were. Every division has its type
level; the subtypes follow. Every other classification is unchanged.

- **The 58 types** in `inst/rules/kidpr2008/types/`: AA 5 (peat soils),
  AB 4 (peatozems), BA 18 (alluvial soils), BB 4 (volcanic soils), BC 10
  (stratozems) and \[DA\] 17 (the weakly developed soils of trunk D, the
  division the book does not code). Each has soilKey’s code in brackets
  (\[AA01\] … \[DA17\], in the order of chapter 4, the natural types
  first), the Russian name as printed (two slips of the diagrams of the
  alluvial soils, глеевы and the second мергелистые, as chapter 6 writes
  them), an English gloss, the formula as the fixture of the formulas
  transcribes it, and the page.
- **What the formulas test (Q14).** The buried soil \[ABC\] names the
  stratozems on a buried soil and is tested, a buried profile starting
  within 100 cm (p. 128); the substrate D is not. The substrate names
  the types of trunk D and is tested: the marks of the loose rock (C=
  loamy and clayey, C.. sandy, C alluvial, C” ash, C aeolian) and the
  hard rock R, with its carbonate or gypsum mark where written (Rca,
  Rcs); the C of the solonchaks is not. The rock under the dry-peat
  soils (AA05) is tested: the hard rock R or loose material C (p. 43); a
  rock under the peat closes no other formula of the peat soils. The
  alluvial and ash marks of the parent material in BA and BB, and the
  buried profiles {ABC} of the volcanic soils, are not tested; the
  buried humus horizons of the alluvial soils are not in the formula
  (p. 124).
- **The peat of trunk A.** A peat horizon that runs across the line 50
  cm under the top of the peat body is TT below that line (Q22): TO
  0-120 cm is TO-TT (AA01), PT over T 25-125 cm is PT-TT (AB01); a peat
  horizon that starts 50 cm or more under the top of the body is TT (TO
  0-50 over TO 50-120 is AA01). A T of the notation in the peat soils is
  TO or TE by the botany of its layer, undecided between them when the
  layer records none.
- **The substrate of trunk D.** The layer directly under the O or W
  names the type; a deeper rock is not tested (W-C..-R is DA04). On the
  data route a layer with no horizon under the O or W is the loose rock,
  and an undesignated layer that names a rock and records no texture is
  undecided between the R and the C types. A C whose mark is not written
  takes it from the data, the layer’s own origin first and the site’s
  parent material only when the layer records none: an alluvial, ash or
  aeolian origin (loess is not aeolian here), else the texture (sand and
  loamy sand are sandy, finer is loamy and clayey), undecided with no
  texture recorded; the legend’s aeolian mark “” is the of the diagrams;
  a proluvial body (an alluvial fan) has no type. A rock R whose marks
  are not written, on the data route or a bare R of the notation, takes
  its carbonate mark from a carbonate rock named (marble included) or
  effervescence and its gypsum mark from a gypsum rock named; another
  rock named has neither; a rock not named leaves them undecided.
- **The stratozems.** Of several stratified horizons in the body, the
  thickest names the type and the others are its features (RY 20 over RU
  30 is BC02); a tie leaves the type undecided.
- **The alluvial soils on the data route.** The surface humus layer the
  key to horizons reads as RU or RY over a buried humus horizon is, for
  the types, the humus horizon AU or AY of the floodplain, and a layer
  with no diagnostic horizon the alluvium: AU over alluvium over Ab over
  alluvium is BA02, as its twin in the notation. The fix is in the
  reading of the alluvial types; key 2.1 and the divisions are
  unchanged.
- **The BH of the ochric soils.** The notation reads BH and BF as BHF,
  so the BH of BB01 and BB03 is read as a BHF of either kind, as Q15
  does for CR07 and CS10; without it the two types could not be reached.
- **The name of a chemozem.** The book divides the chemozems by the kind
  of pollution, keeping the name of the original soil (p. 134). The type
  level is now built: soilKey’s code `[CU:<code of the original soil>]`
  and the names “Chemozems polluted with Cu, Ni, Co; original soil:
  Sod-podzolic” and “Хемоземы, загрязненные Cu, Ni, Co, по исходной
  почве: Дерново-подзолистые”. The pollutants are those recorded in
  `pollutants` for the layers of the X horizon, split on commas,
  semicolons and “and”; the original soil is the profile keyed again
  with the X masked (the X overlays the notation reader parses, AY+Xpb
  as well as AY+X, taken out, a layer that is only X dropped, and the
  contamination records removed), down to its type, and is in the trace
  (phase `chemozem`, an assigned step). An original soil with no
  division is named “…, division not provided by the Field Guide of
  2008”; a masked profile that is a chemozem again leaves the original
  soil undecided (\[CU:?\]). Pollutants not recorded are named so and
  asked in `$missing_data`; an original soil undecided at its type or
  division is named so and makes the name provisional (`original_soil:`
  entries in `provisional_because`). This changes a result of 0.9.337 to
  0.9.339: a chemozem had the division as its name.
- **Contaminated soils outside trunk C.** The X horizon is no horizon of
  the profile for step 5 of the key to trunks, so a contaminated soil of
  trunk A, B or D keeps its division and type (W+X over C.. is DA04, not
  a chemozem; the subtype x will name it). This changes a division
  result of 0.9.337. The X horizon counts at C.3b also when it lies on a
  surface horizon the thickest-horizon rule leaves out (O 15 over AY+X
  10 over EL-BT is a chemozem, \[CU:CA01\]); in 0.9.337 to 0.9.341 it
  was lost.
- **Doubles.** Two formulas match one profile only where the rock names
  what the other formula leaves out: O-Rca is DA07 with DA05 its
  intergrade, W-Rca DA08 with DA06, O-Rcs DA09 with DA05, W-Rcs DA10
  with DA06; the more specific names the type, as decided for trunk C.
- Every chapter 4 formula of trunks A, B and D, written as a profile in
  the Russian notation, reaches its own division and its own type,
  decided. One undesignated profile per division reaches its type
  through the key to horizons on the data.
- **Profiles with a division and no type** under the literal Q13 and Q14
  (`readings.yaml`): TJ-TT over G, H at the top of a peat body, RU or RY
  on the floodplain, AY over Q, AO directly over BAN, PU over RY, O or W
  over D.
- The tests of the oracle of the keys read only the trunk and the
  division as undecided: an undecided type, or the original soil of a
  chemozem, is no answer of keys 2.2 and 2.3.
- A tie of recorded thicknesses at the surface, which leaves a type
  undecided, no longer asks for the depths in `$missing_data`.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **The name of a chemozem:** as designed: soilKey’s code
  `[CU:<code of the original soil>]`, the pollutants as recorded, the
  original soil in the nominative after “по исходной почве:”,
  “pollutants not recorded” when none are, and the name provisional when
  the original soil is undecided.
- **The rock under the dry peat (AA05):** by p. 43 the hard rock R or
  loose material C may lie under the TJ body: TJ-TT over C is AA05, as
  TJ-TT over R; the C closes no other formula of the peat soils (TO-TT
  over C is AA01).
- **After the review:** a peat horizon starting 50 cm or more under the
  top of the peat body is TT, as the data route reads it; in trunk D the
  substrate directly under the O or W names the type and a deeper R is
  not tested; of several stratified horizons in a stratozem the thickest
  names the type; in the peat soils an R under the peat body does not
  block AA01 to AA04 (TO-TT over R is AA01), only AA05 requires R or C
  under the TJ; the chemozems follow Q23, a contaminated soil of trunk
  A, B or D keeping its division and type; a bare R of the notation
  takes its marks from the data as a C does, and an undesignated layer
  that names a rock and records no texture is undecided between the R
  and the C types.
- **A named rock that is neither carbonate nor gypsum** (granite,
  sandstone …) has neither mark: O over an R of granite with no
  effervescence recorded is DA05, decided.
- **The readings of this release, accepted** (`readings.yaml`): TT below
  the upper 50 cm of the peat body and a T of the notation as TO or TE
  by its botany; the substrate of the weakly developed soils (no horizon
  is loose rock, the mark from the origin or the texture, the legend’s
  “” read as , a proluvial body with no type, the marks of R from the
  rock recorded); the BH of BB01 and BB03 a BHF of either kind; the
  profiles the literal formulas leave without a type. Every reading in
  `readings.yaml` is again one of Hugo’s decisions.

#### After the review (2026-11-02)

- **Fixes.**
  - A grey matrix outside the bluish, greenish and neutral hues is
    reductic only with a positive dipyridyl test, recorded water
    saturation or a water table at the layer (or water above the
    surface), never the drainage class alone; an A is AG only in a
    bluish or greenish hue; Gr only with 5 % of redox features or less,
    5-10 % with no location leaving Go and g undecided.
  - The A run at the surface continues only under a layer of A material,
    with more than 1 % carbon (a transition such as BA is no A
    designation); a layer that continues it is read by the subsurface
    tests too, and is undecided between the A and the subsurface code
    when both hold.
  - E: bleached is a moist value of 5 or more with chroma 2 or less; a
    lower chroma counts as lighter only at an equal or higher value;
    clay films common or many, or more clay than the layer above,
    exclude it; above a rock or a coarse layer with no fine earth only a
    bleached layer is an E.
  - Aso holds only on the list of p. 13 (the grisols reading of p. 193
    is evidence), and only in a well aerated A (no functional redox
    features, no reduced matrix).
  - A BT that is also fersiallitic is FSt; a BT or FE with ferric
    nodules under 40 % is BTcn or FEcn, not Fe; -cn only on BT and FE,
    -j only on S, Sci and BT, on an angular (not subangular) structure.
  - TH never with jarosite or a pH under 4 (the sulfated U).
  - Jp under an A or LA in a young deposit as well as under a Js, before
    the S.
  - A G candidate is never narrowed away by a designation.
  - The andosol domain opens only on volcanic material recorded or on
    the andic or vitric properties holding; an Alox + 1/2 Feox under 2 %
    closes it.
  - Na only on a columnar, prismatic or coarse structure, or a massive
    one with 1 cmol+/kg of sodium or more; never undecided on a layer
    with no degraded structure.
  - Ach: the 3 % carbon in the top 10 cm of the A run, a lighter mineral
    layer below and a gradual decrease of the carbon, chernic() alone as
    the stand-in; the moist value stays 3.5 or less (the chapter,
    p. 126, Q17).
  - Ae not on a ploughed layer; M without a designation (a soft layer
    with no fine earth and its carbonates recorded, or an FAO Cr); OL in
    a profile written in capitals still the litter of the depth datum,
    and OF, OH as hints; a light layer under 1 % carbon under an O read
    as an E, not an A; a mineral designation with no data makes the
    layer mineral; OX with pH 5.5-6.5; Sci with pH over 6.5; a loss on
    ignition contradicted by the carbon flagged, and no A over 30 %
    carbon; an imperfectly drained site as a sign of water excess.

#### Hugo’s decisions after the review (2026-11-02)

- **The revised readings** (`inst/rules/rp2008/readings.yaml`): the
  designations narrowing the candidates (never a G away; BA is no A; OL,
  OF and OH in capitals; a mineral designation makes the layer mineral),
  the reductic matrix, the holorganic layers, the A run at the surface,
  Ach, Aso and An, BT and E, the intertropical horizons, Sn, FS, Sp, Sal
  and the andosol gate, the layers and materials, gypsum, silica and
  iron, the overlays and the features, as the fixes above read them.
- **soilKey’s additions, accepted:** Aso needs a well aerated A (no
  functional redox features, no reduced matrix, p. 13); tidal flooding,
  water above the surface or a subaqueous site count as a water table
  for a grey matrix; the A run continues only under a layer of A
  material; a light layer low in carbon is read as an E only directly
  under an O; an E is undecided when the BP below it is undecided; Fe
  only with ferric nodules of 40 % or more where a BT or FE also holds,
  otherwise BTcn or FEcn.
- **Aso:** with the list of p. 13 as the only test, the “imperfect when
  only one holds” clause of Q17 is empty: when the list of p. 13 holds,
  the grisols reading of p. 193 always holds too.
- **The biomacrostructured A (d3):** without biogenic_aggregates_pct, a
  crumb or granular structure with a recorded biological activity (worm
  holes, burrows, earthworms, a mull) reads the biomacrostructured A,
  flagged; a polyhedral, massive or other structure reads the A that is
  not; nothing recorded stays undecided.

## soilKey 0.9.341 (2026-11-02)

### France: the notation of the Référentiel pédologique 2008

The French Référentiel pédologique 2008 (AFES) writes its reference
horizons in a notation of its own (LAch, NaBTg2, II Scag, E&BT, OFrzo)
and defines its references by sequences of them. This release adds the
reader of that notation, the catalogue of its horizons and marks, and
the fields its references will read. Nothing is classified yet, so every
classification is unchanged; the horizons on the data, then the registry
entry with the references, follow.

- **The notation reader** (internal). A designation is read in a closed,
  case-sensitive vocabulary by the longest match (Snd is the silandic S,
  not Sn with d; Sal the aluminic S, not Sa with l; Kc, Xc, OXc and Femp
  are codes of their own) into its code, the listed code a variant
  belongs to (OF for OFr), its family, the overlays L, Na, Sa, the paleo
  π and J (LA, NaBT, πRT, JZtc), its suffixes as features with their
  reading on that host (c is indurated, but the mycogenic structure
  after OF or OH; x is fragic, but mixed rocks after D), a Roman numeral
  for a lithological discontinuity, the digits of a sub-horizon,
  transitions (A-S, and BC or ACk written without the hyphen) and
  juxtaposed volumes (E&BT). The writings the book uses for another code
  are read with a note (Lav, Vna, Vsa, OFz, OHz, OHmzo), and the old
  codes Ahs, FEm, FEmp and Ap as Aso, Fem, Femp and L. A designation it
  cannot read is left unread with a note; text that is not UTF-8 is read
  as Latin-1; nothing stops with an error.
- **The notation of a profile** is decided before any letter is read,
  since the RP shares A1, A2, Cca, G, Go and Gr with the CPCS 1967, with
  opposite meanings for A2 and Cca. A profile is in the RP notation when
  `site$designation_system` declares it, or when it has one code only
  the RP writes (OL, OF, OH, BP, LA, SV, FS, OX, RT, FE, Sca, Sal, Aca,
  Ach, Aso, Kc, Km, Js, Ys, Ztc, Mli, BTß, E&BT, NaBT …) or two kinds of
  code that it alone usually writes (Fe, K, Si, Hf, Hm, Hs, X, Y, U, V,
  Sn, ND, Sg, Cca, a BT with a lower-case suffix where another
  designation has lower case), and no symbol only the CPCS writes (A00,
  A0, (A), (B), Bfe, Can, an A2 used as an E) and no sign of the Russian
  notation. A profile with both is undecided: no designation is read as
  an RP code, and both readings go to the evidence. The country is never
  read. In a profile declared `rp1995`, or written with FEm, FEmp or
  Ahs, FE is the ferric Fe of the RP of 1995, not the ferruginous FE of
  2008.
- **Hints from other notations.** A CPCS designation gives the RP codes
  of Annex 6 (A2 gives E or Ea, Cca gives Ck, K, Kc or Km, (B) the S
  horizons, with the slips of the table noted), and an FAO designation
  the codes of soilKey’s table of the FAO letters (Bt gives BT or FSt,
  Bw the S horizons, Oi OL). They are candidates for the identification
  on the data, never the RP code. The CPCS and Russian readers do not
  change.
- **The catalogue** `inst/rules/rp2008/horizons.yaml`: the 75 codes of
  the list of reference horizons, the 4 layers and 8 materials, 11
  variants printed in the definitions and chapters (Fox, Fhy, the five
  kinds of OX, Gr, Go, Mma, Marg), the 7 O sub-horizons of Annex 1, 4
  old codes and the B of the transitions (each with the name as printed,
  an English gloss, its family, the page and its class for the
  recognition), the 5 prefixes and 32 suffixes with the hosts the book
  lists, the writings of the book read as another code, the Annex 6
  table and the table of the FAO letters. Every sequence of reference
  horizons printed in the 34 chapters and in Annex 1 (359 rows, 308
  distinct strings) reads with no unknown code.
- **New fields.** Horizon: `coarse_fragments_wt_pct` and the four
  classes by weight `gravel_wt_pct` (graviers, 0.2-2 cm),
  `cobbles_wt_pct` (cailloux, 2-7.5 cm), `stones_wt_pct` (pierres,
  7.5-20 cm) and `boulders_wt_pct` (blocs, over 20 cm); `cec_method`;
  `redox_relict`; `anthropic_material` and `anthropic_material_pct`;
  `o_zoogenic`; and the 21 fields that decide a reference horizon:
  `fine_organic_matter_pct`, `biogenic_aggregates_pct`,
  `biogenic_aggregate_size`, `effervescence_hot`, `mgco3_pct`,
  `fe_total_pct`, `fe_ffe_pct`, `weatherable_minerals_pct`,
  `oxides_triacid_pct`, `clay_mineralogy`, `halloysite_pct`,
  `kaolinite_pct`, `smectite_pct`, `degradation_form`, `tongue_vol_pct`,
  `tongue_width_mm`, `lamellae_cumulative_cm`, `c_pyro_pct`,
  `pyrophosphate_index`, `s_total_pct` and `nodules_wt_pct`. Site:
  `valley_position`, `flood_frequency`, `poldered`,
  `lateral_bp_downslope`, `rp_anthropic_history`,
  `rp_qualifiers_recorded` and `parent_material_relation`. The values
  `rp`, `rp2008`, `rp1995`, `referentiel` and `afes` of
  `site$designation_system`, the humus forms of Annex 1 in `humus_form`,
  and the origins `colluvic`, `marine` and `transported` of
  `layer_origin`.
- The description of `cole_value` now says what it measures: from moist
  at 33 kPa to oven dry, not from 1500 kPa.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **Registry names (Q2):** the system will be `rp2008`, namespace `rp`,
  aliases `rp` and `referentiel`; `france`, `french` and `fr` stay with
  the CPCS, so nothing changes for those who use it.
- **The notation (Q9):** declared, or one symbol only the RP writes, or
  two that it alone usually writes, with no symbol only the CPCS or the
  Russian notation writes; a mixed profile is undecided; the CPCS and
  FAO designations give hints through Annex 6, and the data decide;
  never by the country.
- **The vocabulary (default 12):** closed and case-sensitive, by the
  longest match; L, Na, Sa, π and J are overlays and the suffixes
  features; -c is indurated except in Kc, in Xc and after OF or OH; the
  variants of the book are read; FE is read as Fe only in an RP 1995
  profile or with FEm, FEmp or Ahs.
- **The new fields:** the coarse elements by weight in the book’s four
  classes (Q11), the method of the CEC (Q12), relict redox features
  (Q13), the position in the valley, the floods, the polders and a BP
  downslope (Q14), the anthropic materials and history (Q15), the
  qualifiers recorded and the relation to the parent material (Q21), the
  zoogenic O and the humus forms (Q22), and the 21 fields that decide a
  reference horizon (Q23).
- **The readings of the reader, accepted**
  (`inst/rules/rp2008/readings.yaml`): ND, the nodular horizon, is only
  a likely sign of the notation, since databases write ND for “not
  determined”; the suffixes read only on the hosts the book lists
  completely; Ga, Ea and the V variants read as their code with a
  feature; the frozen mark \* of the cryosols; transitions written
  without the hyphen; Roman numerals without a space and a numeral
  written alone; the old codes in any RP profile and as signs of the
  notation; the classes of the symbols beyond those of Q9; the CPCS A2
  used as an E; the sign of the Russian notation; the patterns of Annex
  6 and the table of the FAO letters; the writing of the sequences;
  Latin-1 text.

#### After the review (Hugo, 2026-11-02)

- **Fixes.**
  - V and X written alone are the vertic and peyric horizons, not Roman
    numerals (SV/V, O/X).
  - Ap (formerly L) inside a transition or written with a slash (Ap/C)
    is no sign of the notation and no longer makes the profile one of
    the RP of 1995.
  - A juxtaposition is a sign of the notation only as E&BT or with a
    part that is one: the New Zealand L&F and F&H are not.
  - L is a prefix only before the A, E, S, O, H, BT and BP horizons: LF,
    LC, LR, LM and LD are no RP codes.
  - -ho is a sign only on Aho, Acaho, Sho, Zho, THho and Xho with
    nothing after it, and the frozen \* only a likely one, so the FAO
    runs Ahoc and A\* do not make an RP profile.
  - A prefix written apart joins its master (Na BT, Sa A, p. 296), and
    “+” between two horizons is a juxtaposition (E + A, p. 315).
  - The (B)Ca row of Annex 6 is read, and A1g takes the A1 row.
  - Sub-horizons are numbered from 1: A0, A00, BT0 and S01 are no RP
    writing, and A00 keeps its Annex 6 hint OL.
  - Cs is C with -s, not a symbol of the CPCS only; an Australian A2e is
    no longer called CPCS in the explanation.
  - A mark written twice (Sgg, Rcaca) or -c or -m after a code that says
    indurated (Kcc, OXmc) leaves the designation unread, with a note;
    the suffixes of the book’s complete lists are read only on the codes
    it names (St, Ct, FSt; BTd, Sd; Ea, Ga, ga; noz and zo on OF and
    OH).
  - A transition keeps its sub-horizon digits and the features of each
    part.
  - Thin and narrow spaces, the Windows-1252 en dash, the capital Π,
    “pi” and the capital ẞ are read.
  - Pages corrected in the catalogue: Amg p. 12, Alu p. 78, OXfr p. 151.
  - The units of iron: `fe_total_pct` in % Fe2O3, `fe_dcb_pct` and
    `fe_ffe_pct` in % Fe, and the factor 0.6994 for the ratios of free
    to total iron (Sn 0.60-0.90, FFE over total iron above 0.20).
  - The two fields of the plan that were missing: `lateral_cover_pct`
    (horizon: the share of the ground an O horizon covers, Annex 1) and
    `rp_paleo` (site: the paleosolum terms declared, pp. 58-63).
- **New decisions.**
  - An FAO or USDA symbol beside an RP symbol leaves the notation
    undecided, as a CPCS or Russian symbol does: a B with a lower-case
    suffix (Bw, Bs, Bt …), Oh, Oi, Oe, Oa, Cr, AB or BA, and an Arabic
    numeral of discontinuity (2Cg, 3Bt). The RP transitions A-S, AS and
    BC are not such symbols.
  - In a profile written all in capitals the case is lost: the
    designations an upper-cased FAO, USDA or Canadian table also writes
    (OH, OF, OL, AH, AP, BT, BW, CK, CR …) stop counting as signs, while
    the codes only the RP writes in capitals (LA, LE, LS, LBT, SV, FS,
    OX, RT, FE, BP, ND …) still count. OH/AH/E/BT/C is not the RP;
    LA/BT, SV/V and A/FE/C are. This refines the first reading of the
    decision, under which only a declaration recognised a profile in
    capitals, which lost 48 of the 308 sequences of the book.
  - A lone g, the redox horizon written alone, is a likely sign of the
    notation.
  - `site$designation_system` is read by prefix: a value that starts
    with rp, referentiel or afes declares the RP (AFES 2009, RP08,
    Référentiel pédologique français), rp1995 or rp95 the RP of 1995.
    The Russian reader reads its own declarations the same way (a value
    that starts with kidpr, ru, rfg or rsc); nothing else in it changes.

## soilKey 0.9.340 (2026-11-02)

### Attachment: engine pieces for systems that are not keys

This release prepares the French Referentiel pédologique 2008, which is
not a key: a soil is attached to one, two or none of its references,
simply or imperfectly. It adds the generic pieces that system will use.
No system uses them yet, and every other classification is unchanged.

- **`within_tolerance(value, threshold, direction, tol)`** compares a
  value with a threshold that has a tolerance. It returns “pass”,
  “imperfect” (beyond the threshold but within the tolerance), “fail” or
  NA. The edge of the tolerance band is inside it.
- **Tolerance tables.** A system lists its tolerances by kind of
  threshold (depth, pH, CEC, …), for one threshold or for every
  threshold of a kind. A threshold the table does not list is strict.
- **A tolerant mode of the rule engine.** A class can be evaluated
  twice, strictly and then tolerantly. In the tolerant pass, the
  predicates that read their thresholds through the new helpers see each
  listed threshold moved by its tolerance, in the direction that favours
  the class. Inside a `none_of` block the direction flips: “no BT within
  120 cm” is read within 100 cm, not 140. The two verdicts give the
  degree: simple, imperfect, simple or imperfect (undecided between the
  two), undecided, or fail. The criteria that fail, pass only within
  tolerance, or are missing are named. The mode is off unless a system
  asks for it, and it belongs to that system: a predicate of another
  system, even one run from inside the tolerant pass, reads its
  thresholds as printed. So every other system runs as before. A class
  that passes strictly is simple. A threshold must be one known number;
  a tolerance table is always checked.
- **The attachment combiner** chooses the main name among the classes
  that attach. Exclusions come first, resolved together: only a class
  that is not excluded excludes another. The explicit precedence rules
  come next, then the degree (simple before imperfect), then an order
  list. A double or multiple name is written only for a listed group, in
  the group’s order. A class that could take the name once its data are
  known makes the name provisional, read at the best degree it can still
  reach. When nothing attaches, the name says so and the three nearest
  classes are listed. Codes in the rules that name no class are noted.
- **A `candidates` slot** in the classification result holds every class
  that may attach the soil, with its degree, rank and criteria. It is
  empty for every other system, and printing and the summary are
  unchanged unless it is filled.
- **An additive level with no typical class.** `typical = NULL` adds no
  “typical” label when nothing is named, for systems that have none.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **The band edge counts inside.** Against “no BT within 120 cm” (120 ±
  20), a BT at exactly 100 cm is imperfect; at 99 cm it fails.
- **Provisional.** An undecided class that could take the name makes the
  name provisional.
- **Exclusion by an undecided class.** The excluded class stays a
  candidate, and the name is provisional. Classes that exclude each
  other are all kept, with a note.
- **Precedence cycles.** Pairs on a cycle are dropped, with a note; the
  degree and the order decide. When the pairs and the degrees disagree,
  a note says the order is a convention.
- **Distance.** The nearest classes are ranked by the number of failed
  criteria, then by the sum of the failures in tolerance units.
- **Candidates.** Undecided classes are always in the candidates; failed
  ones only as the nearest, when nothing attaches.

## soilKey 0.9.339 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the types of the divisions CK to CT

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) gains the types of
the ten divisions CK to CT: 111 types, matched as the types of CA to CJ
are (0.9.338). Every division of trunk C now has its types but the
chemozems (CU), which have none. Every other classification is
unchanged.

- **The 111 types** in `inst/rules/kidpr2008/types/`: CK 12
  (solonetzes), CL 3 (solonchaks), CM 4 (hydrometamorphic), CN 9
  (organo-accumulative), CO 11 (eluvozems), CP 13 (lithozems), CQ 10
  (abrazems), CR 13 (agroabrazems), CS 19 (agrozems), CT 17 (turbozems).
  Each has soilKey’s code in brackets (\[CK01\] to \[CT17\], in the
  order of chapter 4), the Russian name as printed (two slips of the
  diagrams, Агрослонцы and Сухотофяно-литоземы, as chapter 6 writes
  them), an English gloss, the formula as the fixture of the formulas
  transcribes it, and the page.
- **What the formulas test (Q14).** The BCA under the solonetz horizon
  (BCAs,cs) is optional, in the solonetzes, the solonetzic abrazems,
  agrozems and turbozems. The hard rock R of the lithozems is tested,
  with its carbonate mark where the formula writes it without
  parentheses (Rca: the carbolithozems CP10, CP11). The gleyed substrate
  DG of the gley eluvozems is tested; the D of the others is not. The
  fragments of a TUR (TUR\[SEL+ASN\]) are tested.
- **The fragments of a TUR (Q20)** come from the notation or from the
  column `turbated_fragments` (“SEL;ASN”); with neither, the solonetzic
  types are undecided when the TUR has a high exchangeable sodium, and
  the TUR is not theirs otherwise.
- **Near-identity readings (Q15):** S over Q is a gley solonchak (CL01);
  a BT exposed or under PB is read as BI (CQ01, CR04, CR05); the BH of
  CR07 and CS10 is a BHF of either kind.
- **Doubles.** Two formulas match one profile only where one names what
  the other leaves out: O-EL-DG is CO02 with CO01 its intergrade
  (likewise CO04 and CO03, CO10 and CO09), AU-Cca-Rca is CP11 with CP06
  its intergrade (likewise CP10 and CP09), PB-BM-BCA is CR09 with CR08
  its intergrade.
- Every chapter 4 formula of CK to CT, written as a profile in the
  Russian notation, reaches its own division and its own type, decided,
  with and without its optional horizons, except CS16 and CS17 without
  their BCA: a thin TUR of solonetz fragments under P or PU over the
  parent material has no division (C.6а). One undesignated profile per
  division reaches its type through the key to horizons on the data.
- **An exposed BT is an abrazem.** At C.20 a BT at the surface, with no
  humus, organic, agro or eluvial horizon above it and the description
  starting at 0 cm, counts as BI. This changes a division result of
  0.9.337 and 0.9.338: BT over C, which had no division (“not
  provided”), is now an abrazem (CQ), type CQ01.
- **The secondary solonchaks.** In the types of the halomorphic soils an
  S or SS laid over another horizon counts as the S of the formula: AY+S
  over C is CL03, AU+S over G or Q is CL01. The key to divisions sends
  these profiles to CL as before; outside CL an overlay stays a feature
  of its layer.
- **The review of the types of CK to CT.** On the data route the gleyed
  substrate of the gley eluvozems and the carbonate rock of the
  carbolithozems are read from the data (a gley colour or a redox sign;
  a carbonate rock named or effervescence), undecided when not recorded,
  so CO02, CO04, CO05, CO08, CO10, CO11, CP10 and CP11 are reachable
  there. The missing data of an undecided type name `turbated_fragments`
  when the fragments of a TUR are what is unknown. A formula that starts
  with SEL, S, a middle horizon or TUR leaves out a natural organic or
  humus horizon at the top that no formula of its division writes (a
  thin O or an AY over SEL-ASN is CK01) and is closed on one another
  formula writes (AU-SEL-BSN has no type). The post-solonetzic turbozems
  are tried with the agro types.
- **Known limitation** (as in 0.9.338): a description that ends in a
  horizon decides the type that needs nothing below it (O-EL with no
  substrate described is an eluvozem, PU-TUR a dark turbozem).

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **Secondary solonchaks:** the secondary solonchaks form over any
  profile (pp. 56, 105), so in the types of CL an overlay S is the S of
  the formula; the \[ABC\] of CL03 is any formed profile, not tested.
- **Exposed BT:** the near-identity of Q15 (a BT exposed is BI) holds at
  the key to divisions too, at C.20, with the guard of Q19.
- **The fragments of TUR:** every fragment a formula writes must be
  among those of the TUR (TUR\[SEL+ASN\] at the surface is no CT14);
  with no record of them, the type is undecided when the TUR has an ESP
  of 15 % or more and the TUR is not one of these otherwise.
- **The five doubles** (CO02 and CO01, CO04 and CO03, CO10 and CO09,
  CP10 and CP09, CP11 and CP06): the more specific names the type, the
  other is an intergrade.
- **A division and no type:** the profiles the literal rules leave
  without a type stay so, with the note of Q15: TJ over C (CN), V at the
  surface (CQ), O, T or PT over Q, AU-SEL-BSN, AU-ASN without SEL, PB or
  PU over BSN; a horizon foreign to the division under the plough is
  ignored (PB over BFM is CR01); CS16 and CS17 without their BCA have no
  division; on the data a carbonate layer directly under the plough is
  read as AJ.
- **On the review (2026-11-02):** in the turbozems every middle horizon
  of C.5 closes the formulas (P-TUR-BHF-C, PU-TUR-V-C and PU-TUR-BM-C
  have no type) and BT counts as BI in CT05 to CT08; a BCA is ignored in
  the formulas of CQ, CR, CS and CT that have a middle horizon and do
  not write BCA (BI-BCA-Cca is CQ01, PU-BM-BCA CS12, PU-BI-BCA CS13), as
  in CD; a plain TUR (CT01 to CT13) is no TUR of solonetz fragments; the
  G or Q of CL01 and CL02 lies directly under the S; CT13 takes PTR as
  well as PT; P directly over BCA is CS14. A surface horizon over a
  formula that starts with no surface horizon closes it when another
  formula of the division writes it (AU, AJ in CK) and is left out when
  none does (O, AY): AU-SEL-ASN is CK05 only, AU-SEL-BSN has no type.
  The BCA rule brings the double CR09 and CR08, CR09 naming the type.

## soilKey 0.9.338 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the types of the divisions CA to CJ

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) names its types by
the formula of the profile, drawn in chapter 4. This release adds the
type level for the ten divisions CA to CJ: 106 types, matched on the
diagnostic horizons the divisions read. The other divisions keep the
division as the name until their types follow. Every other
classification is unchanged.

- **The type level.** After the division,
  [`classify_kidpr2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_kidpr2008.md)
  matches the profile against every formula of the division with
  [`match_horizon_sequence()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/match_horizon_sequence.md),
  three-valued. The profile is the one the divisions read: fresh litter
  left out, the profile under a deposit of 40 cm or less, the surface
  horizons by the thickest-horizon rule (p. 37), sub-horizons merged,
  transitions and small horizons left out, an overlay a feature of its
  layer. The type is the third level of the result, with soilKey’s
  English gloss in `name` and the Russian name in `levels$name_native`.
  An undecided type tried before the one assigned makes the name
  provisional; with none matched and some undecided, the name stops at
  the division and the warnings name the candidates.
- **The 106 types** in `inst/rules/kidpr2008/types/`: CA 27, CB 17, CC
  3, CD 13, CE 7, CF 4, CG 3, CH 9, CI 20, CJ 3. Each has a code of
  soilKey’s in brackets (\[CA01\] to \[CJ03\], in the order of chapter
  4, the natural types first), the Russian name as printed, an English
  gloss, the formula as the fixture of the formulas transcribes it, and
  the page. The test of each is the new predicate
  [`type_formula_kidpr()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/kidpr2008_types.md).
- **A combination no formula provides for** keeps its division. The type
  is unassigned, a warning says the Field Guide of 2008 does not provide
  for it, and the three nearest formulas by edit distance are in that
  warning and in the trace (phase `types_nearest`).
- **Intergrades.** When two formulas match, the more specific names the
  type; the other is named in the evidence and in the warnings. Among
  the formulas of CA to CJ this happens only for AY-BEL-BM, where CD09
  names the type and CD01 is the intergrade, and for AU-BM-BCA, where
  CD08 names it and CD03 is the intergrade.
- **Fixes of the review.** A tie or a missing thickness among the
  organic and humus horizons at the surface, or an undecided layer that
  could make one of them the thickest, now leaves the type undecided
  between its candidates (O 10 cm over AY 10 cm over EL-BEL-BT is CA01
  or CA04); the type no longer follows one reading silently. On the data
  route an FAO transition (BC, B/C) or an FAO C layer between two
  horizons is passed over, as the divisions do: Ah-Eg-Btg-BC-Bg is CA05.
  A nearest formula that only a gap blocks says so in the note.
- **The stratified body of the stratozems** counts P and PU only over
  the first RJ, RY or RU, as the agro stratozems draw them (P-RY-D,
  PU-RU-D). This changes a division result of 0.9.337: RY 12 cm over
  P-EL-BEL-BT, or over PU-AU-BCA, is no longer a stratozem (BC) but CA17
  or CI11.
- **A V laid over another horizon** is a feature of its layer for the
  key to divisions too. This changes a division result of 0.9.337: AU
  over G+V is a gley soil (CH, type CH04), not a humus-accumulative
  soil.
- **The matcher** takes a new option, `agro_remnant = "thickest"`: under
  an agro horizon only the thickest natural horizon of the surface run
  stays in the sequence, as its remnant, and the others are features.
  The default keeps the old behaviour. A list of schemes may also be
  closed on a vocabulary per scheme.
- Every chapter 4 formula of CA to CJ, written as a profile in the
  Russian notation, reaches its own division and its own type, decided.
  So do the profiles without their optional horizons, except CA24
  without its EL: P directly over BT is an agrozem. One undesignated
  profile per division reaches its type through the key to horizons on
  the data.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **Closed formulas (Q13):** every horizon that some formula of the
  division writes must be in the type’s formula when it is in the
  profile; a horizon foreign to the division is ignored and may name a
  subtype. Most specific first, agro before natural; a second match is
  an intergrade.
- **BEL closes only where it is diagnostic:** BEL blocks a formula that
  does not write it only in the types where page 44 makes it diagnostic
  (CA07, CA08, CA11, CA20, CA21, CD09). In every other formula a BEL is
  read as part of the passage from the eluvial to the middle horizon: it
  neither blocks the formula nor is required by it. So AU-EL-BEL-BT-G-CG
  is CA10, AY-EL-BEL-BT-BCA-Cca CA12, PU-EL-BEL-BT-G-CG CA23 and
  AY-EL-BEL-BM-C CD07, while AY-EL-BEL-BT-C stays CA04, AU-BEL-BT-C CA07
  and AY-BEL-BT-C CA11. The key to divisions already keeps a BEL apart
  from the clay-illuvial chernozems: AU-BEL-BT is CA07, AU-BI is CI02,
  AU-BEL-BI has no division.
- **What a formula tests (Q14):** a horizon in parentheses is optional;
  BEL is required only where it is the diagnostic eluvial horizon (CA07,
  CA08, CA11, CA20, CA21, CD09); the g and q marks are expected, not
  required; the parent material is not tested; directly under passes
  over transitions and sub-horizons, with up to 15 cm with no diagnostic
  horizon between AU and BCA.
- **No type (Q15):** the division stays and the type is unassigned, with
  the nearest formulas and a note. The near-identity readings: the BF of
  CB05, CE06 and CE07, and the BH of the gley Al-Fe-humus soils, are a
  BHF of either kind; CJ01 takes BCA or CAT; CH02 takes O, T or H over
  G-CRM.
- **A layer with no horizon** on the data, between two horizons of a
  formula, may be a transition or loose rock: the type is undecided,
  with its candidates, not unassigned. Up to 15 cm of it between AU and
  BCA is still passed over.
- **E and EL in CB and CE:** an EL counts as an eluvial horizon with E.
  It fills the E of a formula (O-EL-BHF-C is CB07, O-EL-CRM-C is CE05)
  and blocks the formulas without E (no podbur CB01, no CE01); with no
  formula with E, the type is unassigned (Q15).
- **BCA in CD:** like BEL, a BCA neither blocks a formula of CD that
  does not write it nor is required by it (p. 85): AY-BM-BCA-Cca is
  CD01, AO-BM-BCA CD02; CD08 and CD13 still win where they match.
- **Overlays at the division key:** only a V that is the horizon of its
  own layer is a middle horizon; a V laid over another horizon is a
  feature (G+V under AU is CH04). The overlays S and X count as before.
- **The stratified body:** P and PU count only over the stratified
  horizons.
- **The readings of the types** (`readings.yaml`): the T of a formula
  takes TO and TE; a natural humus or organic horizon of the surface run
  that a formula does not write stays out of the closure, and under the
  plough the thickest natural horizon is the remnant; an overlay (S, X
  or V over a host) is a feature for the types, not a horizon of the
  formula; at equal specificity the agro types come before the natural
  ones, then the order of chapter 4.

## soilKey 0.9.337 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the registry entry, the trunks and the 27 divisions

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) joins the registry
as `kidpr2008` (aliases kidpr, russia, ru2008), experimental and opt-in:
[`classify_all()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_all.md)
does not run it unless asked, so every other classification is
unchanged. This release keys the five trunks (key 2.2) and the 27
divisions (key 2.3) on the diagnostic horizons of the profile, from the
Russian notation where the profile is written in it, else from the key
to horizons on the data (0.9.335-0.9.336); the types and subtypes
follow.

- **[`classify_kidpr2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_kidpr2008.md)**
  and
  **[`make_kidpr2008_example()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_kidpr2008_example.md)**
  (one small profile in the Russian notation per division). The result
  names the division (or the trunk), with an English gloss in `name` and
  the Russian of the book in `levels$name_native`; a profile that is not
  a soil (trunk E), a thin layer of loose rock over hard rock, and a
  combination of horizons the Field Guide does not provide for are noted
  in the warnings, the division unassigned.
- **The keys flattened** (`inst/rules/kidpr2008/key.yaml` and
  `divisions/`): each trunk and division is a first-match entry whose
  gate is the conjunction of the conditions of the book’s path to it
  (less what an earlier entry of the list excludes), written with the
  path (C.4а-C.5а-C.6б-C.7а); the steps of the key to divisions are
  written once and named by the gates. The trunks E, D, A, B, C; trunk
  A: AB, AA; trunk B: BA, BB, BC; trunk C: CP, CL, CU, CQ, CO, CN, CT,
  CR, CS, CC, CF, CG, CH, CE, CJ, CK, CB, CA, CD, CI, CM; trunk D:
  \[DA\], the division the book does not code.
- **The predicates** (internal, `_kidpr`): a horizon present, starting
  the profile, the surface horizon, directly over another, below
  another, the profile made only of some horizons, hard rock within 30
  cm, a TUR over 40 cm, the peat body, the deposit at the surface, the
  stratified humus body, a soil horizon within 1 m, a river floodplain
  on modern alluvium, volcanic ash and the contaminated horizon X,
  three-valued, reading the frame of
  `identify_horizons(pedon, "kidpr2008")` once per classification.
- A literal walker of keys 2.2 and 2.3, with its own reading of the
  profile, is the test oracle of the flattened lists: on every
  combination of the tested horizon-presence space they agree once the
  repairs below are applied, and every difference from the literal key
  is one of them. A sample of that space is also classified end to end
  as pedons in the Russian notation, and a set of common soils of Russia
  on the data route. Every profile formula of chapter 4 reaches its own
  division.
- The level labels Trunk and Division (EN, PT) in the app and the
  report; the app offers the 27 examples; the site attributes
  `frost_regime` and `designation_system`, and `landform`,
  `landform_element`, `parent_material` and `contaminated`, name the
  system that reads them.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **Levels and registry (Q1, Q2):** trunks and divisions now, types and
  subtypes later; trunk E is not a soil (rock outcrops, technogenic
  surface formations, a deposit that is not humified over a buried
  soil), with a note, and the chapter 8 groups are not keyed; id
  `kidpr2008`, namespace `kidpr`; the codes of the book, \[DA\] for the
  uncoded division of trunk D.
- **Precedence (Q9):** the printed order of the steps and of their
  alternatives (C.7: BFM, BPL, CR, CRM, BMK, ASN or BSN; C.8: BHF, BT,
  BM); C.19в before C.19а (P with AY and PU with AU are
  organo-accumulative soils); C.6б over C.6а when BFM, BPL, CRM, CR, CRH
  or BMK is in the profile (P-G-CRM is a gley soil); an agro horizon
  with no natural remnant on alluvium is an agrozem (p. 124).
- **Gaps (Q10):** only those the book’s types prove are repaired: AY and
  AK at C.2, PT and PTR at C.19а, AK at C.19в, a TUR over 40 cm tested
  at C.6 and a TUR at the surface counted at C.4, trunk D taking an S
  alone over loose rock, AY or AO directly over G to the gley soils;
  every other combination with no exit is “not provided by the Field
  Guide of 2008”, the division unassigned, with a note.
- **The surface, the sources (Q11, Q12):** the agro horizon, else the
  thickest of the natural organic and humus horizons that start the
  profile (a W of 5 cm or less over another horizon is a feature);
  division names from the chapter 4 headings, the index and key forms as
  synonyms.
- **Truncated, turbated, synlithogenic, peat, chemozems (Q19-Q23):** a
  middle horizon at the surface counts only when the description starts
  at 0 cm; the turbozems need a TUR over 40 cm; trunk B takes only what
  one of its divisions takes (a floodplain with alluvial material; BAN;
  a stratified humus body of 40 cm or more, P and PU counted), and the
  deposit of step 2 is the material at the surface that is not a horizon
  formed in it; the peat body of more than 50 cm sums the contiguous
  organic layers, H, PT and PTR included, a description ending in peat
  at 50 cm or less undecided; the chemozems only at C.3б, after the
  lithozems and the halomorphic soils, X from the extremely hazardous
  category within 30 cm.
- **soilKey’s readings, accepted** (`readings.yaml`): V and CRH count
  among the middle horizons of C.5 (the types CI04, CI05, CI14, CI15
  have no other); a profile C.6 gives no answer (an agro horizon on ASN
  or BSN, the agro-solonetzes CK09-CK12) goes on to C.7; the peat T of
  the key’s lists includes TO and TE; the surface S or SS of C.3 starts
  within 10 cm; loose rock belongs to the deposit only over a buried
  soil or an organic or humus horizon (TPO and the deposit of the data
  always), and a buried soil directly under a thin deposit is the soil
  keyed; a valley, alluvial plain or delta landform leaves the
  floodplain undecided; P or PU at C.19а is read as present; each gate
  leaves out the exclusions an earlier entry of the list supplies, so
  that an undecided class makes the one after it provisional. Every
  reading in `readings.yaml` is now one of Hugo’s decisions.

#### After the review (Hugo, 2026-11-02)

- **Fixes.**
  - TPO, and the deposit the key to horizons finds on the data, belong
    to the deposit at the surface: TPO or a raw deposit over 40 cm on a
    soil is trunk E, not a soil.
  - A layer the data leave undecided between peat horizons counts in the
    peat body, and step 6 no longer asks for the decomposition or the
    von Post value it does not need.
  - A layer the data leave undecided between soil horizons is a soil
    horizon for step 1, so such profiles are no longer provisional on
    trunk E.
  - A layer in which the key on the data finds no diagnostic horizon may
    be a transition: it no longer proves that the profile has no soil
    horizon, so the canonical plinthosol is no longer trunk E. Rock, TPO
    and a deposit still do.
  - FAO and WRB transitions (AB, BC, E/B and the like) are passed over
    as those of the Russian notation are. A chernozem Ah-AB-Bk is a
    humus-accumulative soil on both routes.
  - A missing depth or thickness leaves the step that needs it
    undecided: hard rock, a surface salt horizon or a contaminated layer
    of unknown depth, and the thickest-horizon rule with a thickness
    missing. No R warning any more.
  - The texts of the site are read as words. A terrace is no floodplain,
    glaciofluvial material and outwash are no alluvium, and outwash or
    washed sand is no volcanic ash.
  - The peat body is more than 50 cm, as the book says.
    [`classify_kidpr2008()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_kidpr2008.md)
    says it needs a PedonRecord when it is given something else.
  - A description that starts with fresh litter at 0 cm starts at 0 cm
    for a truncated soil.
  - The test oracle reads the profile on its own. Its space now holds
    TPO, the deposit of the data, transitions, layers with no diagnostic
    horizon and an O thicker than the humus horizon under it.
- **New decisions.**
  - BAN is formed in volcanic ash by its definition, so BAN alone makes
    the volcanic soils: H-BAN-C is BB, by the notation or by the key on
    the data.
  - Step 5 of the key to trunks reads the profile after the
    thickest-horizon rule, as C.2 and C.19 do. O over a thinner humus
    horizon is only O, a weakly developed soil, and O with W needs no
    repair.
  - Every ploughed soil of the iron-metamorphic (CC) and light-humus
    carbonate-accumulative (CJ) divisions is an agrozem (CS), or an
    agroabrazem (CR) under PB, with or without a remnant of the natural
    horizon (pp. 83, 99). P-AJ-BCA, P-AY-BFM and P-AJ-BM-BCA are
    agrozems, PB-BFM an agroabrazem. This replaces the reading of an
    agro horizon directly over BFM or BMK.
  - On the data route an FAO or WRB transition counts as a transition
    only when the key to horizons finds no diagnostic horizon in it. AE
    read as AEL and EB read as BEL keep their horizon, so the grey
    forest soil keeps its division (CA06).
  - On the data route a layer designated C (C, Cg, 2Ck) in which the key
    to horizons finds no diagnostic horizon is loose rock, one of the
    readings key position 66 lists.
  - C.14 reads “directly under”, as C.13 does. The key prints “under”,
    but the text of the gley soils (p. 92) puts G directly under the
    organic or humus horizon and leaves out a profile with any other
    mineral horizon, and the text decides. O-BI-G is not provided by the
    Field Guide of 2008.
  - BMK stays out of C.5: AJ-BMK-C is not provided.

## soilKey 0.9.336 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the diagnostic horizons on the data

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) identifies the
diagnostic horizons of a profile by a key of 66 positions (section 2.1).
This release runs that key on the recorded data, so that every layer
gets its Russian horizon where the profile is not written in the Russian
notation, with soilKey’s WRB diagnostics standing in where a field
descriptor of the key is missing. Nothing is classified yet, so every
classification is unchanged; the registry entry with the trunks and
divisions follows.

- **The key 2.1** (internal; the horizon identification
  [`identify_horizons()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/identify_horizons.md)
  dispatches to once the registry entry exists). The 66 positions in the
  book’s order, each a question on the layer and on the whole profile
  (the layers above and below, the depth of a boundary, frost in the
  profile). It reaches the 50 horizons, the modifications AV, BH and BF,
  the peat as rock TT, the features u, tr, rh, r, ao, e, el and ca, and
  no diagnostic horizon (position 66). The overlays S, X and V are kept
  beside the horizon of the layer; one left undecided leaves only the
  overlay undecided. Two answers the key gives no exit (a mixed layer
  neither TUR nor tr; continuous effervescence with cutans and no
  white-eye) leave the layer undecided between their neighbours. In a
  profile dark from a dark rock, a middle horizon gets the feature u and
  goes on at 31.
- **One row per layer**: the horizon and its modification, overlays,
  features, small horizons (e, el, ao, r, rh), the route (notation, data
  or both), the path of the key in the book’s notation, the evidence,
  the WRB diagnostics that stood in and the fallbacks used, and, when
  undecided, the candidates and the attributes that would decide it. A
  layer written in the Russian notation keeps its horizon; the key runs
  on its data too, and a reading that differs goes to the evidence.
  Designations in other notations give hints only; fresh litter is no
  horizon; hard rock is R.
- **The readers** (internal): the colour words of the key in Munsell,
  the Kachinsky gradations of texture and the clay ratio, acid or not,
  the salts and the pollutants, the organic matter, the decomposition,
  the carbonates, frost, ploughing and the surface deposit, each
  three-valued and noting the fallback it used. soilKey’s cambic horizon
  also stands in for the transformed structure of BM, and its andic
  properties for the volcanic ash of BAN; a layer under pH(H2O) 7.0 is
  read as holding no free carbonates when no effervescence is recorded,
  and a layer with a particle-size analysis, CaCO3 or a mineral bulk
  density but no carbon as mineral.
- **The fixes of the review.** A grey layer under an organic layer, or
  one continuing the surface horizon, is a humus horizon only when it
  looks like one (not gley or olive, not massive, single-grained or
  stratified, not frozen, darker than the parent material), so the CRM,
  CR or G under the O of a cryozem or a gleyzem, a pale soil’s BPL and
  layered alluvium are no longer read as AY or AJ. The light horizon is
  compared with the middle horizon under the BEL. The argic stand-in
  gives no cutans to massive layers, carbonate layers or layers outside
  the clay maximum; the solonetz structure comes only from a columnar
  structure recorded in the layer’s run; the carbonate neoformations not
  recorded are read by calcic(), protocalcic_properties() or the
  carbonate maximum of the solum. The Soviet plough layer (Apakh, Ap
  with a Cyrillic p) and a clear plough boundary are read; the site’s
  mixing depth no longer makes the plough layer mixed. With equal values
  the lower chroma is the lighter layer; CRM is dull (chroma 3 or less)
  with a cryogenic structure; BMK needs the effervescence; a rich
  granular AU is no AH; a film colour must be brighter than the parent
  material; AK must be strictly the darkest; a natural surface layer
  lighter than the humus horizon under it is a deposit (criterion 3 of
  position 8); Russian texture words are read in either order.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **Without the notation (Q4):** the key runs on the attributes; where a
  field descriptor is missing a soilKey WRB diagnostic stands in,
  flagged: spodic() for the iron films of BHF, argic() for the cutans of
  BT and BI, calcic() for the carbonate neoformations of BCA, the
  structure of natric_horizon() for ASN and BSN (the exchangeable sodium
  never decides). An undecided question follows every branch: one
  outcome gives the horizon, several leave it undecided with the
  candidates.
- **Colours (Q5):** dry Munsell, one cut-point per binary choice of the
  key (dark: value 4 or less, chroma 2 or less; grey: chroma 3 or less
  in 10YR, 2.5Y, 5Y or N, 7.5YR only at chroma 2 or less; whitish: value
  7 or more, chroma 2 or less); dry value = moist value + 1 when only
  the moist colour is recorded, flagged; the gley, olive and solonetz
  colours read moist, the gley set the whole gley chart.
- **Organic matter (Q6):** humus = 1.724 x OC; LOI from `loi_pct`, else
  1.724 x OC; decomposition from `peat_decomposition_pct`, else von Post
  (H7 or more, H4 or less), else the rubbed fibre (under 17 %, 40 % or
  more); between them undecided.
- **Texture (Q7):** the Kachinsky gradations from `phys_clay_pct` or
  `texture_class_ru`, else the USDA classes in order of fineness, one
  step one gradation, flagged; BT against BI by the clay ratio of 1.4 to
  the overlying humus or eluvial horizon.
- **Salts and pH (Q8):** `soluble_salts_pct`, else the EC of chapter 9
  (ECe 16 dS/m, EC 1:5 2 dS/m), else a salt crust or efflorescences
  recorded at the surface; pH(KCl) alone acid under 5.0, not acid from
  6.2.
- **The surface (Q11), the sources (Q12):** a horizon starts at the
  surface at the top of the mineral soil, under the agro layers or under
  the deposit; exact boundary values follow the key’s inequality (e 2 cm
  or less, O 10 cm or less, el 5 cm or less, salts over 1 %, a humified
  deposit of 40 cm a horizon, a raw one a feature).
- **Ploughing (Q18):** the Russian index, else the plough suffix p in
  the layers from the surface, else a tilled land use with an abrupt
  boundary within 40 cm; a designated profile with no plough mark is
  natural, a profile with no designation and no land use undecided.
- **TUR (Q20), the deposit (Q21), peat (Q22), X (Q23):** TUR from
  `foreign_fragments_pct` (80 % or more) or the site’s mixing depth,
  flagged; the deposit is the mineral material over a buried soil, or a
  layered deposit at the surface, never a humus horizon formed in it; TO
  and TE in the upper 50 cm of the peat, TT below, TJ by the value
  mesophilic; X from `contamination_hazard`, the site’s contamination
  without a category undecided.
- **Frost (position 26, the review):** `frost_regime` first; else frozen
  ground in the profile (ice, a temperature of 0 C or less, the
  permafrost sign, the FAO frozen suffix, cryoturbation) yes; else the
  Koppen climate (D with c or d, ET, EF yes; A, C, D with a or b, BWh,
  BSh no; BWk and BSk undecided); else the soil temperature regime
  (cryic, gelic, pergelic yes; mesic or warmer no; frigid undecided);
  else a mean annual air temperature over 5 C no; nothing recorded,
  undecided. Latitude does not decide; the route is flagged.
- **After the review (Hugo, 2026-11-02):** no free carbonates under
  pH(H2O) 7.0 when no effervescence is recorded; carbonate neoformations
  not recorded read as the carbonate maximum of the solum (calcic() or
  protocalcic_properties() passing, or the layer with more carbonate
  than every layer above, at least as much as those below except the
  parent material, and 1 % or more), not for the parent material,
  undecided otherwise; Koppen BWk and BSk fall through to the soil
  temperature regime and the air temperature; a film horizon neither BFM
  nor fading is BHF; GY, G, BG, B and PB above chroma 1 need a structure
  or a redox sign as 2.5Y does; plant residues count above 5 %; LOI
  10-15 % with a crumb or granular structure is AU; the clay maximum is
  90 % of the highest argic clay; the site’s mixing depth is undecided
  when ploughing is.
- **Litter (Hugo, 2026-11-02):** an FAO Oi or L is fresh litter only in
  a run of such layers that starts the description and is 5 cm thick or
  less (a run with no recorded thickness stays litter); thicker, or
  lower in the profile, it is an organic layer the key reads on the
  data, so a raised bog described Oi/Oe is peat and 40 cm of Oi over a
  gleyed layer is T. The Soviet A00 stays litter.
- **The peat body of positions 41 and 44 (the review):** only weakly
  decomposed peat, without H, PT or PTR, as the key writes it (the 51 cm
  body of the organogenic trunk keeps them).
- **Gley in 2.5Y (the review):** with 2.5Y at chroma 2-3 a G needs a
  massive or structureless structure or a recorded redox sign (mottles,
  redox features, a dipyridyl test); the rest of the gley chart (N, and
  GY, G, BG, B, PB at chroma 1) suffices by colour.
- **Defaults:** the agro horizon by the colour of position 19 (PU dark;
  P grey as Q5 reads it, chroma 3 or less in 10YR, 2.5Y, 5Y or N, with a
  dry value of 5 or more, so 10YR 5/3 is P; PB the others; 15a allows a
  brown tint); V by slickensides, wedge-shaped peds and clay 30 % or
  more within 80 cm, one or two of the signs the feature v; continuous
  effervescence by `effervescence_extent`, else CaCO3, else the
  effervescence class; white-eye = soft concretions; field observations
  not recorded are absent, measurements not recorded leave their
  question undecided; field-only criteria are evidence.

## soilKey 0.9.335 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the notation of the Field Guide of 2008

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) writes its
horizons in a notation of its own (AY, EL, BEL, BTg, BCAs,cs) and names
its types by profile formulas in it. This release adds the reader of
that notation, the catalogues of its horizons and features, and the
fields its horizon key will read. Nothing is classified yet, so every
classification is unchanged; the horizon key on the data, then the
registry entry with the trunks and divisions, follow.

- **The notation reader** (internal). Each designation is read into its
  horizon and features: small horizons written alone (O-e-BHF-C),
  bracketed features (\[hh\], \[e-hf\], \[akl\], also on a host:
  AJ\[akl\]), turbated mixtures (\[AY, EL\]tr, TUR\[SEL+ASN\]), a
  remnant in parentheses ((EL)), the modifications BH, BF and AV, the
  rock flags (CG, CQ, DG), the rock marks (C, C”, C, C”“, C=, C..), a
  lithological layer (2BM, IIBT), sub-horizons (BT1, BT2), transitions
  (AUBM, AU/BM, BC), a buried horizon in brackets (\[AU\], \[BTg\]) and
  an overlay written after a”+” (AU+S). A row it cannot read gets the
  hints of the FAO letters, and each reading it had to make is noted (a
  note after a space, a trailing “?”, a bracket that is no feature of
  the catalogue read by its parts). Text that is not valid UTF-8 is read
  as Windows-1251, the Cyrillic code page, when it can be, else left
  unread; nothing stops with an error.
- **The catalogues** `inst/rules/kidpr2008/horizons.yaml` and
  `features.yaml`: the 50 diagnostic horizons (Russian name as printed,
  an English gloss, the chapter 3 group, the path of the horizon key,
  the page), the modifications AV, BH and BF, the alias PC, the rock
  symbols C, D, CLM, R, TT and TPO (technogenic surface formations), the
  marks and the four tokens of the chapter 6 formulas (AM, AKL, PY, TR);
  the 64 features of section 3.2 and the three indices only the chapter
  4 lists use (w, x, rx), with their aliases, their host horizons and
  the host-bound forms of the lists (ELf, Th, Tote, AUlc-BCAmc …). Every
  profile formula of chapter 4 (275) and of the chapter 6
  correlation (266) parses with them, with no unknown token; 478 of them
  are recognised as Russian with no declaration (the other 63 are
  written only with letters other notations share).
- **The WRB cryic conditions** read a profile declared in the Russian
  notation by its permafrost sign, not by an f, which is ferruginated
  there (ELf); no other profile changes.
- The split of a run of features written without commas (internal, the
  formula parser) takes linear time; a long run that could not be split
  took seconds to minutes.
- **New fields.** Horizon: `phys_clay_pct` and `texture_class_ru` (the
  Kachinsky texture), `loi_pct` and `peat_decomposition_pct` (the
  organic horizons), `plant_residues_pct`, `uncoated_grains_pct`,
  `effervescence_extent`, `sulfide_odour`, `slickensides_size` and
  `cryoturbation` (positions of the horizon key),
  `foreign_fragments_pct` and `turbated_fragments` (turbated layers),
  `contamination_hazard` and `pollutants` (the contaminated horizon X).
  Site: `frost_regime`. The value `mesophilic` of `peat_moor_type`, and
  the Russian names of `site$designation_system` (kidpr, kidpr2008, ru,
  ru2004, ru2008, russian, russia, rfg2008, rsc2004).

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)

- **Notations (Q3):** only the Russian notation of 2004/2008 gives the
  profile type: declared in `site$designation_system`, or recognised by
  an index only it writes (AY, AU, EL, BEL, BHF, BCA, PU, TUR …) or a
  sign only it writes (the permafrost sign, a rock mark, a
  comma-separated feature list, a bracketed feature), once the Cyrillic
  letters that look like Latin ones are read as Latin; never by the
  country. FAO letters (Ap, Bt, Bs, Bk) only give hints to the key on
  the data, and so does the Soviet notation of 1977 (A0, A1, A2, Bca);
  in a profile with its numbered tokens, AO is the Soviet A0. In a
  profile written all in capitals, the indices an upper-cased FAO
  designation could spell (AY, EL, BEL …) count while the rows that read
  as FAO ones (AP, BW, BTG) are not more numerous, and the capitals
  after an index are then features (BTG = BT + g); PU, PT, TUR, SEL, TO
  … always count. AH, AK, AO, BH and BF count only where the case of the
  letters is kept, or beside an index no FAO master starts (P, G, T …).
- **The notation (defaults 8 to 13):** the Cyrillic look-alikes are
  folded and the permafrost sign is read in both its forms; the aliases
  tr = tu, ek = ko, agr = ag, ae = ael, cs = as and PB = PC are read as
  the first; Tote is TO with te; the tokens AM and AKL of chapter 6 are
  read; a lithological layer is numbered in Arabic or Roman figures; a
  layer may hold a horizon and an overlay S, X or V; small horizons are
  marked rows, sub-horizons are merged and transitions are not
  diagnostic; a feature string without commas is read by the longest
  match, with a note where it could be read otherwise (hi, gr, md, mr,
  rh, ur, yu, hh, ff, rr, rx, hf, agr); a feature written alone is a
  small horizon only where the text allows it (e, el, ao, ek, r …, not
  g, s, ca or v); CG, CQ and DG are a gleyed or quasi-gleyed rock, not a
  G or Q horizon; the printing slips of the keys are corrected.
- **The new fields (Q6, Q7, Q20, Q22, Q23, Q24):** the Kachinsky texture
  (`phys_clay_pct`, `texture_class_ru`), the loss on ignition and the
  degree of decomposition, the fragments of a turbated layer and their
  horizons, the hazard category and the pollutants of the contaminated
  horizon, `mesophilic` peat, and the seven descriptors that decide
  positions of the horizon key (uncoated grains, the extent of the
  effervescence, the frost regime, plant residues, the smell of hydrogen
  sulfide, the size of the slickensides, cryoturbation). The descriptive
  ones (skeletans, the place and layering of the clay films, the mineral
  admixture, carbonate pendants, an erosion mark) are not added: the
  notation or the evidence carries them.

## soilKey 0.9.334 (2026-11-02)

### Russia: the engine for profile formulas

The Russian soil classification (Field Guide of 2008) names its types by
profile formulas (“O-EL-BEL-BT-C”) and its subtypes by a list of
features per division. This release adds the generic pieces it needs; no
system uses them yet, so every classification is unchanged. The Russian
notation, horizons, divisions and types follow.

- **Profile formulas.** An internal parser reads a formula into slots:
  alternative codes (“RY(RJ)”, “CG (CQ~~)”, and soilKey’s ”O\|T\|H”),
  optional horizons in parentheses, features (typical, or required where
  they name the type, as Rca), the role of each slot (surface, middle,
  parent), buried profiles (\[ABC\], {ABC}), turbated compositions
  (TUR\[AU+SEL+ASN\]), small horizons (\[e-hf\], e), rock flags (CG, CQ,
  DG) and rock marks (C~~, C”, C, C”“, C=, C..). Given a vocabulary of
  horizons and features, an unknown token stops it with its name.
- **[`match_horizon_sequence()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/match_horizon_sequence.md)**
  matches the identified horizons of a profile against a formula: TRUE,
  FALSE or NA when an undecided layer could change the answer, with the
  slots matched, the slots missing, the extra horizons and the edit
  distance. A horizon fills a slot by its code or by an overlay (an AU
  with an S overlay fills an S slot); surface and agro codes the formula
  does not name stay out of the closure unless `closure_surface = TRUE`,
  so a natural remnant under the plough does not block an agro type.
  Internal helpers run a division’s schemes, pick the most specific
  match (the others noted as intergrades) and, when none matches, rank
  the nearest schemes by edit distance.
- **[`identify_horizons()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/identify_horizons.md)**
  gives the reading of every layer as a diagnostic horizon (code,
  overlays, features, small and transitional rows, buried profiles,
  route, verdict, evidence, the candidates when undecided), by the
  system’s own identification; a system without one stops with an error,
  as every system does in this release.
- **A walker of horizon keys** (internal): a key written as a tree of
  questions answered TRUE, FALSE or NA.
- **An additive level** (internal): after the type, every listed feature
  that passes is named, in list order. The Hungarian subtype properties
  keep their own code.
- [`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html) of a result lists the
  classes of one level together (“CA01 Podzolic \> g gleyic, y
  tongued”), so the Hungarian subtype and variety properties are no
  longer chained with “\>” as if each were below the one before.

#### Hugo’s decisions (2026-11-02)
