## soilKey 0.9.245 (2026-10-13)

### SiBCS key: the vertic horizon by the features of the book, read also from the text of the description

Of the 72 profiles of the national BDsolos export with a reference in
Vertissolos, 10 keyed there in the default mode. The book (SiBCS 2018,
Cap. 2, p. 73) knows the vertic horizon by “superfícies de fricção
(slickensides) em quantidade no mínimo comum, e/ou unidades estruturais
cuneiformes e/ou paralelepipédicas”, asks of it “uma espessura mínima de
20 cm”, and gives it “precedência diagnóstica sobre os horizontes B
incipiente, B nítico e glei”. `horizonte_vertico()` was the WRB horizon
with other limits: slickensides only, and 20 cm of one layer. And the
surveys older than the structured field sheet wrote the slickensides and
the structure in the text of the horizon, which the loader did not read.

- **The loader reads the text of the horizon description.** The column
  “Descrição Original” of the export is read for two things, where the
  structured columns are empty, and is not kept. The amount of
  slickensides is the one written beside the term (“‘’slickenside’’
  comum e moderado”, “abundantes superfícies de fricção”); a mention
  with no amount fills nothing, as decided on 2026-10-13, and neither
  does an amount that belongs to another feature (“cerosidade forte e
  abundante apresentando slickensides”) or a comparison (“mais
  abundantes que o horizonte superior”). A wedge-shaped or
  parallelepipedic structure is added to the structure of the horizon; a
  structure “com tendência a paralelepipédica” is not one. The terms are
  read in the spellings the export has (“slikenside”, “silkensides”,
  “paralelepédica”). The reader was checked against every phrase of the
  export that holds the terms: 127 different ones for the slickensides,
  36 for the structure. It reads an amount in 212 layers and the
  structure in 41.
- **The vertic horizon.** A layer with 300 g/kg of clay or more is
  vertic by slickensides in amount of common or more, or by wedge-shaped
  or parallelepipedic structural units, with cracks of 1 cm where their
  width is recorded; the 20 cm are those of adjoining layers.
- **Its precedence.**
  [`B_incipiente()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_incipiente.md)
  left out the layers of the WRB vertic horizon; it leaves out those of
  this one.
- **The Vertissolos step** (Cap. 4, p. 112) asks what its first words
  ask, a “relação textural insuficiente para identificar um B textural”:
  a profile whose B textural is identified by the textural ratio of
  item (h) is no Vertissolo. One identified by its cerosidade alone,
  with a ratio known to be below the limit, is not kept out. Where the
  ratio cannot be computed, the B textural keeps the profile out.
- **Item (a) of the step**, “Teor de argila, após mistura e
  homogeneização do material de solo, nos 20 cm superficiais, de no
  mínimo 300 g kg-1”, is the clay of each layer weighted by what it has
  within the upper 20 cm. The plain mean of the layers that begin at 20
  cm or above was tested.

#### Measured

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order:

|                    | 0.9.244       | 0.9.245       |
|--------------------|---------------|---------------|
| default mode       | 3,938 (51.9%) | 3,969 (52.3%) |
| morphological mode | 4,828 (63.6%) | 4,854 (63.9%) |

Default mode: 38 profiles change order, 32 reach their reference, 1
leaves it and 5 go from one wrong order to another. Reference
Vertissolos agreed 10 to 41 of 72; profiles keyed Vertissolos 16 (10 of
that reference) to 50 (41). Of the 35 that become Vertissolos, all by
what the text says: 23 by the amount of slickensides alone, 6 by the
structure alone, 6 by both.

The one that leaves its reference is a Gleissolo Háplico vertissólico
with “slickensides moderado e comum” from 60 cm (SE 6459): the step
takes a vertic horizon that begins within 100 cm, and Vertissolos key
before Gleissolos.

Morphological mode: 31 change, 27 to their reference and 1 from it, a
Bruno Não Cálcico with common slickensides from 12 cm and a textural
ratio of 1.32 (BA 8520). Reference Vertissolos agreed 19 to 45.

Panel of complete profiles (781): 419 to 429 and 506 to 512. FEBR
(1,000): 376 and 501, confusion matrices identical. Redape (94): 77 and
84, no profile changes. The 44 canonical profiles keep their class in
the three systems, in both modes.

#### Not changed, and measured

Item (c) of the Neossolos step, “Ausência de horizonte vértico
imediatamente abaixo de horizonte A”, is tested as a vertic horizon that
begins within 50 cm. By the letter, with the first vertic layer right
below an A, 14 profiles change order in the default mode: 10 reference
Vertissolos with a C or an AC between the A and the first vertic layer
go to Neossolos, and no profile reaches its reference.

## soilKey 0.9.244 (2026-10-13)

### SiBCS key: the mudança textural abrupta and the B plânico as the book states them

[`mudanca_textural_abrupta()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/mudanca_textural_abrupta.md)
was the WRB abrupt textural difference under another name: every pair of
adjoining layers was compared, in the order of the rows, and no distance
was asked. A jump of clay between two B horizons, or from a B to a C,
was an abrupt change, and
[`B_planico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_planico.md)
took any layer with such a jump for the B plânico.

The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 1, p. 30-31): the mudança textural abrupta is
“um considerável aumento no teor de argila em pequena distância na zona
de transição entre o horizonte A ou E e o horizonte subjacente B”, twice
the clay when the A or E has less than 200 g/kg and 200 g/kg more
otherwise, “em uma distância vertical ≤ 7,5 cm”. And the B plânico (Cap.
2, p. 65) is “um tipo especial de horizonte B textural \[…\] subjacente
a horizontes A ou E, apresentando mudança textural abrupta ou transição
abrupta associada à relação textural com valor dentro do especificado
para o horizonte B textural (subitem h), porém calculado entre o
primeiro sub-horizonte B e o horizonte imediatamente acima (A ou E)”.

- **Mudança textural abrupta.** The first B horizon is compared with the
  horizon immediately above it, which has to be an A or an E. The
  distance is read from the distinctness of the transition, which the
  BDsolos loader brings since 0.9.241: abrupt or clear is within 7.5 cm,
  gradual or diffuse is not; where it is not recorded the two horizons
  are compared. The subgroups that ask for the attribute (“abrúpticos”)
  read it the same way.
- **B plânico.** It is looked for in the first B sub-horizon, by one of
  the two ways of the book: the mudança textural abrupta, or a
  transition recorded as abrupt with the clay of that sub-horizon over
  the clay of the horizon above beyond the limit of item (h) (1.50, 1.70
  or 1.80). The second way was not tested.
- **Its texture.** As a type of B textural, that sub-horizon has a
  texture francoarenosa or finer (p. 54). The WRB property asked 15% of
  clay of the lower layer; the attribute of the book asks none, and
  without the texture the sandy Bh of 9 reference Espodossolos, 2 to 7%
  of clay below an E with 0 to 3%, was a B plânico in the default mode.
- **Where the colour and the structure are asked.** In that first
  sub-horizon, as decided on 2026-10-13. Measured before the texture was
  asked: of any B sub-horizon, 216 profiles keyed Planossolos with 122
  of that reference; of the first, 178 with 109.
- Item (g) of the B textural reads the transition by the same function.

The first B sub-horizon is the first horizon whose designation begins
with B, a BA or the B1 of the old notation included, as in item (h),
which leaves out of the B only the BC. The other reading, with those as
the horizon above, was measured: the B plânico changes in 20 profiles, 6
reference Planossolos lose it and 1 gains it.

A profile with no horizon designation at all is tested as before. The
WRB
[`abrupt_textural_difference()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/abrupt_textural_difference.md)
is not changed.

#### Measured

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order:

|                    | 0.9.243       | 0.9.244       |
|--------------------|---------------|---------------|
| default mode       | 3,929 (51.7%) | 3,938 (51.9%) |
| morphological mode | 4,817 (63.4%) | 4,828 (63.6%) |

Default mode: 50 profiles change order, 24 reach their reference, 15
leave it and 11 go from one wrong order to another. Reference
Planossolos agreed 98 to 109 of 291; profiles keyed Planossolos 153 (98
of that reference) to 169 (109).

The 15 that leave their reference:

- 7 reference Planossolos. In 4 the jump of clay is inside the B, below
  its first sub-horizon; in 2 the transition where the jump is was
  recorded as gradual; in 1 the first B sub-horizon has no colour
  recorded.
- 6 reference Luvissolos and 2 reference Argissolos, now with a B
  plânico. In 4 by the second way (abrupt transition and the ratio of
  item h); in 3 the B begins at 6 to 8 cm, and the WRB property asked
  the lower layer to begin at 10 cm or below; in 1 the B has 7% of clay
  and 32% of silt. All have the colours and the structure of the
  definition.

The fourth level changes in 157 profiles that keep their first three, by
the attribute of the “abrúpticos”.

Morphological mode: 41 change, 24 to their reference and 13 from it.
Panel of complete profiles (781): 416 to 419 and 502 to 506. FEBR
(1,000): 376 and 501, confusion matrices identical. Redape (94): 77 and
84, no profile changes. The 44 canonical profiles keep their class in
the three systems, in both modes.

## soilKey 0.9.243 (2026-10-13)

### SiBCS key: the B latossólico is asked for its Ki

The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 59, item e) asks of the B latossólico a
“Relação molecular SiO2/Al2O3 (Ki) igual ou inferior a 2,2, sendo
normalmente menor que 2,0”, and tells the B incipiente from it by a Ki
“maior que 2,2” (p. 61). The item was not tested. The profile schema has
the silica and the alumina of the sulfuric attack, from which
[`compute_ki()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/compute_ki.md)
gives the index, but the BDsolos loader did not read them, although the
export records them in 71% of its rows.

- [`load_bdsolos_csv()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/load_bdsolos_csv.md)
  reads “Ataque sulfúrico - SiO2” and “- Al2O3” into `sio2_sulfuric_pct`
  and `al2o3_sulfuric_pct`, converted from g/kg to %. The index computed
  from them reproduces the Ki column of the export (99.1% of the rows of
  one state within 0.05).
- In
  [`B_latossolico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_latossolico.md)
  a layer whose Ki is recorded above 2.20 is no B latossólico. The
  horizon is what is left: the adjoining sub-horizons that meet every
  requirement still have to make 50 cm. Where the sulfuric attack is not
  recorded the horizon is tested as before.

The limit is read as written and by sub-horizon, as decided on
2026-10-13 after the alternatives were measured (the limit at one
decimal, so that 2.24 counts as 2.2, cost 16 profiles where this costs
23).

#### Measured

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order:

|                    | 0.9.242       | 0.9.243       |
|--------------------|---------------|---------------|
| default mode       | 3,952 (52.0%) | 3,929 (51.7%) |
| morphological mode | 4,844 (63.8%) | 4,817 (63.4%) |

**The agreement goes down, and it is the book that takes it down.** In
the default mode 83 profiles lose their B latossólico: 34 reference
Latossolos (1,041 agreed before, 1,007 now), of which 16 have every B
sub-horizon above 2.2 and 18 have one that breaks the 50 cm; 11
reference Cambissolos reach their order (394 to 405); the other 38 go
from one wrong order to another (29 of them reference Argissolos that
were keyed Latossolos). Of the profiles keyed Latossolos, 70.6% had that
reference before (1,041 of 1,474) and 72.4% now (1,007 of 1,391).

Panel of complete profiles (781): 418 to 416 in the default mode and 504
to 502 in the morphological mode. FEBR (1,000: 376 and 501, confusion
matrices identical) and Redape (94: 77 and 84, no profile changes) do
not change. The 44 canonical profiles keep their class in the three
systems, in both modes.

## soilKey 0.9.242 (2026-10-13)

### BDsolos: the loader reads the kind of sampling point, and the benchmark reports by it

The export marks each record, in its column “Tipo”, as “Perfil
completo”, “Perfil parcial” or “Amostra extra”. The loader did not read
the column. Of the 7,593 records of the national export with a reference
order, 4,674 are complete profiles, 332 partial profiles and 2,587 extra
samples. An extra sample is, in most cases, two sampled layers of a
point (a topsoil and a subsoil sample, often with a gap between them):
the thickness recorded is that of the samples, and a horizon that is
asked for 50 cm cannot be shown by it. One figure for the three mixed
what the key does on a described profile with what it can do on two
samples.

- [`load_bdsolos_csv()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/load_bdsolos_csv.md)
  puts the column in `site$sampling_type`, as written (the double space
  of “Perfil parcial” made one).
- [`benchmark_bdsolos()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/benchmark_bdsolos.md)
  gains `sampling_type = "Perfil completo"`: the figures of each system
  (`accuracy`, `n_compared`, `n_correct`, `confusion`, `per_class`) are
  those of the complete profiles, and the new `by_sampling_type` gives
  the counts of every kind and of all the records together.
  `sampling_type = NULL` counts every record, as the function did.
  Pedons that carry no `site$sampling_type` (another source, a hand-made
  list, a file with no “Tipo” column) are all counted, as before.
- The BDsolos row of
  [`run_all_benchmarks()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/run_all_benchmarks.md)
  and of
  [`benchmark_unified()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/benchmark_unified.md)
  is drawn from complete profiles: extra samples and partial profiles
  are left out before the cap.

The key is not changed. On the national export, at this version:

| Kind of point   | n     | default mode  | morphological mode |
|-----------------|-------|---------------|--------------------|
| Perfil completo | 4,674 | 2,850 (61.0%) | 3,228 (69.1%)      |
| Perfil parcial  | 332   | 111 (33.4%)   | 233 (70.2%)        |
| Amostra extra   | 2,587 | 991 (38.3%)   | 1,383 (53.5%)      |
| all             | 7,593 | 3,952 (52.0%) | 4,844 (63.8%)      |

**The panel of the EJSS article is another sample now.** It was a draw
of 800 of the 984 labelled records of the first three files (Acre,
Alagoas, Amazonas), extra samples included. It is a draw of 800 of the
1,111 labelled complete profiles of the first five (Acre, Alagoas,
Amazonas, Amapá, Bahia): 418 of 781 in the default mode and 504 of 781
in the morphological mode (19 of the 800 carry a label that names no
order). At 0.9.241 the old panel gave 361 and 495 of 798. The two are
different samples and their figures are not to be compared as a gain of
the key.

FEBR, Redape and the 44 canonical profiles are not touched.

## soilKey 0.9.241 (2026-10-13)

### SiBCS key: the B textural and the B latossólico are tested by the items of the book

Three things in the two horizons that separate most of the profiles of
Brazil were not the book’s (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 54-59), and one in
the Neossolos step followed from them.

- [`B_textural()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_textural.md)
  was the WRB argic horizon: a layer with 6 percentage points of clay, a
  ratio of 1.4 or 20 points more than the least clayey layer anywhere
  above it. Item (h) of the book, the relação textural, had been joined
  to it; items (f), (g) and (i) were not tested.
- [`B_latossolico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_latossolico.md)
  asked its 50 cm of each layer on its own: a B latossólico described as
  B1, B21 and B22 of 35 cm each was none.
- Since 0.9.61 a B textural did not exclude the B latossólico unless its
  clay films were common or more, on a rule the comments attributed to
  Cap. 18 of the book, which deals with families and series. The book
  (p. 59): the B latossólico “não apresenta características diagnósticas
  de horizontes glei, B textural, B nítico e plíntico”. The first defect
  hid this one: with the thickness alone corrected, 168 reference
  Argissolos of the national BDsolos export became Latossolos.
- `neossolo()` set a diagnostic B aside when the profile had caráter
  flúvico (0.9.10), because the clay increase of the argic horizon fired
  between the stratified C layers of the canonical Fluvisol.

#### The B textural

A profile with horizon designations is tested by the items of p. 55-56:
a B horizon (BC excluded) of texture francoarenosa or finer and 7.5 cm
or more, with one or more of

- **(f)** an E horizon above it, the B having more clay and being no B
  espódico, plíntico or plânico;
- **(g)** a mudança textural abrupta from the A or E to the B (Cap. 1,
  p. 30-31): twice the clay when the A or E has less than 200 g/kg, 200
  g/kg more otherwise, “em uma distância vertical ≤ 7,5 cm”. The
  distance is read from the distinctness of the transition, which the
  BDsolos loader now brings (`boundary_distinctness`: “Abrupta” and
  “Clara” are within 7.5 cm, “Gradual” and “Difusa” are not); where it
  is not recorded the two layers are compared;
- **(h)** the relação textural above 1.50, 1.70 or 1.80 according to the
  clay of the A. Footnote 4 asks for the “média aritmética do teor de
  argila total do horizonte B (excluído o BC)”; the means were weighted
  by the thickness. The designations are read with their material number
  and the old “(B)”;
- **(i)** where the increase is below item (h), the cerosidade of a
  sub-horizon of the upper part of the B (read as its upper half):
  texture média with no macroaggregates and cerosidade of moderate
  grade; texture média with prismatic or blocky structure of moderate or
  strong grade and cerosidade of at least moderate grade; texture
  argilosa or muito argilosa with that structure and cerosidade at least
  common and weak or few and moderate; or a relação textural of 1.4 with
  a fragipã;
- **(j)** across a discontinuity of parent material, or with only a
  ploughed layer above the B, items (h) or (i) are needed.

A profile with no horizon designation at all (depth slices) cannot be
read by these items and is tested as before, by the clay increase
between layers. In the morphological mode a “t” in the designation of a
B horizon stands for the B textural the data do not show, now with a
material number in front too (“IIBt”).

#### The B latossólico

Texture francoarenosa or finer, less than 17 cmolc per kg of clay,
cerosidade at most few and weak (item h, layer by layer; a range counts
by its upper end), in B horizons where the designations are recorded,
and 50 cm of the horizon: of the adjoining sub-horizons that meet those
requirements, taken together
(`test_minimum_thickness(adjoining = TRUE)`). The layers of a B textural
are no B latossólico. A plinthic or gleyic horizon or a B nítico in the
profile exclude it as before.

The Latossolos step asks that no B textural lie above the B latossólico:
“o primeiro horizonte diagnóstico de subsuperfície, a contar da
superfície, tem prevalência” (Cap. 4, p. 110), so that a thick BC of
low-activity clay below a B textural makes no Latossolo.

[`B_incipiente()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_incipiente.md)
excludes the layers of this B textural and of this B latossólico (item
a, p. 60); it excluded those of the WRB argic and ferralic horizons (30
cm, 16 cmolc). `carater_latossolico()` looks for the B latossólico below
the sub-horizons that carry the evidence of the B textural. `neossolo()`
no longer sets a diagnostic B aside: the B textural is looked for in B
horizons, and the canonical Fluvisol has none.

[`argic_with_strong_clay_films()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/argic_with_strong_clay_films.md)
and
[`audit_argic_strong_films()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/audit_argic_strong_films.md)
are kept as tools; the key no longer uses their rule.

The SiBCS B textural no longer goes through
[`argic()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/argic.md),
so that `options(soilKey.diagnostic_engine = "aqp")` does not change it,
nor does the inference from “Bt” with clay films that the engine bundled
(in the RJ file the reference Argissolos agreed were 181 with that
engine and are 168 with either now). The engine still gives the B
latossólico its limit of 20 cmolc and its fallbacks; a “t” the data do
not show is read by the morphological mode.

#### Measured

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order:

|                                    | 0.9.240       | 0.9.241       |
|------------------------------------|---------------|---------------|
| default mode                       | 3,783 (49.8%) | 3,952 (52.0%) |
| morphological mode                 | 4,452 (58.6%) | 4,844 (63.8%) |
| complete profiles (4,674), default | 56.7%         | 61.0%         |
| complete profiles, morphological   | 62.7%         | 69.1%         |
| extra samples (2,587), default     | 39.3%         | 38.3%         |
| extra samples, morphological       | 50.1%         | 53.5%         |

Default mode: 1,780 profiles change order, 677 reach their reference,
508 leave it. By reference order: Latossolos 899 to 1,041 agreed,
Neossolos 690 to 856, Cambissolos 342 to 394, Argissolos 1,256 to 1,086,
Luvissolos 125 to 101. Of the profiles keyed Argissolos, 58% had that
reference before and 71% now; of those keyed Latossolos, 62% and 71%.

**What it costs.** In the default mode 385 reference Argissolos leave
their order and 215 enter it. Those that leave have a relação textural
below item (h) and no cerosidade recorded: the data do not show the B
textural the surveyor saw; 181 of them carry the old name Podzólico.
They are concentrated in the Amazon: in Amazonas 184 of 254 reference
Argissolos agreed before and 94 now, in Pará 165 and 115. The panel of
the EJSS article is the first 800 profiles of the export, which are
those of Acre, Alagoas and Amazonas, and it goes down: 387 to 361 in the
default mode and 507 to 495 in the morphological mode. FEBR (1,000): 387
to 376 and 498 to 501.

Redape (94 profiles of the correlation meetings, with cerosidade and
structure recorded): 69 to 77 in the default mode and 74 to 84 in the
morphological mode. The 44 canonical profiles keep their class in the
three systems, in both modes.

#### Not tested, and why

Items (a) structure, (c) rock structure, (e) Ki and (f) weatherable
minerals of the B latossólico: the profile schema has no Ki, although
the BDsolos export records it in 71% of its rows. Lamellae (item d of
the B textural). A B argiloso with cerosidade common or more and a
structure of weak grade is covered by no condition of item (i): it is no
B textural, and by item (h) of the B latossólico it is none either.

## soilKey 0.9.240 (2026-10-13)

### SiBCS key: the “(B)” of the old horizon notation is read as the B incipiente it names

Until 1988 the B incipiente was written “(B)” in Brazil: “A (B) C”, “A1
(B)1 (B)2 C”, “A II(B)21 II(B)22”. Larach et al. (1988, “Definição e
notação de horizontes e camadas do solo”, the reference of SiBCS 2018
for the notation) replaced it by “Bi”, which the book uses (“O horizonte
B incipiente (Bi)”, Cap. 3).
[`B_incipiente()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_incipiente.md)
takes its candidate layers from the designation, and `.desg_master()`,
which every SiBCS test of the master horizon reads, left “(B)” as
written: for the key it was not a B horizon. In the national BDsolos
export 552 layers of 333 profiles carry it, and 293 of them are among
the 640 profiles whose reference order is Cambissolos. With no
diagnostic B found, they were keyed Neossolos.

`.desg_master()` now reads “(B)”, “(B)21”, “(B1)” and “II(B)22” as “Bi”,
“Bi21”, “Bi1” and “Bi22”. The horizon data keep the designation as
written, and a parenthesis that does not open the designation (“A3/(B)”,
“B(2)”) is left alone. Nothing else of the B incipiente changes: the
layer still has to be 10 cm thick and not to be a B textural,
latossólico, espódico or plânico, so that a “(B)” that the data show to
be a B latossólico is one. The reader serves the SiBCS key only; WRB and
USDA read the designation by patterns of their own and are not touched.

#### Measured

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order:

|                    | before        | after         |
|--------------------|---------------|---------------|
| default mode       | 3,579 (47.1%) | 3,783 (49.8%) |
| morphological mode | 4,249 (56.0%) | 4,452 (58.6%) |

In the default mode 234 profiles change order: 212 reach their
reference, 8 leave it and 14 go from one wrong order to another.
Cambissolos: 134 of 640 agreed before, 342 after. The 8 that leave their
reference are profiles labelled Neossolos (six of them by the old names
Solo Litólico and Solo Aluvial) with a “(B)” of 10 cm or more, which by
the book is a B incipiente: “Admitem um horizonte B em início de
formação, cuja espessura não satisfaz a nenhum tipo de horizonte B
diagnóstico” (Neossolos Litólicos, Cap. 12).

Panel of the EJSS article (798 profiles): 367 to 387 in the default mode
and 489 to 507 in the morphological mode; only the row of the reference
Cambissolos moves (15 to 35 agreed in the default mode). FEBR (1,000)
keeps its confusion matrices (387 and 498 agreed) and no profile of
Redape (94) changes (69 and 74). The 44 canonical profiles keep their
class in the three systems, in both modes.

#### Found on the way, not changed here

- The export has a column “Tipo” that the loader does not read: of the
  7,593 profiles with a reference order, 4,674 are “Perfil completo”,
  332 “Perfil parcial” and 2,587 “Amostra extra”, in most cases two
  sampled layers, often with a gap between them. The order agreement of
  the three groups is 54.7%, 34.9% and 35.1% in the default mode.
- The minimum thickness of a diagnostic horizon is asked of each
  sub-horizon on its own: a Latossolo described as B1, B21 and B22 of 35
  cm each has no B latossólico of 50 cm for the key.
- [`B_textural()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_textural.md)
  is the WRB argic horizon with its thresholds, joined to item
  8.  of the book; items (f), (g) and (i) are not tested, and the B
      latossólico does not exclude the B textural.

## soilKey 0.9.239 (2026-10-12)

### SiBCS key: the glei horizon is read by the colours of the book, with the drainage class as the record of its saturation

`horizonte_glei()` was the WRB test of gleyic properties under another
name: redoximorphic features of 5% or more in a layer that starts within
50 cm, with no colour asked. A mottled Argissolo was a Gleissolo, and a
grey Cg with no amount of mottles recorded was not. In the national
BDsolos export the key called 468 profiles Gleissolos, of which 123 had
that reference, and 141 reference Gleissolos were keyed Neossolos.

The book (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 2, p. 70-71): “o horizonte glei é um
horizonte mineral, com espessura mínima de 15 cm, com menos de 15% de
plintita e é saturado com água por influência do lençol freático durante
algum período ou o ano todo \[…\], apresentando evidências de processos
de redução, com ou sem segregação de ferro, caracterizadas por um ou
mais dos seguintes requisitos”: (a) the dominant colour, by four items;
(b) “Coloração variegada com pelo menos uma das cores de acordo com um
dos itens anteriores”; (c) reduced iron shown by a field test.

- **Colours.** A layer qualifies by item (a1), neutral or bluer than
  10Y; (a2), hues redder than 5YR with value 4 or more and chroma 1 or
  less; (a3), hues 5YR or yellower with value 4 or more and chroma 2 or
  less, or 3 in a hue 10YR or yellower when the chroma decreases in the
  horizon below; (a4), any hue and value with chroma 2 or less and
  mottles; or (b), a variegated layer (`variegated_colors`) with one
  colour of those items. Organic layers and layers with 15% of plinthite
  or more do not qualify. Item (c) is recorded by no profile.
- **Saturation.** It is not measured. What a survey records of it is the
  drainage class of the site, and Anexo B (p. 315) describes the
  classes: in a “mal drenado” soil “o lençol freático comumente está à
  superfície ou próximo dela durante uma considerável parte do ano”,
  while an “imperfeitamente drenado” one shows “indícios de gleização
  nos seus horizontes mais profundos”. The colours make a glei horizon
  when the site is “mal drenado” or “muito mal drenado”. A class written
  as a range counts by its wetter end (“imperfeitamente a mal drenado”
  is “mal drenado”), an exception to the rule that a range is read by
  its lower end. The field is read as `site$drainage` (the BDsolos
  loader) or `site$drainage_class`.
- **No drainage class recorded.** The layer itself has to show the
  saturation, beside its colours: mottles (“O horizonte sendo saturado
  com água periodicamente ou o solo tendo sido drenado deve apresentar
  algum mosqueado”, p. 70), a colour of item (a1), or a variegated
  colour. Without that, the greyish A and the pale E of any soil satisfy
  item (a3).
- **Morphological mode.** The “g” of a designation (Cg, Btg) stands for
  the colours and for the saturation, as before.
- **Gleissolos** (key, Cap. 4, p. 112-113): the glei horizon within 50
  cm, or between 50 and 150 cm “desde que imediatamente subjacente a
  horizontes A ou E ou a horizonte hístico com menos de 40 cm de
  espessura”. Any glei horizon within 150 cm used to count.
- **Neossolos** (p. 111): “Ausência de horizonte glei dentro de 50 cm a
  partir da superfície, exceto no caso de solos de textura areia e areia
  franca”. 150 cm was tested, with no exception.

The new internals are `.glei_colour_item()`, `.glei_colour_layers()`,
`.drainage_class()` and `.textura_areia_ou_areia_franca()`. The WRB
test,
[`gleyic_properties()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/gleyic_properties.md),
is not changed.

#### Effect

## soilKey 0.9.238 (2026-10-12)

### SiBCS key: the B plânico is tested for its structure and for the colours of a variegated or mottled horizon

SiBCS 2018 (Cap. 2, p. 65-66) describes the B plânico by more than the
key tested. It “Apresenta estrutura prismática, colunar ou em blocos
angulares e subangulares grandes ou médios e, às vezes, estrutura
maciça”, and its colours “devem atender a pelo menos um dos seguintes
requisitos”: (a) the matrix colour; (b) “Coloração variegada com pelo
menos uma cor apresentando matiz e croma conforme especificado no item
(a)”; (c) “matiz 10YR ou mais amarelo, cromas ≥ 4, combinado com
mosqueado de croma conforme especificado no item (a)”.
[`B_planico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_planico.md)
tested an abrupt textural change and item (a). A B horizon with small
subangular blocks was a B plânico, and a variegated one, which has no
matrix colour, was none.

- **Structure.** Where the sheet records it, the structure has to be one
  of those the definition describes: prismatic, columnar or massive; or
  blocks, angular or subangular, that are medium or larger. A size
  written as a range is read by its lower end (“Pequena a média” is
  small), as the other minima are. A structure that is not recorded
  passes, and so do blocks with no size. The new internal
  `.structure_size_class()` reads the size in both languages.
- **Item (b)** reads `variegated_colors`, and **item (c)**
  `mottle_colors`: a matrix of hue 10YR or yellower and chroma 4 or
  more, with a mottle whose colour satisfies item (a).

Of the reference Planossolos of the national BDsolos export that have a
B plânico and a recorded structure, 84 of 90 have one of the list; the
six that do not are in small blocks.

#### Effect

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order:

|                                     |        Default |  Morphological |
|-------------------------------------|---------------:|---------------:|
| Order agreement                     | 3,349 to 3,355 | 3,959 to 3,967 |
| Reference Planossolos agreed (291)  |       91 to 98 |       89 to 96 |
| Profiles keyed Planossolos          |     153 to 153 |     141 to 141 |
| Reference Argissolos agreed (2,016) | 1,182 to 1,184 | 1,331 to 1,334 |
| Reference Luvissolos agreed (197)   |     112 to 109 |     124 to 121 |

In the default mode 66 profiles change order: 22 now agree with their
reference, 16 no longer do, 28 go from one disagreeing order to another.
The same number of profiles is keyed Planossolos, and more of them are
(59% to 64%): the structure takes out B horizons in small blocks, most
of them reference Argissolos with an abrupt change, and items (b) and
(c) bring in Planossolos whose B is variegated. Measured apart, items
(b) and (c) alone gave 13 gains and 13 losses, and the structure alone 9
gains and 6 losses.

Other benchmarks:

- Redape (94 profiles): 69 to 70 in the default mode and 73 to 74 in the
  morphological mode. `GeoTab_PE_041_Pombos`, a reference Planossolos
  with a variegated “2Btn”, is now keyed Planossolos.
- BDsolos panel of the EJSS article (798 scored): 351 to 350 in the
  default mode and 459 to 458 in the morphological mode.
- FEBR (1,000 profiles): 387 and 496, unchanged.
- The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems, in
  both modes.

The precedence of the plinthic horizon is as it was: a B plânico that
coincides with a plinthic horizon, without the sodic character, is no B
plânico of a Planossolo (key, Cap. 4, p. 112; Cap. 2, p. 68).

## soilKey 0.9.237 (2026-10-12)

### Redape and SmartSolos: the structure codes are read on the scales the service documents

The GeoTab files of Redape, and the SmartSolos Expert service they were
made for, record the soil structure as integer codes. The service
describes them
(`https://www.agroapi.cnptia.embrapa.br/store/api-docs/agroapi/SmartSolosExpert/v1`):

| Field | Description |
|----|----|
| `ESTRUTURA_GRAU` | “de ausente (1) a forte (4)” |
| `ESTRUTURA_TAMANHO` | “de muito pequeno (1) a extremamente grande (6)” |
| `ESTRUTURA_TIPO` | “laminar (1), prismática (2), colunar (3), blocos angulares (4), blocos subangulares (5), granular (6), grumosa (7)” |

Since 0.9.189 the Redape loader read the grade on a scale of three
(“weak” for 1) and the type in another order (“granular” for 1,
“columnar” for 5). Of the 444 horizons of the 94 profiles: the 137 with
subangular blocks were read as columnar, the 79 with angular blocks as
prismatic, the 63 granular ones as platy; the 211 of weak grade were
read as moderate, the 73 moderate ones as strong, and the 24 strong ones
had no grade at all. The encoders that send a profile to the service
([`classify_via_smartsolos_api()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_via_smartsolos_api.md),
since 0.9.54) made the same two mistakes the other way round.

- [`load_redape_pedons()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/load_redape_pedons.md)
  decodes the three fields on the documented scales. A grade of 1 is
  “structureless”, a size of 6 “extremely coarse”, a type of 7 “crumb”.
- The payload sent to the service encodes them on the same scales, so
  that what the loader decodes the encoder sends back as the same code.
- A structure recorded as absent is now a grade below weak. It was read
  as not recorded, which passes a minimum such as the “grau moderado ou
  forte” of the B nítico. No profile of Redape or BDsolos records one.

The documented scales were checked against the data: 35 horizons of 7
Redape profiles are also in the BDsolos export, which keeps the words of
the field sheet. Code 5 is “Blocos subangulares” there in 18 of 18
horizons, 6 is “Granular” in 6 of 6, 2 is “Prismática” in the one case;
grade 2 is “Fraca” in 20 of 22 and grade 3 “Moderada” in 6 of 7.

`CEROSIDADE_GRAU` is described the same way, “de ausente (1) a forte
(4)”, and is left on the scale of three it was read with (1 weak, 2
moderate, 3 strong). The files hold 1, 2 and 3 only, and 1 comes with an
amount of clay films in 12 of 13 horizons, which “ausente” would not; no
shared profile records clay films to settle it. It is an open question
for the authors of the files.

#### Effect

- Redape (94 profiles): 68 to 69 in the default mode and 72 to 73 in the
  morphological mode. The profile is
  `GeoTab_PE_045_Cabo_de_Santo_Agostinho`, a reference Nitossolos whose
  B horizons are in subangular blocks of moderate grade (codes 5 and 3).
  Read as columnar, they failed the structure of the B nítico, and the
  profile was keyed Latossolos, or Argissolos in the morphological mode.
  The Redape figures reported from 0.9.189 to 0.9.235 were computed with
  the structure read the old way.
- The national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles), its panel of the EJSS
  article and FEBR do not change, in either mode: they do not go through
  these codes. The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three
  systems.
- The service itself was not called to verify the encoders; they follow
  its published description.

## soilKey 0.9.236 (2026-10-12)

### HTML report: the evidence-grade badge has its colour again

The report colours the evidence grade of each classification with a
class of its own (`grade grade-a` to `grade grade-d`), given by an
internal `.grade_class()`. 0.9.231 added an internal function of the
same name, to read the grade of a soil structure (“Fraca”, “moderate”),
in a file that is loaded later. It replaced the report’s function, and
from 0.9.231 to 0.9.235 every badge was written with `class="NA"`: the
letter was there, without its colour. The report was otherwise
unaffected, and no classification changed.

- The reader of field grades is now `.field_grade_class()`; the report
  has its `.grade_class()` back.
- A new test parses the package sources and fails when a name is defined
  twice. Files are loaded in alphabetical order, and a second definition
  replaces the first without a word; this was the only such name among
  1,343.

## soilKey 0.9.235 (2026-10-12)

### SiBCS key: the variegated colours and the colours of the mottles are read in the depth rule of Plintossolos

A plinthic horizon that starts below 40 cm makes a Plintossolo when it
lies immediately below a horizon “que apresente cores pálidas,
variegadas ou com mosqueados em quantidade abundante” (SiBCS 2018, Cap.
3, p. 104). Since 0.9.234 the key tested the pale colour and the amount
of the mottles. It could not test the rest, because a profile held one
colour per horizon: a variegated horizon, which has no single matrix
colour, reached the key with no colour at all, and the mottles counted
by their amount whatever their colour.

- **Two new columns of the profile**, `variegated_colors` and
  `mottle_colors`: the Munsell notations the field sheet lists,
  separated by “;” (`"10YR 5/3; 2.5YR 4/6"`). They are in
  [`horizon_column_spec()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/horizon_column_spec.md),
  in the JSON schema of the profile and in `inst/ATTRIBUTES.md`, and are
  read only when present.
- **BDsolos loader.** The export has “Variegado - Matiz / Valor / Croma”
  and “Mosqueado - Matiz / Valor / Croma”, each cell listing one entry
  per colour separated by “:” (“10YR:5YR”, “6:5”, “3:6”). They are
  joined into the notations. In the national export, 975 horizons of 654
  profiles are variegated (947 of them have no matrix colour) and 2,649
  horizons of 1,395 profiles have the colours of their mottles.
- **Redape loader.** GeoTab gives up to three more colours in
  `COR_MOSQ_*`. Beside a matrix colour they are read as the colours of
  the mottles (15 horizons); in a horizon with no matrix colour, as its
  variegated colours (7 horizons of 4 profiles).
- **The rule**, in the internal `.plinthic_preceded()`, with the two
  items the three kinds of colour answer to (“a) Matiz 5Y; ou b) Matizes
  7,5YR, 10YR ou 2,5Y com croma menor ou igual a 4”) in the new internal
  `.plintossolo_items_a_b()`:
  - variegated: “pelo menos uma das cores deve satisfazer aos itens (a)
    e (b)”. Hue and chroma only, as the book writes; the moist value of
    5 or more that 0.9.234 asks of a pale matrix colour is not asked
    here. No profile of BDsolos or Redape differs between the two
    readings.
  - mottles: “deverão ocorrer em quantidade abundante (\> 20% em volume)
    numa matriz de coloração avermelhada ou amarelada e deverão
    apresentar matizes e cromas conforme os itens (a) e (b)”. The amount
    is asked as before; the colour, of at least one of the mottles, when
    the sheet records it. A horizon with abundant mottles and no colour
    recorded passes as before. The colour of the matrix is not tested:
    the book gives no hue for “avermelhada ou amarelada”.

#### Effect

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems, in the
default and in the morphological mode. Reloaded with the new loader,
each of the 7,714 profiles of the national BDsolos export is identical
to the one of 0.9.234 in every column that existed.

National BDsolos export, 7,593 profiles with a reference order. In the
default mode no profile changes (3,349; the export records no volume of
plinthite). In the morphological mode:

|                                     | 0.9.234 | 0.9.235 |
|-------------------------------------|--------:|--------:|
| Order agreement (count)             |   3,957 |   3,959 |
| Reference Plintossolos agreed (331) |     118 |     121 |
| Profiles keyed Plintossolos         |     176 |     180 |
| Reference Argissolos agreed (2,016) |   1,332 |   1,331 |

Six profiles change order, and no other changes its second level or its
name:

- three reference Plintossolos now agree, each with a variegated horizon
  above its plinthic one: AM 10006 and AM 12796 (“Btg” 2.5Y 7/1 and 10YR
  6/8 above “Btfg” at 100 cm) and PE 5860 (“2Bt” 10YR 5/3 and 2.5YR 4/6
  above “2Btf” at 93 cm);
- two reference Argissolos are now keyed Plintossolos, for the same
  reason: AM 10788 (“B21” 10YR 7/3 and 7.5YR 5/8 above “B22pl” at 70 cm)
  and BA 8469 (“B21t” 5YR 4/6 and 10YR 6/4 above “B22tpl” at 120 cm).
  Both labels are old “Podzólico Vermelho-Amarelo … plíntico”, a class
  the book places in part among the Plintossolos (Abrangência, p. 104);
- one reference Argissolos is no longer keyed Plintossolos: PA 9609,
  whose “B2t” (7.5YR 5/8) has abundant mottles of colour 5YR 6/8, which
  satisfies neither item.

Other benchmarks:

- Redape (94 profiles): 67 to 68 in the default mode and 71 to 72 in the
  morphological mode. The profile is `GeoTab_PE_048_Goiana` (the PE 5860
  of BDsolos), the limit 0.9.234 left: its “2Bt” is variegated and one
  of its colours is 10YR with chroma 3. The Redape recall of
  Plintossolos pinned in `test-v09107-sibcs-accuracy.R` is 3 of 3 again.
- BDsolos panel of the EJSS article (798 scored): 351 in the default
  mode, unchanged; 458 to 459 in the morphological mode (the three
  profiles of Amazonas above). The article’s own figures are of
  v0.9.189.
- FEBR (1,000 profiles): 387 and 496, unchanged; its loader does not
  bring these colours.

Not changed: a horizon with abundant mottles also makes a horizonte glei
in some profiles (`redoximorphic_features_pct` is what the gleyic test
reads), and a glei horizon above the plinthic one satisfies the rule by
itself, whatever the colour of the mottles. The other tests that read a
colour (B plânico, horizonte glei, the colour suborders) still see no
colour in a variegated horizon.

## soilKey 0.9.234 (2026-10-12)

### SiBCS key: the morphological mode reads “v” and “pl”, and a Plintossolo needs its plinthic horizon where the book says

The morphological mode
(`options(soilKey.morphological_inference = TRUE)`) lets a horizon
designation stand for a diagnostic the data cannot test. Two letters of
the Brazilian notation were not read by it, and reading one of them
brought out a rule that was looser than the book.

- **“v”, vertic features** (Bv, Cv, Biv).
  [`vertic_horizon()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/vertic_horizon.md)
  reads the suffix only under an option of its own, because it also
  serves WRB and USDA, where “v” is plinthite (KST, FAO).
  `horizonte_vertico()`, the SiBCS wrapper, now turns that reading on in
  the morphological mode. For WRB and USDA nothing changes.
- **“pl”, plinthite in the older surveys** (B21pl, Cpl), where “f” is
  written today. `horizonte_plintico()` reads it in the morphological
  mode, with the thickness it asks of “f”. Of the 331 profiles of the
  national BDsolos export whose reference order is Plintossolos, 80
  carry “pl” and 64 carry “f”.
- **Where the plinthic horizon starts.** `plintossolo()` accepted a
  plinthic, litoplinthic or concretionary horizon that started anywhere
  within 200 cm. The definition (SiBCS 2018, Cap. 3, p. 104; key, Cap.
  4, p. 113) accepts it within 40 cm, or within 200 cm only “quando
  precedidos de horizonte glei ou situados imediatamente abaixo do
  horizonte A ou E ou de outro horizonte que apresente cores pálidas,
  variegadas ou com mosqueados em quantidade abundante”. The new
  internal `.plinthic_preceded()` tests that: a glei horizon above; or,
  in the horizon immediately above, an A or an E, mottles in abundant
  amount (more than 20%), or a pale colour. For the pale colour the book
  gives the hue and the chroma (5Y; or 7.5YR, 10YR or 2.5Y with chroma 4
  or less) and no number for the lightness; a moist value of 5 or more
  is taken, so that a brown 10YR 4/4 is not pale. Variegated colours are
  not recorded and not tested.
- **Cambissolos.** `cambissolo()` excluded a profile with any plinthic
  horizon, at any depth. The book excludes the ones that meet “os
  requisitos estabelecidos para serem enquadrados” as Plintossolos (Cap.
  3, p. 88); the test now asks `plintossolo()`.
- **The canonical Plintossolo.**
  [`make_plintossolo_canonical()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/make_plintossolo_canonical.md)
  reuses the WRB fixture, whose plinthic horizons are written “Btv” and
  “Cv”. In the Brazilian notation that “v” is vertic, and the Brazilian
  “f” is frozen soil for KST and FAO. The profile is classified by the
  three keys (it is one of the demonstration profiles of the app), so
  its horizons are now “A”, “Bt”, “C”, with the plinthite it has
  measured. Its class does not change in any of the three systems.

In the default mode, no profile of the national BDsolos export changes
order (the export records no volume of plinthite). The 44 canonical
fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

In the morphological mode, on the national BDsolos export (7,593
profiles with a reference order):

|                                     | 0.9.233 | 0.9.234 |
|-------------------------------------|--------:|--------:|
| Order agreement (count)             |   3,855 |   3,957 |
| Order agreement                     |   50.8% |   52.1% |
| Reference Plintossolos agreed (331) |      60 |     118 |
| Profiles keyed Plintossolos         |     155 |     176 |
| … of which reference Plintossolos   |     39% |     67% |
| Reference Vertissolos agreed (72)   |      10 |      20 |
| Reference Argissolos agreed (2,016) |   1,298 |   1,332 |

185 profiles change order: 125 now agree with their reference, 23 no
longer do, 37 go from one disagreeing order to another. Reading “pl”
under the old depth rule would have gained 67 Plintossolos and lost 57
Argissolos, whose plinthite lies deep in a B textural (“B21 B22pl”); the
rule of the book keeps 58 of those Plintossolos and returns the
Argissolos. The three losses of the “v” are intergrades (“Chernossolo …
vertissólico”, “Gleissolo … vertissólico”).

Other benchmarks:

- BDsolos panel of the EJSS article (798 scored): 351 in the default
  mode, unchanged; 412 to 458 in the morphological mode (51.6% to
  57.4%). Amazonas, one of its three states, holds most of the “Laterita
  Hidromórfica” profiles written with “pl”. The article’s own figures
  are of v0.9.189.
- FEBR (1,000 profiles): 387 and 496, unchanged.
- Redape (94 profiles): 67 and 71, the same totals, with two profiles
  that change in both modes because its loader brings plinthite: a
  reference Plintossolos whose “2Btf” starts at 93 cm under a “2Bt” no
  longer agrees, and a reference Argissolos with “Btf” deep under “Bt2”
  now does. The first is a limit of what a profile carries, not of the
  rule: the sheet records that “2Bt” as variegated (10YR 5/3 and 2.5YR
  4/6), which the book accepts (“pelo menos uma das cores deve
  satisfazer aos itens (a) e (b)”), and a profile holds one colour per
  horizon. In the national BDsolos export a variegated colour is
  recorded just above the first plinthic designation in 11 profiles.

Two canonical fixtures written in the notation of KST change SiBCS order
in the morphological mode, which reads the Brazilian notation: the
Cryosol, whose “f” (frozen) was read as plinthite at depth, is no longer
keyed Plintossolos; the WRB Plinthosol, with its “Btv”, is keyed
Vertissolos.

## soilKey 0.9.233 (2026-10-12)

### SiBCS key: the colour of the B plânico is the one the book lists

SiBCS 2018 (Cap. 2, p. 65-66) asks of a B plânico a matrix colour of
“Matiz 10YR ou mais amarelo, cromas ≤ 3” or of “Matizes 7,5YR ou 5YR,
cromas ≤ 2”.
[`B_planico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_planico.md)
tested the first with the pattern `10YR|2\.5Y|5Y`, which “5YR”, “7.5YR”
and “2.5YR” also match, because all three contain “5Y”. A B horizon of
hue 5YR or 7.5YR passed with chroma 3, and one of hue 2.5YR passed at
all.

- The hue is now read as a number and a family by the new internal
  `.munsell_hue_parts()` (“7.5YR” and “7,5YR” are 7.5 and “YR”). 10YR
  and the Y hues pass with chroma 3 or less; from 5YR up to, not
  including, 10YR, with chroma 2 or less; a redder hue does not pass.
- Neutral and gley hues (N, GY, G, B) are not among the requirements the
  book lists and do not pass, as before.

The alternatives (b) and (c) of the book, a variegated colour and a
matrix of chroma 4 or more with mottles of low chroma, need the colours
of the mottles, which the profiles do not carry; they are not tested, as
before.

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order),
nineteen profiles change order in the default mode: seven now agree with
their reference, six no longer do and six go from one disagreeing order
to another. Order agreement 3,348 to 3,349; reference Planossolos agreed
95 to 91, Chernossolos 26 to 29, Argissolos 1,180 to 1,182. In the
morphological mode, 3,854 to 3,855.

The other benchmarks do not change: the BDsolos panel of the EJSS
article (351 and 412 of 798), FEBR (387 and 496 of 1,000) and Redape (67
and 71 of 94).

## soilKey 0.9.232 (2026-10-12)

### BDsolos loader: slickensides, gravel in per cent, hues with a dot

Three things the BDsolos export records and the profiles did not carry
as the diagnostics read them.

- **Slickensides.** “Superfície de fricção - Quantidade” (filled in 53
  profiles of the national export) was not loaded, so the vertic horizon
  had no slickensides to test: the key agreed with none of the 72
  profiles whose reference order is Vertissolos. The column now goes to
  `slickensides`, as the sheet words it (“Pouca”, “Comum”, “Abundante”).
- **Reading the amount.** `test_slickensides_present()` and the crack
  test that stands on it compared the amount with the literal English
  terms. They now read it through the new internal `.amount_at_least()`,
  in English or Portuguese, a range by its lower end: SiBCS asks for
  slickensides “em quantidade no mínimo comum” (Cap. 2, p. 73). Amounts
  in English are read as before.
- **Gravel.** “Frações da amostra total - Cascalho (g/kg)” went into
  `coarse_fragments_pct` as it came, so that 560 g/kg read as 560 %:
  2,677 horizons of 1,285 profiles had more than “100 %”. It is now
  divided by 10, as the clay, silt and sand of the same export already
  were.
- **Hue.** The export types the Munsell hue with a decimal comma
  (“7,5YR”, “2,5YR”) in 7,492 horizons of 3,430 profiles, and the
  patterns of the diagnostics are written with a dot.
  [`load_bdsolos_csv()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/load_bdsolos_csv.md)
  now gives “7.5YR”, as the FEBR loader already did.

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order),
default mode:

|                                   | 0.9.231 | 0.9.232 |
|-----------------------------------|--------:|--------:|
| Order agreement (count)           |   3,340 |   3,348 |
| Order agreement                   |   44.0% |   44.1% |
| Reference Vertissolos agreed (72) |       0 |      10 |

Sixteen profiles change order, all to Vertissolos and all through the
slickensides: ten agree with their reference, two no longer do (a
reference Gleissolos and a reference Luvissolos with slickensides
“comum” or more) and four go from one disagreeing order to another. The
gravel and the hue change no order.

The hue changes the second level of 1,079 profiles whose order stays the
same. With a hue it could not read, the key left the colour suborder at
“Vermelho-Amarelos”; it now follows the hue (Argissolos
Vermelho-Amarelos to Amarelos in 287 profiles and to Vermelhos in 232,
Latossolos Vermelho-Amarelos to Vermelhos in 201 and to Amarelos in 178,
Luvissolos Háplicos to Crômicos in 71). Against the reference labels
that carry a present-day order name (5,461), the second level agrees in
1,088 profiles where it agreed in 1,059: 211 profiles gained and 182
lost. Latossolos keyed in the right order have the right suborder in 362
profiles (305 before), Argissolos in 190 (241 before):
“Vermelho-Amarelo” is the most frequent suborder of the reference
Argissolos, and the default coincided with it.

The other benchmarks do not change at the order level: the BDsolos panel
of the EJSS article (351 and 412 of 798), FEBR (387 and 496 of 1,000)
and Redape (67 and 71 of 94).

## soilKey 0.9.231 (2026-10-12)

### SiBCS key: in the B nítico, a grade written as a range is read by its lower end

SiBCS 2018 states the criteria of the B nítico as minima: structure “de
grau de desenvolvimento moderado ou forte”, cerosidade “em quantidade no
mínimo comum e com grau forte ou moderado” (Cap. 2, p. 61-62). A range
meets a minimum only if all of it does. The amount of cerosidade has
been read that way since 0.9.227 (“Pouca a comum” is below “comum”); the
two grades were read with the pattern `moder|strong|forte`, which “Fraca
a moderada” matches.

- The new internal `.grade_class()` reads a grade of development on the
  scale weak / fraca, moderate / moderada, strong / forte, in English or
  Portuguese, and a range by its lower end.
  [`B_nitico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_nitico.md)
  uses it for the grade of the structure and for the grade of the
  cerosidade. “Moderada a forte” passes; “Fraca a moderada” and “weak to
  moderate” do not. A grade that was not recorded does not fail the
  layer, as before.

The other kind of criterion is a maximum, and there a range counts by
its upper end: the B latossólico admits “no máximo cerosidade pouca e
fraca” (p. 58-59), so “Pouca a comum” exceeds it. The clay-film gate of
the B latossólico already reads it so and is not changed.

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order),
default mode, seven profiles change order: two reference Nitossolos are
no longer reached (PR 6654, SC 11902), two reference Argissolos are no
longer keyed Nitossolos and agree (MT 6184, MT 10801), one reference
Argissolos goes from Argissolos to Neossolos (MG 5916), and two go from
one disagreeing order to another. Order agreement 3,341 to 3,340;
reference Nitossolos agreed 80 to 78, Argissolos 1,179 to 1,180.

The other benchmarks do not change: the BDsolos panel of the EJSS
article (351 and 412 of 798), FEBR (387 and 496 of 1,000) and Redape (67
and 71 of 94).

## soilKey 0.9.230 (2026-10-12)

### SiBCS key: the clay-film gate of the B latossólico reads “many”

A B latossólico gives way to a B textural when the layers with the clay
increase have cerosidade “comum” or “abundante” (SiBCS Cap. 18, in
[`B_latossolico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_latossolico.md)
since 0.9.61). The gate, `.argic_strong_films_match()`, read “comum”,
“abundante”, “common” and “abundant”, but not “many”: the term the
English field sheets (KST, FAO) use for the class above “common”, and
the one the Redape loader writes for its code of “abundante”. A profile
whose films were “many” kept its B latossólico and keyed out as
Latossolos.

- `.argic_strong_films_match()` now reads “many” as a strong amount, as
  a word (“very many” too, “germany” not).

The 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems.

On Redape (94 profiles), four profiles of Rio Grande do Norte whose
reference is Argissolos and whose clay films are “many” go from
Latossolos to Argissolos:

|               |    0.9.229 |    0.9.230 |
|---------------|-----------:|-----------:|
| Default mode  | 63 (67.0%) | 67 (71.3%) |
| Morphological | 67 (71.3%) | 71 (75.5%) |

No profile is lost. The other benchmarks do not change: the national
BDsolos export (its amounts are in Portuguese; the same order for each
of the 7,694 labelled profiles), the BDsolos panel of the EJSS article
(351 and 412 of 798) and FEBR (387 and 496 of 1,000; its loader records
no cerosidade). The article’s own figures are of v0.9.189.

## soilKey 0.9.229 (2026-10-11)

### SiBCS benchmarks: a label is read by what it states, when that places it in another order

The label map read every “Podzólico” as Argissolos and every
“Cambissolo” as Cambissolos. Anexo I of SiBCS 2018 (p. 342) is finer,
and three kinds of label state attributes that the book places in
another order than their name. The new internal
[`.sibcs_stated_order()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/dot-sibcs_stated_order.md)
reads them, after the order of the name.

- **Podzólico Vermelho-Amarelo or Vermelho-Escuro that states Eutrófico
  and high-activity clay** (“Ta”, “argila de atividade alta”) is
  Luvissolos: Anexo I lists the “Podzólicos Vermelho-Amarelos Eutróficos
  Ta” and the “Podzólicos Vermelho-Escuros Eutróficos Ta” under
  Luvissolos. 31 labels of the national BDsolos export. The “Podzólicos
  Amarelos” are Argissolos in Anexo I without condition and stay so.
- **A label that begins with “Argissolo” and states Eutrófico and
  high-activity clay** is read as Luvissolos. Such a label contradicts
  itself: an Argissolo has a B textural “de argila de atividade baixa,
  ou atividade alta desde que conjugada com saturação por bases baixa ou
  com caráter alumínico” (p. 87), and a B textural with high-activity
  clay and high base saturation is a Luvissolo (p. 95). The 36 labels of
  this kind, 19 of them from Acre (“ARGISSOLO VERMELHO-AMARELO Eutrófico
  argila de atividade alta A moderado textura argilosa.”), read as the
  old Podzólico names with the first word replaced. The attributes
  stated are taken, not the word.
- **Cambissolo in the old form that states Eutrófico, high-activity clay
  and A chernozêmico** is Chernossolos: the exception of Anexo I
  (“exceto os Cambissolos Eutróficos com horizonte A chernozêmico e com
  argila de atividade alta”). 11 labels. A label whose second word is a
  present suborder (“CAMBISSOLO HÁPLICO Eutrófico Ta A chernozêmico”, 2
  labels) was written in SiBCS and is left as it is.

“Eutrófico” is the word itself: “Epieutrófico” and the like do not
count. A label that states both “Ta” and “Tb” keeps the order of its
name.

Left as they were, on purpose:

- the 52 “Podzólico … Eutrófico” or “Equivalente Eutrófico” labels that
  do not state the clay activity: the book places them in Luvissolos if
  Ta and in Argissolos if Tb, and the label does not say;
- the “plíntico” labels under Podzólico (93), Latossolo (32) and Glei
  (4): the book sends “parte” or “alguns” of them to Plintossolos;
- the Podzólicos Vermelho-Escuros Tb (51), “alguns” of which the book
  sends to Nitossolos.

The key does not change; only the reference order of 78 labels does. On
the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order),
default mode:

|                                 |       0.9.228 |       0.9.229 |
|---------------------------------|--------------:|--------------:|
| Order agreement (count)         |         3,299 |         3,341 |
| Order agreement                 |         43.4% |         44.0% |
| Reference Luvissolos (agreed)   |      130 (67) |     197 (113) |
| Reference Chernossolos (agreed) |      116 (23) |      127 (26) |
| Reference Argissolos (agreed)   | 2,083 (1,186) | 2,016 (1,179) |
| Reference Cambissolos (agreed)  |     651 (124) |     640 (124) |

49 of the 78 profiles now agree with their reference. 7 no longer do:
they are among the 36 “Argissolo” labels, and the key returns Argissolos
for them. None of the 42 Podzólico and Cambissolo profiles agreed
before.

Other benchmarks:

- BDsolos panel of the EJSS article (798 scored): 339 to 351 in the
  default mode (42.5% to 44.0%), 400 to 412 in the morphological mode
  (50.1% to 51.6%). Acre is one of its three states. The article’s own
  figures are of v0.9.189 and do not change.
- FEBR: its 1,442 labels are an order and a suborder, none states the
  clay activity, and all are read exactly as before.
- Redape does not go through this function.

At `level = "subordem"` the stated order is followed by the next word of
the label, as for the old names: it is not a suborder of SiBCS 5 in
general.

## soilKey 0.9.228 (2026-10-11)

### SiBCS key: a horizon is read without the number of its material

A horizon below a lithologic discontinuity is written with the number of
its material in front: “2Bt1” today, “IIBt1” in the surveys that
numbered the materials in Roman numerals. The SiBCS diagnostics chose
their horizons with patterns such as `^B` and `^A`, which neither form
matches, so a “IIBt” was not a B horizon for them. In the national
BDsolos export 1,984 horizons of 874 profiles carry such a number, 670
of them B horizons. The clearest loss was in Planossolos, whose B
plânico is very often the top of a second material (“A1 A3 IIBt IIC”):
the abrupt textural change passed in 186 of the 291 profiles with that
reference order and the B plânico in 56.

- The new internal `.desg_master()` gives a designation without the
  number of the material, Arabic or Roman (“2Bt1” and “IIBt1” are
  “Bt1”). The 56 designation patterns of the SiBCS diagnostics, in 39
  functions of the order, suborder, attribute and family levels, now
  read it. All of them ask whether a horizon is a B, an A, a C, an R or
  an O, or a B with some suffix; none looks for the number. The horizon
  data keep the designation as written.
- Three of those functions already accepted an Arabic number
  (`^[0-9]*A`) but not a Roman one.

The canonical fixtures have no numbered horizon and classify as before.
Their SiBCS order no longer depends on the number: with the subsoil of
each fixture written as a second material (“II” or “2” in front of its
horizons), 18 of the 44 changed order before this version (the canonical
Planossolo became Gleissolos, the Luvissolo Argissolos) and none does
now.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order),
default mode:

|                                     | 0.9.227 | 0.9.228 |
|-------------------------------------|--------:|--------:|
| Order agreement (count)             |   3,245 |   3,299 |
| Order agreement                     |   42.7% |   43.4% |
| Reference Planossolos agreed (291)  |      56 |      95 |
| Reference Luvissolos agreed (130)   |      52 |      67 |
| Reference Cambissolos agreed (651)  |     119 |     124 |
| Reference Nitossolos agreed (347)   |      78 |      80 |
| Reference Chernossolos agreed (116) |      22 |      23 |
| Reference Argissolos agreed (2,083) |   1,194 |   1,186 |

163 profiles change order, all of them with a numbered horizon (859 of
the labelled profiles have one): 62 now agree with their reference, 8 no
longer do and 93 go from one disagreeing order to another. Most of the
93 go from Argissolos to Luvissolos (95 profiles in all, 15 of them
gains): in 88 of those the profile has no B horizon without a number, so
the tests of clay activity and base saturation found no B horizon,
answered no, and the profile fell to Argissolos, the end of the key for
a B textural. They now read the IIBt.

Other benchmarks, before and after:

- BDsolos panel of the EJSS article (798 scored): 335 to 339 in the
  default mode (42.0% to 42.5%), 396 to 400 in the morphological mode
  (49.6% to 50.1%). The article’s own figures are of v0.9.189 and do not
  change.
- FEBR (1,000 profiles): 387 and 496, unchanged.
- Redape (94 profiles): 61 to 63 in the default mode, 65 to 67 in the

Not changed here: the tests shared with WRB and USDA (`^Bw|^Bo|^Boi`,
`^[BE]` and the like in `utils-diagnostic-tests.R` and
`designation-inference.R`), whose benchmarks, KSSL above all, are full
of “2Bt”; and `.desg_material_number()`, which reads the number of the
material for the WRB tests and reads Arabic numbers only.

## soilKey 0.9.227 (2026-10-11)

### SiBCS key: the B nítico test reads cerosidade and structure in the language of the field sheet

SiBCS 2018 (Cap. 2, p. 61-62) asks of a B nítico “cerosidade em
quantidade no mínimo comum e com grau forte ou moderado” and “estrutura
em blocos ou prismática”.
[`B_nitico()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/B_nitico.md)
compared `clay_films_amount` with the literal English terms
`c("common", "many", "abundant", "strong")`. The BDsolos export words
the amount as the Brazilian field sheets do (“Comum” in 1,218 horizons,
“Pouca” in 874, “Abundante” in 523), so the criterion passed in none of
its profiles: of the 7,694 labelled profiles of the national export,
[`classify_sibcs()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_sibcs.md)
returned Nitossolos for none, although 145 of the 347 whose reference
order is Nitossolos record cerosidade “comum” or more and “moderada” or
more.

- The amount is now read on the ordinal scale of `.clay_films_class()`
  (none, few / pouca, common / comum, many or abundant / abundante), the
  reader the WRB nitic horizon already used, in English or Portuguese
  and whatever the case. `min_cerosidade` keeps its default; its lowest
  term sets the threshold, and a term the scale does not know passes
  only if it is listed, as before.
- A range of amounts is read by its lower end: “Pouca a comum” is below
  “comum”, “Comum a abundante” meets it.
- The type of structure is matched without depending on accents:
  “Prismática” and “Prismática que se desfaz” (789 horizons of the
  export) did not match the pattern `prismatic|prismatica`. The new
  internal `.field_term()` gives a field term in lower case and without
  accents.

Profiles described with the English terms are read exactly as before:
the 44 canonical fixtures keep their class in the three systems, and
their SiBCS order is now the same when their terms are written in
Portuguese.

On the national BDsolos export (7,593 profiles with a reference order),
default mode:

|                                     | 0.9.226 | 0.9.227 |
|-------------------------------------|--------:|--------:|
| Order agreement (count)             |   3,182 |   3,245 |
| Order agreement                     |   41.9% |   42.7% |
| Reference Nitossolos agreed (347)   |       0 |      78 |
| Reference Argissolos agreed (2,083) |   1,209 |   1,194 |

130 profiles change order: 83 now agree with their reference, 20 no
longer do and 27 go from one disagreeing order to another. The key
returns Nitossolos for 121 profiles: 78 with that reference, 39 whose
reference is Argissolos and 4 of other orders. The 39 have at least 350
g/kg of clay from the surface, a B/A clay ratio of 1.5 or less and
cerosidade “comum” or more: by the data they meet the B nítico of the
book. 16 of them carry the old name “Podzólico”, which the label map
reads as Argissolos; the book’s Anexo I says some Podzólicos
Vermelho-Escuros Tb and Vermelho-Amarelos Tb went to Nitossolos.

The other 269 reference Nitossolos are still not reached: 160 record no
cerosidade at all, 42 record it below the threshold, and the rest fail
another criterion in their own data (most often a B/A ratio above 1.5).

Other benchmarks, before and after:

  with a reference order): 326 to 335 in the default mode (40.9% to
  42.0%), 388 to 396 in the morphological mode (48.6% to 49.6%). The
  article’s own figures are of v0.9.189 and do not change.
- FEBR (1,000 profiles): 387 and 496, unchanged. Its loader records no
  cerosidade.
- Redape (94 profiles): 61 and 65, unchanged. Its loader already
  translates the codes of the amount into the English terms.

Not changed here: the grade of cerosidade and of structure is still read

## soilKey 0.9.226 (2026-10-11)

### SiBCS benchmarks: the old soil names of the reference labels are read as their present-day order

0.9.225 left out of the scored profiles every reference label whose
first word is not an order of SiBCS 5. Most of those labels are names of
the classifications in use before SiBCS: 876 of the 7,694 labels of the
national BDsolos export, counting the 252 that begin with “Solo” or
“Solos”. The 5th edition (Santos et al., 2018) says where each old class
went, in the “Abrangência” paragraph of each order (chapter 3, p. 87 to
106) and in its Anexo I (p. 342).
[`normalise_febr_sibcs()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/normalise_febr_sibcs.md)
now follows it.

- **Names the book gives to one order** are in
  `.SIBCS_LEGACY_ORDER_MAP`: Latosol (Latossolos), Planosol and
  Solonetz-Solodizado (Planossolos), Brunizem and Rendzina
  (Chernossolos), Regossolo, Litosol and Solos Litólicos (Neossolos),
  Solos Orgânicos (Organossolos), Vertisol (Vertissolos), Cambisol
  (Cambissolos), Solos Concrecionários and Concrecionários Lateríticos
  (Plintossolos), Rubrozem (Argissolos), with the misspellings of these
  and of the present orders found in the export (“PLITOSSOLO”,
  “NEO0SSOLO”, “POZDÓLICO”, “ARE1A QUARTZOSA”). 628 labels.
- **Names that take two words** are in the new
  `.SIBCS_LEGACY_TWO_WORD_MAP`: Bruno Não Cálcico (Luvissolos), Humic
  Glei and Low-Humic Glei (Gleissolos), Solos Indiscriminados
  Concrecionários (Plintossolos), and Terra Roxa and Terra Bruna
  Estruturada (Nitossolos). For the last two the book says “na maioria”
  (p. 98), with a “pequena parte” in Argissolos (p. 87); the name does
  not say which, and the 147 labels are read as the majority.
- **“Solo” or “Solos” in front is not the name**: the word after it is
  (“SOLO LITÓLICO” is Neossolos, “SOLOS ORGÂNICOS” Organossolos). A
  “Solos …” label followed by no name of the maps is `NA`, as before.
- **A hyphen separates the words of a name** as a space does
  (“LATOSSOLO-VERMELHO”, “SOLONETZ-SOLODIZADO”).

These readings are tried only when the first word gives no order, so a
label that was read before is read the same.

Left out on purpose, and still `NA` (101 labels):

- names the book divides between orders by something the name does not
  say: Hidromórfico Cinzento (Gleissolos without an abrupt textural
  change, Planossolos with one), Solonchak (Gleissolos only with a glei
  horizon), Alissolo;
- names that are not in its correlation: Laterítico Bruno Avermelhado
  (which is not Laterita Hidromórfica), Solos Brunos Ácidos, Solos
  Coluviais, Mediterrâneo Vermelho-Amarelo;
- labels that begin with a Soil Taxonomy name (“Typic Haplorthox ou
  Latossolo …”), “aterro”, and the labels the database itself marks as
  doubtful (“\*MUDAR\*”, “\*CORRIGIR\*”).

On the national BDsolos export (7,714 profiles, 7,694 with a label),
default mode of
[`classify_sibcs()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/classify_sibcs.md):

|                         | 0.9.225 | 0.9.226 |
|-------------------------|--------:|--------:|
| Scored profiles         |   6,818 |   7,593 |
| Order agreement (count) |   2,873 |   3,182 |
| Order agreement         |   42.1% |   41.9% |

775 labels are now scored and the key agrees with 309 of them. The
agreement goes down by 0.2 point because of the Terra Roxa and Terra
Bruna profiles: the key places none of the 147 in Nitossolos (without
them the figure would be 42.7%). That is not particular to the old
names. In this run the key returns Nitossolos for none of the 7,694
profiles, and agrees with none of the 306 labelled Plintossolos or the
61 labelled Vertissolos. The reference follows the book; the cause on
the key’s side has not been looked into here.

FEBR is not affected: its 1,442 labels are all present-day orders and
are read exactly as before.

On the BDsolos panel of the EJSS article (800 profiles of AC, AL and
AM), run at this version, the scored profiles go from 785 to 798 (the
two left out are the “Classificação ?” and “Alissolo” labels).
Agreement: 320 of 785 to 326 of 798 in the default mode (40.8% to
40.9%), 382 of 785 to 388 of 798 in the morphological mode (48.7% to
48.6%). The article’s own figures are of v0.9.189 and do not change.

At `level = "subordem"` an old name gives its order followed by the next
word of the label, as the names already in the map did. That word is not
a suborder of SiBCS 5 in general: the old names are for comparisons at

## soilKey 0.9.225 (2026-10-11)

### SiBCS benchmarks: a reference label counts only if it is a SiBCS order

[`normalise_febr_sibcs()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/normalise_febr_sibcs.md)
reads a reference label by its first word, and that word came out
whatever it was. “CLASSIFICAÇÃO ? CAMBISSOLO HÁPLICO …” was the class
“Classificacaos”, “Alissolo Crômico” was “Alissolos”, “LATOSOL AMARELO”
was “Latosois” and “ESPODOSSOLO.” was “Espodossolo.s”. No prediction can
equal those, yet the benchmarks counted them as scored profiles and as
errors: 631 of the 7,694 labels of the national BDsolos export, in 79
forms.

- The result must now be one of the 13 orders of SiBCS 5 (the new
  internal `.SIBCS_ORDERS`) after the legacy map. Anything else is `NA`,
  so the profile is left out of the scored ones, as a label of the
  “Solos …” kind already was.
- Punctuation around the first word is dropped first, so “ESPODOSSOLO.”,
  “Vertissolo.” and “PLANOSSOLO(???)” are read as their orders.

On the national BDsolos export (7,714 profiles, 7,694 with a label):

|                         | 0.9.224 | 0.9.225 |
|-------------------------|--------:|--------:|
| Scored profiles         |   7,442 |   6,818 |
| Order agreement (count) |   2,871 |   2,873 |
| Order agreement         |   38.6% |   42.1% |

624 labels stop being scored and 7 are now read as an order. The
agreement rises because the 624 were errors by construction; the key did
not change. Most of them are names of older editions that have a
present-day order and no entry in `.SIBCS_LEGACY_ORDER_MAP` yet: “Terra
Roxa …” and other “Terra” names (147), “Latosol” (139), “Planosol” (54),
“Brunizem” (43), “Bruno Não Cálcico” (40). They are left out here, not
mapped: which order each one belongs to is a pedological decision for
the map.

FEBR is not affected: its 1,442 labels are all orders already.

On the BDsolos panel of the EJSS article (800 profiles of AC, AL and
AM), run at this version, the scored profiles go from 787 to 785: the
“Classificação ?” and “Alissolo” labels are left out, and “ESPODOSSOLO.”
is read as Espodossolos (a hit in the morphological mode: 381 to 382 of
them agree). The article’s own numbers are those of v0.9.189 and do not
change.

## soilKey 0.9.224 (2026-10-10)

### Pro app: every instance serves the scripts a drawn widget brings

The Map tab could come up as a grey box, without base map or overlay,
when Cloud Run had a second instance up. A map with provider tiles
brings two scripts when it is drawn, the provider list and leaflet’s
plugin for it. They are not in the page, so the start-up registration of
0.9.215 left them out. Shiny registered them only in the R process that
drew a map, and a request routed to another instance got HTTP 404. Seen
on 2026-10-10 in the request logs of the live 0.9.222 and of a 0.9.223
test revision, with two sessions open at once: page and websocket on one
instance, the two 404s on another.

A local run through every tab, with each resource path logged, found the
same for two other widgets: DT’s DataTables core and plotly’s plotly.js
bundle are registered when the first table or plot is drawn. No 404 was
seen for those.

- `sk_register_widget_deps()`, called at start-up after the page is
  rendered, registers what a table, a plot and a map with provider tiles
  bring: 34 prefixes at start-up in the local run, against 28. Only
  prefixes that are not registered yet are added, so nothing of the page
  is re-pointed, and a widget’s own jQuery is left out.
- Maps and map proxies get their provider tiles through
  `sk_provider_tiles()`.
- A provider list in the temporary folder is never served from there.
  Shiny serves the folder a dependency is in, whole, and leaflet has a
  fallback that writes the provider list to the R session’s temporary
  folder; `sk_own_dependency()` moves such a dependency to a folder that
  holds only its files. The container image does not take that fallback:
  there the list comes from the installed leaflet.providers package
  folder, so no temporary folder was served by the live app. (This note
  first said it was; a check inside the 0.9.224 image showed otherwise.)

Checked in a fresh local process, before any session: the two provider
scripts answered 404 and now answer 200. In a session through every tab
no prefix is re-pointed, and the only new one is the jQuery of plotly’s
crosstalk, which the browser does not ask for (the page’s jQuery is
there). The base map loads and changes with the selector.

Checked on the container image: a fresh instance of 0.9.223 answered 404
for the five draw-time scripts before any session (the two provider
scripts, the DataTables core, plotly.js and typedarray), and one of
0.9.224 answers 200. Four sessions at once, over three instances, drew
every map, table and plot without a failed request.

## soilKey 0.9.223 (2026-10-10)

### The AfSP row of the benchmark suite

[`run_all_benchmarks()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/run_all_benchmarks.md)
has a row for the AfSP sample (WRB, Africa), and it was never there.
[`load_afsp_sample()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/load_afsp_sample.md)
returns a list that holds the 120 profiles in `$pedons`, beside the
date, source and filter of the snapshot. The suite cut that whole list
to `max_n` and handed it to
[`benchmark_afsp()`](https://hugomachadorodrigues.github.io/soilKey/reference/benchmark_afsp.md),
